artigo.texto: South Korea's Samsung, Hyundai Motor Join Forces on Solid-State Battery Mass-Production Processes, Filing 9 Joint Patents Battery cooperation between Samsung and Hyundai Motor Group is moving beyond supply contracts into joint design and next-generation technology development. After jointly filing patents that simultaneously raise the safety and energy density of electric-vehicle battery packs, the two sides have entered a phase in which they are jointly securing not just materials research but mass-production process technology for next-generation solid-state batteries. According to the Korea Intellectual Property Rights Information Service (KIPRIS), a patent titled "Battery Pack and Vehicle Including the Same," jointly filed by Hyundai Motor, Kia and Samsung SDI, was published on the 22nd of last month. Its core is a gas vent at the bottom of the battery cells and a separate channel at the lower part of the battery pack. The structure vents high-temperature gas generated in a thermal-runaway situation to the outside while merging the previously separate gas-venting space and impact-protection space into one to raise energy density. The patent was designed around Samsung SDI's flagship prismatic battery. Five Hyundai Motor and Kia researchers and two Samsung SDI researchers are named as inventors. The key point is that the two companies' cooperation has expanded beyond simple cell supply to joint design of battery packs tailored to vehicles. Samsung SDI signed its first EV battery supply contract with Hyundai Motor in 2023. Under the terms, Samsung SDI will supply prismatic batteries made at its Hungarian plant for Hyundai Motor and Kia's Europe-bound EVs for seven years from this year through 2032. The number of models actually using them is also growing. Starting with Kia's EV2, the number of vehicles using Samsung SDI batteries has expanded to three models, including Hyundai's Ioniq 3 and Genesis's top-tier electric SUV, the GV90. The move is seen as a result of Hyundai Motor and Kia — which have mainly used pouch-type cells — rating the prismatic battery's energy density and safety highly. Cooperation is also taking concrete shape in next-generation solid-state batteries. Hyundai Motor, Kia and Samsung SDI jointly filed a total of nine solid-state-related patents, including divisional applications, from 2022 through last year, two of which were registered last year. Initially the focus was on coating technology to protect sulfide-based solid electrolytes that are vulnerable to moisture, but from 2023 the research scope widened to battery life improvement and mass-production processes. A representative example is the joint filing of temperature-measurement technology for the high-temperature warm isostatic pressing (WIP) process needed to manufacture solid-state batteries, along with battery-cell preheating and transfer devices. Solid-state batteries replace liquid electrolytes with solid ones to improve safety and energy density, and their applications could expand beyond EVs to humanoid robots and other uses. Euisun Chung, chairman of Hyundai Motor Group, said in August regarding the group's electrification strategy: "EVs will go their own way as EVs, but we are also researching solid-state batteries, so that part has to come out before we can move to a more efficient direction." Note: Publication and registration dates and contract terms are based on the Korea Intellectual Property Rights Information Service and industry confirmation. Executive-level exchanges underpin the broadening of the two groups' cooperation. On the 9th, Samsung Electronics hosted "HMG Appreciation Day" at its Seocheon Training Center in Yongin, Gyeonggi Province, inviting key Hyundai Motor Group executives. Samsung Electronics Vice Chairman Jeon Young-hyun and Hyundai Motor Group Vice Chairman Jang Jae-hoon presided over the event, which was attended by 177 people, including executives, senior managers and spouses from both groups. It was the first time Samsung has held a large-scale invitation event for a specific South Korean group. At the event, Vice Chairman Jang said, "Samsung and Hyundai Motor Group are expanding the possibilities for cooperation beyond vehicle components such as automotive electronics, audio and batteries to future industries such as robots and energy," adding, "I hope we will respect each other's strengths, pool our efforts and take on future challenges together." Vice Chairman Jeon responded, "I hope Samsung's technology, spanning components to finished products, will come together to open up new value and infinite possibilities." The two companies' ties date back to 2020. In May 2020, when Chairman Chung was senior vice chairman, he visited Samsung SDI's Cheonan plant and discussed next-generation EV batteries with Samsung Electronics Chairman Lee Jae-yong, and two months later Lee paid a return visit to Hyundai Motor and Kia's Namyang Research Institute. This exchange is seen as having paved the way for the 2023 supply contract. A relationship that had been kept at arm's length — partly because of Samsung's foray into the auto business in the 1990s — has turned into a cooperative framework under third-generation management. Robots are cited as the next point of contact for cooperation. In February last year, Hyundai Motor, Kia and Samsung SDI signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) to jointly develop high-performance batteries dedicated to robots. Under the structure, Samsung SDI handles materials and cell design, while Hyundai Motor and Kia's Robotics Lab applies them to actual robots and verifies performance. Humanoids must deliver large bursts of power while fitting batteries into a narrow body, and because they move in the same spaces as people, safety against impacts and repeated joint movement is also required. artigo.texto: Japan's AIST and Partners Develop Robotic System That Automates Synthesis of All-Solid-State Battery Materials, Processing 10 Samples in a Row The research group of Senior Researcher Yuki Yamaguchi at Japan's National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology (AIST), together with Denso Wave (Agui, Aichi Prefecture), Aichi Institute of Technology and the Aichi Center for Industry and Science Technology, has developed a "human-collaborative automated experiment system" that performs mechanochemical synthesis of all-solid-state battery materials as a seamless automated process. The partners announced the system in November 2026. It handles powders sensitive to moisture and oxygen inside a glove box under an inert gas atmosphere and can process up to 10 samples consecutively on a single command. The aim is to reduce reliance on manual work by researchers and boost the efficiency of materials exploration. Mechanochemical reactions are a technique that harnesses the mechanical energy generated when powder is crushed in a ball mill to drive chemical reactions. The series of tasks — weighing raw material powders and grinding beads, packing them into a container and running them through a planetary ball mill — has been replaced by robots. Because the solid electrolytes and electrode materials used in all-solid-state batteries react easily with moisture and oxygen in the air, the entire apparatus is housed in a glove box filled with inert gas. The hard part of automation was handling the powder. Delicate motions such as scooping powder with a spatula are difficult for robots to reproduce. Denso Wave developed an end tool dedicated to powder handling, while Aichi Institute of Technology designed automation modules to handle peripheral tasks such as opening and closing the ball mill containers. The joint research framework combined AIST's expertise in ceramics and battery materials with the Aichi Center for Industry and Science Technology's materials evaluation platform to integrate the component technologies. The system's throughput is 10 samples per command. The planetary ball mill handles two samples per run, and the design executes this five times in succession. From transporting reagent storage containers and ball mill containers to the grinding process and subsequent sample storage, the system performs the work automatically without interruption. Conditions such as reagent quantities, bead type and amount, mill rotation speed and processing time can be changed for each sample, allowing systematic investigation of diverse combinations. Reproducibility of experimental know-how is another feature. The system can automatically reproduce tacit knowledge such as how to select reagents and beads, weighing procedures and the order of operations, while also managing experiment parameters centrally as digital data. Such data can be used as explanatory variables for materials informatics (MI) and process informatics (PI), paving the way for AI-driven condition optimization. Note: Compiled based on the announcement. All-solid-state batteries are next-generation storage batteries expected to offer high safety and energy density, but developing the solid electrolytes and electrode materials that determine performance requires comprehensively investigating a wide range of compositions and processing conditions. Conventionally, researchers have repeated experiments by hand, which has been one factor holding down development efficiency. In 2023, AIST also used an automated powder-weighing device and a collaborative robot to speed up the search for conditions in a chemical sintering process that proceeds at 100°C or below; the latest work extends that technology to mechanochemical synthesis and all-solid-state battery materials. The research group plans to broaden the target materials and experimental processes and to refine the system so it can be applied to ceramics materials development in general. From fiscal 2029 onward, the partners are considering installing it as an experimental facility available for shared use, as part of a materials evaluation and development platform that regional companies can access. All-solid-state batteries are a field where major automakers and battery manufacturers in Japan and abroad are competing to achieve mass production, and the speed of materials development affects competitiveness. This initiative, combining experiment automation with data accumulation, offers materials exploration sites — where it is hard to rack up trial runs — the option of continuous, hands-free experimentation. Bridging to mass-production processes is essential for practical application, and attention will focus on whether making the equipment more versatile and opening it to regional companies can raise the level of Japan-originated materials development infrastructure.

artigo.texto: The data center industry is awaiting the commercialization of solid-state transformer technology, which skips power conversion steps and limits energy loss. The tech is already in use in electric vehicle charging and is about a year away from commercialization for data centers, where the voltages in question are much higher and the demand variances are swingier. According to Jeffries, the U.S. market for solid-state transformers will be about $4.3 billion per year by 2030 and would eliminate $1.39 million in costs per megawatt for data centers, which adds up for data centers that may be over 1,000 megawatts. Though many existing data centers are under construction already without the tech, the companies working on solid-state transformers believe that given that savings — and the chance to free up space for more processing — they’ll be able to plug in nicely into existing builds.

artigo.texto: Revolve Renewable Power agrees to acquire 6 MW Ontario battery storage portfolio for CAD $1.5 million Revolve Renewable Power Corp. (CSE: REVV; OTCQB: REVVF) signed a definitive agreement on October 30, 2026, to acquire Logan Energy Storage ULC and its three-project battery energy storage portfolio in Ontario. The deal is valued at CAD $1.5 million and covers a combined capacity of 6 MW / 11.7 MWh. Deal terms and structure Revolve executed the definitive equity purchase agreements on October 30, 2026, through a subsidiary. The structure is clean: Revolve is buying all issued and outstanding shares of Logan Energy Storage ULC, which holds the three Ontario BESS projects. The total purchase price is CAD $1,500,000, funded entirely from cash already on the balance sheet — no new debt, no equity financing required to close. The seller is at arm’s length to Revolve, so there are no related-party considerations. The transaction still needs to clear customary closing conditions and applicable regulatory approvals before it’s final, and Revolve hasn’t put a target closing date out there publicly. Once the Logan acquisition closes, Revolve expects its Ontario battery storage capacity to reach approximately 20.2 MW / 36.0 MWh across nine projects. Why Revolve is acquiring the Logan portfolio The Logan deal isn’t a one-off move. It fits squarely into Revolve’s stated strategy of building a battery storage platform in Ontario while simultaneously advancing a greenfield development pipeline in the province. Ontario’s energy storage market has become a deliberate focus for the company. Revolve completed its first major step in that direction back in August 2026, when it closed the acquisition of the Trillium Storage portfolio — six projects totaling 14.2 MW / 24.3 MWh. Logan is the follow-on, adding three more projects to that growing base. CEO Myke Clark described the transaction as part of the company’s “disciplined acquisition and development strategy.” That language signals Revolve is selecting assets that fit a defined platform-building approach in a market it’s already committed to — not chasing deals opportunistically. Expected impact on Revolve’s Ontario storage capacity Once the Logan acquisition closes, Revolve expects its Ontario battery storage capacity to reach approximately 20.2 MW / 36.0 MWh across nine projects. That’s a meaningful jump from where it stood before Trillium, when the company had zero operating storage assets in the province. The math is straightforward. Six Trillium projects contributed 14.2 MW / 24.3 MWh. Logan’s three projects add 6 MW / 11.7 MWh on top of that, bringing the combined total to nine projects across the two acquisitions. Clark emphasized that the Logan deal is expected to further establish Revolve’s presence in Ontario — and beyond the capacity numbers, the company is targeting contracted, cash-generating assets that produce recurring revenue rather than depending on merchant power prices alone. Worth noting: these are forward-looking expectations. Revolve has flagged that actual results could differ depending on regulatory approvals, operational performance, and whether the portfolio performs in line with management’s assumptions. Background: Revolve’s growth in Canadian energy storage Revolve Renewable Power Corp. is headquartered in Vancouver, BC. The company owns, operates, and develops power generation and digital infrastructure projects across North America, trading on the Canadian Securities Exchange under REVV and on the OTCQB under REVVF. Battery energy storage systems — BESS — store electricity and discharge it back to the grid when it’s needed. They play an increasingly important role in supporting grid stability and integrating variable renewable sources like wind and solar. Ontario, with its evolving energy mix and ongoing grid modernization efforts, has become an active market for exactly this kind of infrastructure. Revolve’s entry into Ontario battery storage is relatively recent; the Trillium acquisition in August 2026 was its first major transaction in this space, and management has indicated it expects to keep building through further acquisitions and development activity. What this deal means for Revolve going forward Taken together, the Trillium and Logan acquisitions give Revolve a nine-project, 20.2 MW / 36.0 MWh battery storage footprint in Ontario — assembled in roughly three months. For a company that had no Ontario storage assets before mid-2026, that’s a notable pace of portfolio construction. The Logan deal’s modest price tag — CAD $1.5 million funded from existing cash — also reflects a capital-efficient approach. Revolve isn’t stretching its balance sheet to make this happen, which leaves room for continued deal-making if the right opportunities come up. What happens next depends on closing. Once customary conditions and regulatory approvals are satisfied, Revolve will hold a nine-project Ontario storage portfolio that it describes as a foundation for longer-term growth, both through additional acquisitions and through its greenfield development pipeline in the province. artigo.texto: A Eletronet anunciou nesta segunda-feira, 9, um investimento de R$ 25 milhões para construção de um novo data center em São Paulo. Com obras já iniciadas, a previsão é de que a unidade entre em operação no primeiro trimestre de 2027. Segundo a empresa especializada em infraestrutura de telecomunicações, o complexo denominado ELET1 terá aproximadamente 350 m², capacidade para cerca de 90 racks e potência inicial de 0,5 megawatt (MW), podendo chegar a 1 MW em uma futura expansão. A Eletronet informou que o novo centro de dados deve fortalecer a oferta de serviços de colocation, conectividade e interconexão, além de ampliar a escala ao atendimento de provedores de nuvem, operadoras de telecom, provedores de serviços de Internet (ISPs) e hyperscalers. "O ELET1 representa um passo estratégico para fortalecer nossa atuação no segmento de data centers. Estamos ampliando nossa estrutura para atender às necessidades dos clientes que já utilizam nossos serviços e abrir novas oportunidades de negócios, em um contexto no qual a hiperconectividade e a disponibilidade se tornam cada vez mais essenciais", afirma Rogerio Garchet, CEO da Eletronet, em nota. Região estratégica De acordo com a Eletronet, o complexo será instalado em uma localização com elevada concentração de redes de telecomunicações e provedores de conteúdo. Desse modo, estará preparado para atender à crescente demanda por serviços de data center para os segmentos de nuvem, streaming e telecom. A unidade também vai abrigar o ponto de interconexão (PIX) da Eletronet no IX.br São Paulo, um dos maiores pontos de troca de tráfego de Internet do mundo. O PIX da empresa, inclusive, tem se destacado no volume de tráfego de download na infraestrutura paulista. O objetivo desse movimento, segundo a empresa, é aumentar as possibilidades de conexão dos clientes com diferentes redes e provedores de serviços digitais. A Eletronet ainda ressaltou que o ELET1 integra a sua estratégia no segmento de data centers e de expansão da sua rede nacional de fibra óptica. Quando o centro de dados estiver em plena operação, a empresa planeja migrar a infraestrutura do data center atualmente em operação em São Paulo para o novo ambiente. Sustentabilidade Em comunicado, a Eletronet salientou que o ELET1 será construído levando em conta as melhores práticas globais de infraestrutura, incluindo soluções de proteção física e lógica, seguindo as diretrizes da norma ISO 27001. Além disso, o data center terá aplicações modernas de gestão ambiental e energética, com base nos padrões ISO 14001, ISO 50001 e LEED. A unidade ainda deve contar com dois geradores redundantes de 500 kVa, dupla entrada de rede, backbone DWDM protegido, sistema de gerenciamento predical (BMS) atualizado, monitoramento contínuo e um Centro de Operações de Rede (NOC) de contingência.

The SUV seen in the latest spy shots is the all-electric version, with EV badging on the tailgate. In international markets, the Atto 2 is also available with a plug-in hybrid (PHEV) powertrain, but the test vehicle spotted in India is the electric version. On the side profile, the SUV gets black and silver body cladding that covers the wheel arches and door sills. It features electric-release door handles, sporty dual-tone alloy wheels, and a charging port on the front fender. The overall design is that of a compact midsize SUV, likely targeting urban buyers. The rear section features connected LED tail-lamps, a roof-mounted spoiler, and a dual-tone bumper. The bumper also gets integrated reflectors and subtle silver accents. The latest spotting gives a much clearer picture of the Atto 2’s overall design compared to the earlier camouflaged test vehicle. BYD Atto 2 EV: Battery, Range and Performance International-spec BYD Atto 2 EV is available with two battery pack options – 45.1kWh and 64.8kWh. Both versions get a front-axle-mounted electric motor, but the output battery varies depending on the variant. According to BYD’s international specifications, the BYD Atto 2 EV has a 0-100kph acceleration time of 7.9 seconds, while the claimed top speed is 170kph. The company claims a WLTP-certified range of up to 430km for the larger battery version. For charging, the SUV offers 11kW AC charging support and up to 155kW DC fast-charging capability. Confirmation of which battery pack and charging specification will be offered in India is expected closer to launch. Also Read: BYD Denza Z9 GT Coming to India With 1000hp+ Power: What We Know So Far Cabin Features: 12.8-inch Rotatable Touchscreen and Panoramic Sunroof The cabin of the international-spec BYD Atto 2 EV comes with a minimalist dashboard layout. It features a 12.8-inch rotatable touchscreen infotainment system, which takes center stage, similar to BYD’s larger Atto 3. It also features an 8.8-inch digital driver display. The feature list includes a panoramic sunroof, a 6-speaker audio system, a 50W wireless phone charger, and a 360-degree camera. The SUV also features a Vehicle-to-Load (V2L) function, which allows compatible external devices to be powered by the vehicle’s battery. Front and rear parking sensors are also part of the international model. It is not yet clear which of these features will be standard or available in selected variants in the India-spec model. Local specifications and equipment list should not be taken as confirmed details. Which electric SUVs will it compete with in India? The potential arrival of the BYD Atto 2 EV in India could make the competition in the midsize electric SUV segment more interesting. This category already includes models like the Maruti Suzuki e Vitara, Toyota Urban Cruiser Ebella, MG ZS EV, VinFast VF6, and Hyundai Creta Electric. The upcoming Tata Sierra EV, Mahindra BE 6, and Tata Curvv EV also expand buyers’ options in this competitive space. The Atto 2’s positioning and final pricing will determine how strong an alternative it can be against these models. If BYD introduces a more accessible electric SUV below the Atto 3 in India, it could give the company a chance to reach a wider customer base. But its success will depend on battery options, real-world range, charging performance, and pricing. Auto India Daily Verdict Undisguised spotting has certainly piqued interest in the BYD Atto 2 EV. A 64.8kWh battery, up to 430km claimed WLTP range, 155kW DC charging, and a feature-rich cabin make it a promising electric SUV, as per international specifications. Pricing will be the most important factor in India. If BYD launches it at a noticeably more affordable price point than the Atto 3, the Atto 2 could become an important volume-oriented model for the company. Official confirmation of the India launch date, battery options, and pricing is currently awaited. artigo.texto: Mini data centers – O Governo Federal vai investir R$ 46,3 milhões no desenvolvimento de uma tecnologia nacional para tornar data centers mais eficientes, seguros e sustentáveis. Aprovado pelo Conselho Gestor do Fundo para o Desenvolvimento Tecnológico das Telecomunicações (Funttel), o projeto prevê uma plataforma inteligente para gerenciar e distribuir dados entre diferentes estruturas, incluindo mini data centers em várias regiões do país. Batizada de Prisma, a iniciativa utilizará inteligência artificial (IA) para definir onde as informações devem ser processadas e distribuir os recursos computacionais conforme a demanda. A tecnologia busca reduzir gastos com energia, custos operacionais e tempo de resposta dos sistemas, além de reforçar a proteção de dados estratégicos. LEIA: Inteligência artificial facilita invasões e aumenta alcance de hackers “Investir em tecnologia nacional é garantir que o Brasil tenha mais autonomia para proteger suas informações e desenvolver soluções para os desafios do futuro. Com o apoio do Funttel, estamos fortalecendo a inovação brasileira e criando condições para uma infraestrutura digital mais moderna, segura e sustentável, reduzindo nossa dependência de tecnologias desenvolvidas no exterior”, afirma o ministro das Comunicações, Frederico de Siqueira Filho. Os recursos serão administrados pela Financiadora de Estudos e Projetos (Finep), enquanto o desenvolvimento ficará sob responsabilidade do Centro Brasileiro de Inovação em Tecnologias da Informação e da Comunicação (CPQD), em Campinas (SP). A expansão dos mini data centers permitirá processar informações mais perto de onde são geradas e utilizadas, beneficiando setores como saúde, defesa, segurança pública, educação e telecomunicações. Eficiência energética e autonomia tecnológica O projeto também pretende diminuir o impacto ambiental dos data centers, que demandam grandes quantidades de energia para processamento e refrigeração. Entre os resultados esperados estão a redução das emissões de carbono, maior resistência a falhas no fornecimento elétrico e proteção contra ataques cibernéticos. A plataforma deverá incluir sistemas de armazenamento de energia e mecanismos de governança de informações críticas, seguindo padrões internacionais de segurança e as diretrizes da Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados (LGPD). artigo.texto: GREENFIELD — Planning Director Ella Wise will have a full plate over the next few months as she leads the Planning Board through changes in permitting for clean energy facilities, as well as carrying out plans to create zoning ordinances regulating battery energy storage systems and data centers in Greenfield. She told the board on Thursday that her work pertaining to changing regulations in technology will start with training city staff on new Massachusetts laws for consolidated permitting for clean energy projects. In 2024, the state Legislature signed a new climate law to speed up permitting for clean energy infrastructure, including solar, wind, anaerobic digestion and battery energy storage facilities. Wise said the law took effect on Oct. 1, allowing developers to opt into a new permitting process in which all departments review projects for approval at the same time, rather than the previous system in which applicants filed with each department individually. “They need to conduct a certain amount of public outreach and meet with city staff, and if all those conditions are met, they have 12 months for us to give them a ‘yes’ or a ‘no’ on their permit,” Wise said. “And that ‘yes’ or ‘no’ has to include the Planning Board and [the Zoning Board of Appeals’] decision, as well as the Conservation Commission’s decision and the Board of Health.” She added that municipalities also have the option of having the state’s Energy Facilities Siting Board assist with or oversee the review. Wise said the city does not need to change any of its zoning codes and regulations because of the state change, but she recommended that the Planning Board review the codes for clean energy facilities. Throughout the rest of the year, Wise said she plans to work with the Franklin Regional Council of Governments on a battery energy storage system ordinance, and come 2027, she will turn her attention to developing data center regulations before City Council’s one-year moratorium expires. The council adopted the moratorium in September. Battery energy storage systems While Greenfield has regulations in place for solar systems and other energy production facilities, Wise told the Planning Board that the city does not have any for battery energy storage systems, and it would be prudent to develop some. “We do have solar zoning. You don’t have any zoning for batteries,” Wise said. “So I think we need to start that process.” Wise said she has drafted an ordinance for battery energy storage systems based on a model state bylaw, and she plans to spend the next few months revising it, with technical assistance from FRCOG. She hopes that by February 2027, the draft will be ready for Planning Board and City Council approval. The draft, which was included in the board’s packet, defines a battery energy storage system as “a system consisting of one or more battery modules for storing electrical energy, any equipment needed to support the safe and proper function or usage of the battery modules, and one or more physical containers providing secondary containment to any of the above. It may be a primary or accessory use to a solar generating facility, power generation facility or other similar uses.” The draft ordinance states that small Tier 1 facilities would be allowed by right in all districts. Larger Tier 2 and 3 facilities would be allowed by right in the General Industrial (GI) and Planned Industry (PI) zoning districts, but would require special permits in the Rural Residential (RC), Suburban Residential (RB), General Commercial (GC) and Office (O) zoning districts. Battery energy storage systems would be prohibited in all other districts. Wise said that while her draft does outline examples of what the different size tiers could be and where they could be allowed, ultimately, the Planning Board would need to make policy decisions on whether battery energy storage systems should be allowed by right or by special permit, what the setback requirements should be and if there should be any required mitigation of environmental impacts. Data centers Wise said she expects a model data center bylaw to be published by the state next month, which would provide the Planning Board with a jumping-off point from which to start drafting its own regulations. “I don’t think I can work on a BESS bylaw while working on a data center one,” Wise said. “It just feels like so much to juggle. … So what I’m proposing is to focus our energy on BESS over the next few months, trying to get it done at the end of winter so that we have spring and summer to really have a robust process around data centers.” She expects that throughout the first few months of 2027, the Planning Board will research best practices and review other municipalities’ regulations. From March to May, the board will deliberate on what Greenfield’s version should look like and conduct public outreach, finalizing the ordinance in June or July. The city’s one-year moratorium on the construction of data centers is set to expire in September 2027. Planning Board member Thomas Bledsoe said he attended some trainings on data centers recently, and that noise was one of the largest concerns among the potential impacts, which the board should look to address with its regulations. “I really do think noise is a key issue here, and since it’s a 24-hour service, when we have to think hard about it, I would love to have some specific noise parameters in our code,” Bledsoe said. As the board moves forward, he said it should plan to work with other departments, particularly the Board of Health, and other communities.

artigo.texto: Swiss battery developer Unbound Potential has begun installing its first external pilot system at Gesundheitspark Thalwil, near Zürich. The stationary battery uses the company’s membrane-free redox flow technology and will store surplus electricity generated by the health and sports centre’s photovoltaic installation. Stored energy will be released when required. The installation follows almost four years of research and development and represents the technology’s first deployment outside Unbound Potential’s own test environment. The company said operating the system under real-world conditions would provide data on its performance and reliability as it works towards commercialisation. Unbound Potential: a simpler cell design by eliminating the membrane The company claims that eliminating the membrane used in conventional redox flow batteries enables a simpler cell design, with the potential to reduce manufacturing costs and resource consumption. The company is targeting stationary, long-duration applications, including renewable-energy integration and grid support. The pilot is being supported by the Municipality of Thalwil through its Climate Funding Programme. Gesundheitspark Thalwil, which operates what Unbound Potential described as the municipality’s largest photovoltaic system, is providing the host site. Dr David Taylor, CEO and co-founder of Unbound Potential, said: “Having our first pilot battery go into operation here in Thalwil, where everything started, means a great deal to us. “After almost four years of development, our technology is being deployed for the first time at an external partner. It is a big moment for our entire team.” The system had arrived at the site and was being installed and prepared for commissioning when the announcement was made. The company did not disclose its rated power, energy capacity, intended storage duration or commissioning date. Unbound Potential was founded in January 2023 and employs 28 people. It said it had raised more than CHF14 million ($17.5 million) in investment and grant funding from backers including the Migros Pioneer Fund, Germany’s Federal Agency for Disruptive Innovation, SPRIND, and the Swiss Innovation Agency, Innosuisse. artigo.texto: SoftBank reported a fiscal second-quarter net loss of 1.12 trillion yen ($7 billion) on Tuesday, as losses tied to U.S. AI data center equipment procurement and Intel share declines weighed on earnings. The Japanese investment giant also recorded a 597.2 billion ($3.7 billion) yen loss in the six months ending on Sept. 30 due to changes in procurement plans for power generation equipment for AI data center projects in the U.S. SoftBank said it had made advance investments to secure power generation equipment for its AI data center projects in the U.S. amid concerns over potential shortages and long procurement lead times. Power is increasingly becoming a key constraint for the AI data center buildout as power grids become overwhelmed with applications from large energy users like data centers. Cumulative payments for power-generation equipment for U.S. AI data center projects, like the PORTS-Pike Technology Campus in Pike County, Ohio, totaled $9.48 billion as of the end of September. "We made bridge investments in advance to secure power generation equipment in anticipation of shortage," a SoftBank executive said during the company's earnings call. Here's how SoftBank fared in the fiscal second quarter: - Net loss of 1.12 trillion yen in the quarter compared with a net profit of 2.5 trillion yen a year earlier. - Revenue stood at 2.22 trillion yen in the quarter, compared with LSEG estimates of 2.02 trillion yen. Revenue rose 13.3% in the six months ended Sept. 30, supported by growth in telecommunications and AI computing businesses. The company said its SoftBank segment recorded higher sales across all businesses, while revenue at its AI computing segment increased. The company's Vision Fund segment swung to a loss of 81.58 billion yen in the fiscal second quarter, compared with a profit of 2.38 trillion yen a year earlier. Vision Fund 1 recorded an investment loss of $20 million in the quarter, despite a $1.3 billion gain on ByteDance, as shares of publicly traded portfolio companies, including Coupang and Grab, declined. The Vision Funds segment recorded investment gains of 85.45 billion yen, down sharply from 2.81 trillion yen in the year-earlier period. Vision Fund 2 posted investment gains of 89.26 billion yen, while Vision Fund 1 recorded a loss of 3.86 billion yen on its investments. As of the end of September, SoftBank's cumulative investment in OpenAI stood at $54.6 billion, with a fair value of $99.6 billion and a cumulative investment gain of $45 billion, according to the company. SoftBank said a potential increase in OpenAI's valuation following a new funding round had not yet been reflected in its results, pending an official announcement. The updated valuation could be reflected in the fiscal third quarter, potentially boosting its net asset value and improving its loan-to-value ratio, the company said. "ChatGPT has been continuously a weapon of OpenAI, especially for consumers," the SoftBank esecutive said during the company's earnings call, highlighting the chatbot's growing user base. AI worries hit stocks Shares of the Japanese investment giant closed 13.9% higher on Tuesday. The gains came as Asian technology stocks, including Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, rose following an overnight rebound on Wall Street. On its AI infrastructure investments, SoftBank highlighted a 20-year lease agreement with OpenAI for eight gigawatts of IT capacity at a data center project in Ohio. Addressing concerns of water consumption at its planned data center in Texas, SoftBank said it was taking steps to reduce water use through a closed-loop, air-cooled system. The company also pointed to plans to hire and source locally. Ahead of its earnings release, SoftBank Group announced on Monday plans with Grab and Malaysia's PETROS to commit a combined $1.85 billion in initial capital to develop AI infrastructure in Malaysia, with a long-term target of at least five gigawatts of AI computing capacity.

artigo.texto: Microsoft data center in Washington state brings "a kind of boom" despite growing AI pushback Opposition to data centers helped propel Democratic candidates who pledged to stall new construction to victory in last week's midterm elections. More than half of voters said artificial intelligence and data centers were a significant factor in their votes, according to a CBS News exit poll. But one town says it has benefited from data centers, despite the pushback growing across the nation. For 20 years, Microsoft has operated its Columbia Data Center in Quincy, Washington, where Mayor Paul Worley told CBS News its presence has created "a kind of boom" for the area. Additional tax revenue from the project has funded a new high school and hospital, and helped improve other critical services, he said. Microsoft president Brad Smith told CBS News about the pledge it makes to the communities where it builds and operates data centers. "Basically, we will put the community first," he said. "We will not do anything that will increase the electricity rates of our neighbors. We'll ensure that we replenish more water, we put more water back into the community than we use." He also highlighted the role data centers play in powering every action we take on our phones and other connected devices. "Every time we tap on our phone, it's connecting through an app, it's pulling data from something like this," he said. The industry, he said, needs to better inform opponents of data centers about the essential services the facilities enable. "They're part of daily life, just like electricity is," Smith said. Why Quincy? The nearby Columbia River provides hydropower that has led seven additional companies to choose Quincy for their data centers. It hasn't been entirely smooth. To accommodate the roughly two dozen data centers that have entered the area over the past two decades, some residents have been asked to vacate their homes. Electricity rates per kilowatt-hour have risen by roughly 55% over the past 20 years, according to the Grant County public utility. While that marks a steep increase, it's still lower than the average increases in national and state electricity rates over the same period. In Washington, electricity rates rose 107% over the same time period. Nationwide, they rose 66%. Smith said he believes it is the company's "fundamental responsibility" to manage the industry's growth and the impact on residents' rising utility costs. "You can't make the challenges go away, but you can be broad-minded, you can [be] committed, and you can take steps to manage growth well," he said. For example, Microsoft pledges to replenish or give communities back more water than it uses. It also commits to paying for its own electricity and ensuring that its usage doesn't increase neighbors' utility rates, Smith said. He added that the facilities create local jobs, too, though many are temporary construction positions. According to Microsoft, the company employs roughly 700 people, or almost 9% of Quincy's roughly 8,000 residents. Questions to ask Yale professor of environmental and energy economics Kenneth Gillingham outlined the questions communities should ask data center developers before they come to town. They include: - What type of technology is it using for cooling? - How large will it be? - How is it going to generate its electricity? Meanwhile, Microsoft's Smith has a clear message for Americans who say they don't want data centers in their backyards. "Give us a chance to talk through what we want to do, and give us a chance to prove that we can do this in a way that will put the community first," he said. "We have to persuade you. But the people that you've elected, they're the ones who are gonna make a decision, not us."

artigo.texto: Anchor Energy launches €75m BESS fund Danish investment platform Anchor Energy Partners has launched a fund with a €75m target that aims to invest in flexibility assets across Europe. Anchor Fund I will acquire and operate derisked, ready-to-build flexibility and storage assets, eventually expanding into renewable colocation and industrial energy. The fund’s initial close was backed by founding investor and co-owner 2degrees, a 50:50 joint venture between Macquarie Asset Management and Aware Super. Financial details were not disclosed. The founding partners are Fabian Siegel, Lasse Helstrup, Alejandra Huerta, Abhi Chirimar and Ludvig Holsteinborg. Their experience spans investing and asset management at Orsted, Danske Commodities, AIP, Icecreek Energy and Boston Consulting Group. The team managed €30bn in funds, including two IPOs, and more than 120MWh of operational BESS in Germany and Finland. Copenhagen-based Anchor said using BESS is the fastest way to add flexibility to Europe’s energy system. The continent has less than 80GWh of BESS capacity against a 1.2GWh requirement by 2050.

artigo.texto: Riverside Council Enshrines Temporary Data Center Ban Language While City Researches AI The Riverside City Council Tuesday voted 5-2 to adopt a resolution barring the city from accepting data center proposals, since the land use is not currently included in city code. Riverside has joined a number of other cities in the county in temporarily banning data centers, though the council took a much different approach than its neighbors. The Riverside City Council Tuesday voted 5-2 to adopt a resolution barring the city from accepting data center proposals, since the land use is not currently included in city code, while a council-led committee researches artificial intelligence (AI) policies, foregoing a second option to impose a 45-day temporary moratorium. “We need to pause the moving forward of development so [we] can figure out, and do that deep dive, and do that research, and set those regulations, and set those parameters,” Councilmember Philip Falcone said at the November 10 council meeting. “To not do them in tandem is disjoint and, I think, not strategic.” Councilmembers Chuck Conder and Sean Mill voted against the resolution — although Mill, in a phone call with The Riverside Record, said he chose to vote against the resolution because he preferred establishing a temporary ban like other cities across the county have done. The council’s decision to move forward with the resolution followed a now-updated agreement between the city of Riverside and a nonprofit organization that previously mentioned a possible data center as part of its proposal. The agreement originally said the nonprofit, and its for-profit counterpart, would “contemplate” the development of a data center after establishing an office in the city. The CEO for both organizations previously told the city’s Economic Development Committee the idea was to create a data center meant for community use — which would have been contained within a typical office server room — to help with training residents on emerging technologies. Falcone, who championed efforts to restrict data centers within city limits, said at the September 14 Land Use Committee meeting that the agreement pushed him to request that staff bring forward a temporary data center ban to the council for discussion. He said he felt a ban would preserve commercial land for sectors he believed would bring more jobs, prevent an electrical grid overload and protect the city’s water supply. The following day, the council voted to create a 13-month AI working group tasked with developing a “forward-looking” strategy to address AI’s rapid growth and outline how the city should utilize the technology in the future. Councilmember Steven Robillard, who is leading the working group, said the group plans to tackle data center policies in the coming months. That decision led city staff to return to the Land Use Committee in October to ask for clarification on how to proceed with the dueling requests. After a discussion, the committee directed staff to bring forward two options: establish an urgency ordinance to impose a temporary 45-day moratorium on the approval of any data center developments that could be extended for up to two years total or adopt language that highlights the city is technically prohibited from accepting data center proposals at this time due to current city code. “There [are] no proposals on the table right now,” Robillard said at the November 10 meeting. “I think the resolution sends the proper message that we currently don’t have a zoning that allows for data centers, we need to discuss the entire conversation in-and-around AI, and its related uses including data centers, and, until we do that, approving the data center doesn’t make any sense.” During public comment, residents and environmental advocates said they supported placing restrictions on data center development due to their concerns with potential long-term negative impacts on the community. However, several union representatives said they were opposed to a ban, citing recently signed California laws placing restrictions on the facilities and concerns that any prohibitions would eliminate job opportunities for union members. “If we utilize the latest technologies like closed loop systems for cooling and a clean energy infrastructure, they could be successful,” Anthony Zambrano, an International Union of Operating Engineers Local 12 representative, said. “In my opinion, no one builds these systems better than union labor.” Conder, throughout his reelection campaign, said he was a proponent of data centers. At a community forum held last month, Conder said he believed the technology has been rapidly improving and could be built to minimize harm to both communities and the environment. “Not all data centers are a million square feet,” Conder said at the November 10 meeting. “They can be as small as a medium-sized box truck that delivers in town here.” He also said, both at the November 10 council meeting and in statements throughout his campaign, that he believed much of the opposition to data centers was funded by foreign governments that prefer to have the facilities built in their countries. An investigation into the claim by NPR found little evidence of a coordinated Chinese campaign to stop data centers in the U.S. The next AI ad hoc committee meeting is scheduled for December 3. The group will continue to meet over the next year to discuss AI-related topics, including data centers, and is set to present a list of policy recommendations for the full council to review later next year. artigo.texto: Expansão em Belo Jardim elevará a capacidade de fornecimento de sistemas de armazenamento de energia para mais de 8 GWh por ano. Empresa atua em parceria com a chinesa CATL e mira o primeiro leilão nacional de baterias. A expansão do mercado de armazenamento de energia no Brasil abriu uma nova oportunidade para a indústria nordestina. O Grupo Moura anunciou um investimento estimado em R$ 200 milhões para ampliar sua estrutura de fabricação de sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias, conhecidos como BESS, em Belo Jardim, no Agreste de Pernambuco. Com a ampliação, a companhia pretende alcançar uma capacidade de fornecimento superior a 8 GWh por ano. O projeto combina tecnologia da chinesa CATL com montagem, integração e atividades industriais realizadas no Brasil. A princípio, a iniciativa ocorre às vésperas dos primeiros leilões brasileiros destinados à contratação de sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias, previstos para os dias 2 e 4 de dezembro de 2026. Belo Jardim entra na disputa por um novo mercado de energia O investimento amplia a atuação de uma empresa que já possui uma trajetória de quase sete décadas na fabricação de baterias. Fundada em 1957, em Belo Jardim, a Moura construiu no município um complexo industrial que atende diferentes segmentos, incluindo os mercados automotivo, industrial e de armazenamento de energia. Segundo informações da companhia, a expansão de aproximadamente R$ 200 milhões reúne investimentos recentes e um novo ciclo de modernização da estrutura produtiva. Além disso, a empresa já possui experiência em mais de 40 projetos de armazenamento instalados no Brasil, com aplicações em setores como indústria, agronegócio, saúde, saneamento e entretenimento. Parceria com empresa chinesa combina tecnologia e produção local A Moura atua ao lado da CATL, fabricante chinesa de baterias e sistemas de armazenamento de energia. A parceria entre as empresas começou em 2020, inicialmente com serviços de assistência técnica, manutenção e pós-venda de baterias de lítio. Agora, a cooperação também envolve o fornecimento de sistemas para os projetos que disputarão o leilão brasileiro. Nesse modelo, a CATL participa com sua tecnologia e experiência internacional, enquanto a Moura assume a industrialização e a integração dos equipamentos em Pernambuco. A estratégia busca atender às exigências de conteúdo nacional previstas para uma das modalidades do certame. Conteúdo nacional pode chegar a 60% Um dos diferenciais do projeto é a tentativa de ampliar a participação da indústria brasileira na cadeia de armazenamento de energia. De acordo com o diretor de operações de lítio do Grupo Moura, Spartacus Pedrosa, a empresa trabalha com uma rota de montagem e integração que pode atingir entre 50% e 60% de conteúdo local, conforme os critérios de nacionalização. Entretanto, a estratégia também pode facilitar o acesso dos equipamentos às linhas de financiamento do BNDES, desde que cumpram os requisitos de credenciamento. Primeiro leilão brasileiro de baterias acontece em dezembro A Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica aprovou os editais dos dois primeiros leilões de reserva de capacidade voltados a sistemas de armazenamento em baterias. O primeiro certame, em 2 de dezembro, será destinado a projetos que atendam às exigências de conteúdo nacional. Já o segundo, previsto para 4 de dezembro, terá regras diferentes de nacionalização. Os contratos terão duração de 15 anos, com início do fornecimento previsto para agosto de 2028. Os sistemas deverão disponibilizar potência por até quatro horas em cada ciclo, podendo ser acionados até duas vezes por dia. Dessa forma, as baterias poderão armazenar energia e devolvê-la ao sistema elétrico nos momentos de maior necessidade. Mercado desperta interesse de empresas A dimensão da oportunidade aparece no cadastramento realizado pela Empresa de Pesquisa Energética. Em agosto de 2026, a instituição informou que recebeu 6.091 projetos para os leilões, somando 296.807 MW de potência. Além disso, o volume demonstra o interesse do mercado por soluções de armazenamento, embora nem todos os projetos inscritos necessariamente participem ou vençam os certames. LEIA TAMBÉM: - Frutas, mel e celulose do Nordeste ganham o mercado da Europa - Estudo revela a situação das rodovias no Nordeste; veja como está por estado - Starbucks anuncia três lojas em Fortaleza e volta expansão no Nordeste - Nordeste ganha loja de gigante com 4 mil lojas pelo mundo; confira onde Investimento amplia importância industrial de Pernambuco Portanto, a ampliação da fábrica reforça a presença de Pernambuco em uma cadeia produtiva relacionada à transição energética. Além da produção de baterias, Belo Jardim concentra atividades de montagem, tecnologia e reciclagem. Em 2025, o Governo de Pernambuco informou que o Grupo Moura contava com 4.114 colaboradores no estado. Afinal, o novo investimento pode ampliar a demanda por profissionais especializados, fornecedores industriais e serviços técnicos. Entretanto, a empresa ainda não divulgou o número de empregos adicionais que pretende gerar com a expansão. Com a entrada em um mercado de maior escala, Belo Jardim passa a disputar espaço em uma atividade estratégica para a modernização do setor elétrico brasileiro. O desafio agora será transformar a capacidade industrial anunciada em contratos efetivos, produção local e novas oportunidades econômicas para o Agreste pernambucano.

artigo.texto: A BYD e a TIM anunciaram duas parcerias no Brasil. A primeira prevê que os veículos leves produzidos pela montadora no país sairão de fábrica com conectividade da operadora embarcada. Ao todo, serão mais de 200 mil veículos com conectividade embarcada nos próximos 24 meses. A segunda contempla a implantação de infraestrutura dedicada de redes 4G e 5G no complexo industrial da montadora em Camaçari, na Bahia. Os modelos da empresa chinesa contarão com o eSIM da TIM, o que permitirá a ativação remota de serviços digitais. No complexo industrial da BYD em Camaçari, o projeto prevê a instalação de sete pontos de cobertura externa e 63 equipamentos distribuídos entre galpões e áreas operacionais. A proposta é oferecer uma rede capaz de acompanhar o crescimento da produção e atender às demandas tecnológicas da unidade. As redes 4G e 5G permitirão conectar colaboradores, visitantes, sistemas operacionais e veículos ainda durante o processo de fabricação. Inaugurado em outubro de 2025, o complexo industrial na Bahia possui 4,6 milhões de metros quadrados e é a maior operação industrial da BYD fora da China. A solução de Internet em Veículos (IoV) da TIM conecta, ao todo, mais de 630 mil veículos. Foto: complexo industrial da BYD em Camaçari, na Bahia. Crédito: divulgação.

artigo.texto: A homeowner in the United Kingdom considering spending an extra £2,000 ($2,670) on home battery storage received an unexpected recommendation from their solar installer: buy less capacity. In the installer's view, another battery module would probably cost more than the homeowner would save by avoiding occasional peak-rate electricity purchases. Here's what to know On Reddit, they wrote that they had been considering 15 kWh or 20 kWh as backup capacity given their daily winter consumption of about 14 kWh. However, their solar installer recommended only going with a 10 kWh capacity. "His advice is the cost to buy that little bit extra from grid is probably cheaper than adding another battery," the original poster wrote. "The extra cost might not make sense for ROI/savings." In addition to asking whether Redditors agreed with the solar installer's advice, the OP also wondered how easy it would be to add extra battery capacity down the line. For homeowners considering making the move to battery backup, EnergySage makes it easy to explore battery products and compare competitive installation estimates. EnergySage has partnered with electrification company Qmerit to help homeowners secure the best available battery-storage pricing. What commenters said When it came to the question of capacity, opinions were divided, though some acknowledged that it ultimately came down to what the OP's goals were. For one commenter, 10 kWh was too little capacity for their own goal of powering the entire house during an outage. While a suitably configured battery can keep household essentials running during outages, when paired with solar panels, it can also offer even greater energy independence, including off-grid use with certain systems. For the original poster, however, the priority was not whole-home backup but saving money on their electricity bill. By charging their home battery when rates were cheapest and using that electricity to power their home when rates were high, the OP hoped to limit the impact of soaring energy prices. Not all household electricity use has to be supplied by storage, another commenter explained. Solar generation consumed immediately and grid electricity used during cheap-rate periods both reduce the amount of energy that needs to pass through the battery. For households seeking a smaller backup option, Pila offers a plug-and-play alternative at a substantially lower price point than whole-home backup systems. Other considerations A 10 kWh starting point seemed more reasonable to the homeowner after a commenter raised the panels' potential contribution. Confirming that solar was part of the installation, the OP noted that even 1 to 2 kWh of winter generation could help offset consumption on heavier-use days. For charging and discharging power, commenters advised checking the battery stack's own specifications rather than relying on the inverter's rating. That distinction is particularly important when running several appliances. In one commenter's hypothetical example, an 8 kW inverter would still have only 5 kW available from a pair of battery modules delivering 2.5 kW each. As for the OP's question regarding battery expansion at a later date, one commenter noted that, for their setup, space for new modules had been an issue. Ultimately, that commenter had to have an inverter moved because it blocked the battery additions. The upgrade also required firmware updates, and the commenter recommended checking the manufacturer's commissioning and warranty requirements. Where can I learn more? Other U.K. homeowners have also been comparing the cost of battery storage with the savings it could deliver. • A U.K. homeowner sought retrofit battery storage after an installer said batteries weren't worthwhile. • A U.K. homeowner exploring battery-only storage to avoid peak electricity rates received a G98/G99 warning. • After solar was ruled out, a U.K. homeowner considered battery-only storage for savings. • A U.K. homeowner's 10-kWh battery payback estimate stretched from three years to five. • A U.K. homeowner's £6,999 battery quote drew scrutiny over £3,000 in installation costs. artigo.texto: South Korean scientists have just unveiled a new liquid-crystal polymer separator, which, when tested in a lithium-metal battery, retained 94 percent of its capacity after 100 charge-discharge cycles at a 4C charging rate. The separator was built by the a research team at the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST). It could reportedly improve battery stability and charging speed, meaning drivers could charge their EVs in just 15 minutes. The study was led by Dong Ki Yoon, PhD, and Hye Ryung Byon, PhD, professors at KAIST’s Department of Chemistry. “Lithium metal batteries can store more energy than conventional batteries,” they stated. “However, during charging, lithium can accumulate in sharp, branch-like structures known as ‘dendrites.'” For the separator, the researchers used liquid-crystalline polymers to control how the lithium ions move inside lithium-metal batteries. Both Yoon and Byon believe that their find could address slow ion transport and dendrite formation. A highway for lithium ions Lithium-metal batteries can store more energy than conventional ones. However, during charging, lithium can accumulate on the electrode surface and, as a result, form dendrites. These tiny needle-like metallic crystals grow on the anodes, and they can damage the separator between the electrodes, which could cause short circuits and increase the risk of fires. More from Energy See All To address this problem, the team created a porous separator made from liquid-crystalline polymers, which have an ordered structure like solids. They also share some properties with liquids. For the project, the team incorporated polyethylene glycol (PEG) chains into the material to facilitate lithium-ion transport. The scientists then monitored the alignment of the liquid-crystal molecules and arranged them either vertically or horizontally to examine how their orientation affected ion movement. The vertically aligned separator created direct pathways for lithium ions to travel toward the electrodes. In contrast to the horizontally aligned separator, it reduced the tortuosity (winding nature), of the ion transport pathways by about 2.5 times. This allowed the lithium ions to move faster and more uniformly. What’s more, it suppressed the dendrite formation and improved the battery stability. Longer battery life Ultimately, the researchers tested the separator in a working lithium-metal battery to evaluate its performance. To their massive surprise, the cell retained 94 percent of its initial capacity after 100 charge-discharge cycles at 4C. In simple terms, a 4C charging rate means a battery can fully recharge in 15 minutes. According to the team, controlling how molecules are arranged could potentially make batteries charge faster and last longer without compromising safety. Yoon emphasized the significance of this finding for future battery development. He said that molecular alignment plays a key role in battery performance. “We expect this approach to contribute to the development of high-energy-density next-generation battery technologies, for which long driving ranges and rapid charging are essential,” he concluded in a press release. The scientists believe the approach could contribute to the development of high-energy-density batteries for future EVs, where rapid charging and longer driving ranges are essential. Further tests will, however, show whether it works in larger batteries as well. The study has been published in the journal ACS Nano.

artigo.texto: Mark Trahant Substack There’s a story about Napoleon Bonaparte I have always liked. Something along the lines of “I know he’s a good general, but is he lucky.” Lucky. So often in my career I have been in the exact right place at the right time, being at places where I didn’t plan. Lucky. Last week I was honored with a Rural Power award by Groundswell and its Rural Renaissance Roadshow. Kenrick J. Escalanti, Quechan, nominated me for this honor to “recognize individuals whose leadership, ideas, storytelling, and service are helping shape a stronger and more equitable future for rural communities.” Instead of a mail-order plaque, the group gifted me a unique embroidered jean jacket to wear proclaiming “Rural Power.” Way cool. Here’s the lucky part. I have been thinking a lot about the debate going on in tribal and rural communities about data centers. It’s absolutely fine for tribes to pause or just say no. But could there also be a deeper conversation, what do we need when it comes to data storage, AI, and a digital future? Where is the richer conversation? Turns out that was the theme of the conference: “At the Data Center Crossroads.” The awards’ panel was first evening of the conference; a start of the conversation. And one of the first questions from the audience asked where I stood on data centers. I jumped right into the deep end. Two things. First, we need a better conversation about data centers and where they should be located. And, second, no elected official should ever sign a Non Disclosure Agreement. I think that runs counter to the public good. Transparency is an important value and the lack of it is exactly why we are having a terrible conversation about what’s needed and why. Data Centers at scale “What is a data center and what do people know?” asks Sherry Stout, program manager for the National Laboratory of the Rockies. She works with state and tribal governments. “So first and foremost, 38% of people statistically in this room, you live within five miles of a data center and you just might not know it,” she says. “If you ask what national polls say 35% of people would say that they have heard —quote — a lot about data centers in this past year. And why is that? … there’s 632 local governments have taken up the issue of data centers this year alone. It’s these very conversations that are so twisted. Data centers are pitched as inevitable on private and public land and many of the people involved won’t answer questions because they’ve signed those NDAs. Sherry Stout: “People are encountering news stories. They’re encountering political processes. They’re encountering social media that’s all about data centers. We’re seeing states that have paused large scale data centers and we’re seeing moratorium that are placed to say we need to pause and figure out what are these things? How are they affecting us and how do we need to go forward? There’s also, let’s just talk about the reality. There are a few very visible, very poorly done examples of data centers and those are going to drive conversations like it or not. NDAs are becoming a greater and greater issue. I spent a lot of last week with some of the hyperscalers talking about the issue of NDAs and it used to be in business that NDAs would actually speed things along because you would have some of that non-compete. But now the second a community finds out that their council has an NDA with a hyperscaler, that has changed the conversation and transparency is really changing. How we think about data transparency and what’s going on is really changing. Then there’s also just some of the reality of there’s a huge worldwide debate right now on the future of artificial intelligence or super intelligence if you work in the federal world. Data centers often can be the face, the physical manifestation of that conversation.” Billions, not millions Pearl Eva Walker is a member of the Memphis City Council where a huge generative A-I data center, Colossus, was built by Space X — Elon Musk —for Grok and is now leases computer capacity to Anthropic. Walker said the bill for that lease is $1.5 billion per month. (Soon to be Colossus 2 and Colossus 3.) More than 7,500 construction workers are building the facilities. That number of workers has caused significant impact to the communities in Memphis, including those across the line in Mississippi that don’t get the same benefits. “… God didn’t create data centers and they are not all good,” Walker said. “How do they become better? Hopefully all good. That’s up to us.” When all this started there were not many community rules in place. So the community had to develop legislation as the data centers were under construction while learning about the impacts as (or after) they happened. That leaves few paths forward for to protect the public. “What do municipalities need to know? If you’re thinking that a data center could come to your city or town, you need to check on the legislation that you have first concerning data centers,” she said. That means a comprehensive legislative plan that outlines what companies have to do and how to hold them accountable. Council Member Walker: “We’ve been accused of signing NDAs. I have not signed an NDA. I have not been asked to sign an NDA. Why? Because they didn’t need us for anything. Why not? Because we didn’t have any guardrails and moratoriums or anything that kept them from coming in. And then on the other side, there were entities such as the chamber that helped them come into the city and maneuver certain spaces and circumstances. But you want to start with the zoning because they can’t do anything without a parcel. So keep that in mind. The Paul Laurie location, it’s been zoned for commercial industrial since the 1950s. And we are in the process of doing some rezoning for the entire city already. And it will include zoning specific to data centers. That is very important because that’s going to guide your municipality, your leadership, the business

artigo.texto: - CATL chairman said sodium-ion batteries offer sufficient range for daily urban travel, while more swap stations can ease concerns about longer trips. - The company's swap stations now cover about 200 Chinese cities, with a target of more than 3,000 passenger car stations by year-end. CATL (HKEX: 3750) said its rapidly expanding battery-swapping network in China will help accelerate sodium-ion battery adoption by easing consumer concerns about driving range. The battery maker's chairman Robin Zeng made the remarks at a Benchmark Mineral Intelligence event in Shanghai, Bloomberg reported on Tuesday. Sodium-ion batteries offer sufficient range for daily urban travel, while an expanding swap network can ease concerns among drivers looking to make longer trips on weekends, Zeng said. "We are building battery-swapping stations on our own, leasing batteries to the consumers," Zeng said. "We need to build more swapping stations on the highways and in the cities." About 200 Chinese cities already have CATL swap stations, he said. The company aims to have more than 3,000 passenger car swap stations across China by the end of this year. Battery swapping allows drivers to replace depleted packs with fully charged ones within minutes, offering an alternative to conventional charging. CATL is promoting sodium-ion batteries as an alternative to traditional lithium-ion batteries in vehicles. The technology offers advantages in cold weather and is seen as potentially improving safety and reducing costs. However, energy density remains a key concern for sodium-ion battery adoption. CATL previously said it expects 10,000 to 20,000 electric vehicles to use its sodium-ion batteries this year. The company also views the technology as a risk management strategy to reduce its exposure to sharp swings in lithium prices. The company launched its Naxtra sodium-ion battery brand in April 2025 and jointly unveiled a passenger vehicle equipped with the battery with Changan Automobile in February this year. CATL said at the time that the vehicle's cells have an energy density of up to 175 Wh/kg and enable a driving range of more than 400 kilometers (249 miles), demonstrating the technology's ability to meet daily travel needs. Cold-weather performance is another key selling point. According to information CATL released in February, the battery retains more than 90% of its capacity at minus 40 degrees Celsius (minus 40 degrees Fahrenheit). The swap network provides supporting infrastructure for broader sodium-ion battery adoption. CATL announced in December 2025 that it had built 1,020 Choco-Swap stations across 45 cities. Its subsidiary Contemporary Amperex Energy Service Technology (CAES) said at the time that it planned to deploy sodium-ion batteries based on Naxtra technology at scale across its swap network starting in 2026.

artigo.texto: The Western Australian Government has awarded $15 million through the Investment Attraction Fund (IAF) New Energies Industries Round 2 to Australian Vanadium Limited (AVL) to establish a high-capacity, relocatable vanadium electrolyte manufacturing facility in the state. The project will expand AVL’s capacity to produce vanadium electrolyte to support large-scale battery installations as well as increasing local content in the vanadium flow battery supply chain. Related article: AVESS wins grant to explore vanadium flow battery manufacturing in Indo-Pacific Vanadium flow batteries use liquid vanadium electrolyte solutions in separate tanks to both store and release electricity. Skilled employment and training opportunities in advanced manufacturing, chemical processing, engineering, construction, commissioning, and plant operations will be created, while its modular and relocatable design enables deployment across regional and industrial centres throughout WA. The IAF funding will also support the development of grid-scale vanadium flow batteries and long-duration energy storage infrastructure in the state. WA State Development and Economic Diversification Minister David Michael said, “The Investment Attraction Fund continues to play a critical role in attracting projects that strengthen Western Australia’s industrial capabilities and support our energy transition. “By supporting AVL’s electrolyte manufacturing capability, we’re creating new opportunities in advanced manufacturing while helping position WA at the forefront of long-duration energy storage technologies. Related article: Western Australia doubles renewable energy target to 75% “The development of a high-capacity vanadium electrolyte facility will support local jobs, strengthen our manufacturing capability, and provide the foundations for future grid-scale battery projects across the state.”

artigo.texto: Nas aldeias da minoria étnica Thai, o conceito de floresta está passando por mudanças positivas. Enquanto no passado as pessoas rezavam aos espíritos da floresta para amenizar a raiva ao colher madeira para a construção de casas, agora suas orações expressam alegria e o desejo de que a floresta floresça ainda mais. As mudanças climáticas deixaram de ser uma ameaça futura e se tornaram uma realidade manifestada por meio de eventos climáticos extremos cada vez mais severos. Sob essa pressão, espera-se que a 31ª Conferência das Partes da Convenção-Quadro das Nações Unidas sobre Mudança do Clima (COP31), que começa na Turquia, promova compromissos mais firmes no enfrentamento das mudanças climáticas, especialmente na implementação de soluções de adaptação e na transição energética. Para o Vietname, a COP31 representa uma oportunidade para promover a cooperação internacional e reafirmar os esforços na proteção ambiental e na resposta às alterações climáticas. Em particular, o desenvolvimento de créditos de carbono florestal de alta qualidade é uma das direções importantes, contribuindo para reforçar a posição do Vietname no mercado internacional de carbono. Com uma maior conscientização sobre o valor das florestas, as pessoas estão participando cada vez mais ativamente da proteção desse recurso. Além da receita gerada pelos contratos de proteção florestal, os créditos de carbono estão abrindo novas oportunidades para a criação de meios de subsistência e o aumento da renda das comunidades. Contudo, a implementação prática do primeiro acordo de crédito de carbono revelou uma importante lição: a necessidade de uma implementação em larga escala, evitando a fragmentação. Cada projeto precisa abranger pelo menos 100.000 hectares, enquanto as áreas florestais destinadas às famílias são frequentemente dispersas e pequenas. Portanto, a formação de um órgão central de coordenação para conectar e organizar a implementação é um requisito essencial. O Sr. Nguyen Tien An, Diretor do Fundo Provincial de Proteção e Desenvolvimento Florestal de Nghe An , afirmou que o fundo atuará como um ponto focal para apoiar as comunidades participantes. Ao mesmo tempo, o fundo poderá coordenar ou autorizar organizações com plena capacidade jurídica a executar tarefas relacionadas. Além de estabelecer um órgão central de coordenação, também foi dada ênfase à consulta pública e à melhoria da capacidade de medição, relato e avaliação. Muitas localidades, incluindo províncias que se preparam para novos acordos, pesquisaram e prepararam proativamente as condições para participar do mercado interno de carbono e implementar projetos inter-regionais de grande escala. Na província de Lam Dong , as autoridades locais também estão se dedicando a preparar o conhecimento e a capacidade para a implementação de créditos de carbono florestal. O Sr. Le Dinh Viet, vice-chefe do Departamento Provincial de Proteção Florestal de Lam Dong, afirmou que a província organizou uma conferência com a participação de especialistas em carbono do governo central para trocar experiências, disseminar conteúdo e fornecer orientações sobre a implementação de tarefas relacionadas no próximo período. Além dos esforços proativos das autoridades locais, o quadro político para a gestão e o desenvolvimento florestal também está sendo gradualmente aprimorado. Após o decreto sobre o mecanismo piloto de pagamento, o Vietnã emitiu um novo decreto sobre investimento e apoio ao investimento na gestão, proteção, uso e desenvolvimento de florestas. Segundo o Sr. Pham Hong Luong, Diretor Adjunto do Departamento de Silvicultura e Proteção Florestal, a nova política é de grande importância para promover os pontos fortes internos dos proprietários florestais, ao mesmo tempo que cria condições para que parceiros e investidores internacionais participem no apoio ao desenvolvimento de projetos de grande escala a nível regional e inter-regional. Desde o compromisso assumido na COP26 de alcançar emissões líquidas zero até 2050 até o primeiro acordo de crédito de carbono florestal com o Banco Mundial , nos últimos cinco anos, o Vietnã construiu gradualmente as bases para o desenvolvimento de um mercado de carbono florestal de alta qualidade. O aprimoramento contínuo das políticas, o fortalecimento da capacidade organizacional e a garantia da participação da comunidade serão fatores cruciais para maximizar o valor dos recursos florestais e contribuir de forma prática para a mitigação das mudanças climáticas.
