artigo.texto: A corrida pelo avanço dos modelos de inteligência artificial provocou um salto dramático na demanda por recursos hídricos ao redor do mundo. Empreendimentos de grande porte chegam a retirar 5 milhões de galões de água por dia para evitar o superaquecimento de servidores, sobrecarregando o abastecimento público em regiões castigadas pela estiagem. Por que os chips de inteligência artificial exigem tanta água? O processamento ininterrupto de redes neurais profundas exige milhares de placas de processamento gráfico operando em capacidade máxima. Essa densidade de circuitos concentrada em gabinetes fechados gera um volume de calor residual que inviabiliza o uso exclusivo de ventiladores convencionais de ar. Para resfriar essa infraestrutura com baixo custo financeiro, a indústria adota torres de arrefecimento evaporativo. Nesse processo, o calor das máquinas é transferido para a água líquida, que evapora na atmosfera e impede o derretimento dos semicondutores durante as operações de cálculo. Quanto representa o consumo diário de 5 milhões de galões na prática? A retirada contínua de água potável por um único galpão tecnológico altera de forma profunda a disponibilidade hídrica dos municípios vizinhos às centrais de dados. Para mensurar a proporção desse impacto frente ao uso humano e urbano tradicional, examine o comparativo volumétrico estruturado na tabela a seguir: Como a evaporação nas torres sobrecarrega bacias e lençóis freáticos? Ao contrário do uso doméstico, em que a água consumida retorna à rede coletora como esgoto para ser tratado, o resfriamento de computadores consome a água de forma consuntiva definitiva. Cerca de 80% do volume captado se transforma em vapor e se dissipa com as correntes de vento, sem recarregar o rio ou aquífero de origem. Esse esvaziamento silencioso dos mananciais foi detalhado pelo Environmental and Energy Study Institute ao analisar o impacto hídrico de servidores. Em regiões agrícolas de clima semiárido, a captação maciça rebaixa o nível dos poços artesianos e compromete a irrigação de lavouras vizinhas durante o verão. Conflito pelo Acesso à Água A instalação de polos tecnológicos em áreas com risco de seca gera disputas administrativas por outorgas públicas, obrigando prefeituras a escolher entre a atração de investimentos e a segurança de abastecimento da população. Leia também: A ilha brasileira que existe há 435 anos e conquista quem procura uma vida mais tranquila perto do mar Quais alternativas de engenharia reduzem o gasto de água nas instalações? Para mitigar a dependência de reservatórios potáveis e responder a novas exigências regulatórias, projetistas desenvolvem métodos térmicos que operam em circuito fechado ou aproveitam fontes residuais. Entre as principais tecnologias disponíveis para substituir as torres evaporativas convencionais, destacam-se as seguintes frentes: - ❄️ Sistemas em circuito fechado: Radiadores que recirculam o mesmo líquido em tubulações seladas, impedindo a perda de vapor para o ar. - 🔬 Imersão direta em fluido dielétrico: Servidores submersos em óleo mineral sintético que conduz o calor sem contato com água líquida. - 🚰 Água de reuso industrial: Utilização de efluentes sanitários tratados de estações municipais no lugar de água potável encanada. Quais são as principais dúvidas sobre o uso de água na inteligência artificial? O consumo oculto gerado pelo uso de ferramentas digitais no dia a dia levanta questionamentos sobre a pegada ecológica dos servidores. Veja os esclarecimentos a seguir: Perguntas Frequentes Esclareça o impacto ambiental dos centros de dados A expansão da infraestrutura digital global depende da superação do desperdício de água potável no resfriamento mecânico. A adoção de circuitos fechados e o uso de águas residuais tratadas são os caminhos necessários para viabilizar a tecnologia sem esgotar bacias essenciais à sobrevivência das cidades.

A Prefeitura de Campo Grande abriu pregão eletrônico para contratar a locação de uma solução de alta disponibilidade de data center em contêiner, com entrega da estrutura, operação ininterrupta e manutenção integral. O aviso do Pregão Eletrônico nº 186/2026, da Secretaria Especial de Licitações e Contratos (Selc), saiu no Diogrande de segunda-feira (9). As propostas podem ser enviadas até as 7h44 de 25 de novembro, e a disputa de preços começa às 7h45. O contrato, pedido pela Agência Municipal de Tecnologia da Informação e Inovação (Agetec), inclui manutenção preventiva, preditiva e corretiva, fornecimento de peças e insumos e suporte técnico completo. Segundo o aviso, o objetivo é “garantir a estabilidade, segurança e escalabilidade do ambiente tecnológico municipal”. Data center em contêiner é uma estrutura modular que reúne servidores, refrigeração e energia em um módulo montado fora e instalado no local, o que costuma encurtar o prazo de implantação. O aviso não informa o valor estimado da contratação nem por quanto tempo o contrato vai durar. artigo.texto: City of Boise approves emergency moratorium on large data centers Boise, Idaho (CBS2) — The city of Boise has approved an emergency moratorium that temporarily pauses the development of large data centers within city limits. The ordinance, passed Tuesday evening during a city Council meeting, halts new applications for data centers for up to six months. It applies to facilities larger than 100,000 square feet or those with a projected power demand of at least 20 megawatts at full buildout. City leaders said concerns about potential impacts on water resources, energy use and land development led to the decision. They also mentioned the rise of moratoriums across 44 other states. Boise residents weighed in on the proposed moratorium with the majority of feedback in support of the moratorium. “These data centers use a tremendous amount of water and as our state goes through this predicted drought through the winter, i feel it's incredibly important to have guidelines in place before more data centers move in and take up what little resources we have,” Boise resident, Kyle Chandler said during Tuesday meeting. Another Boise resident urged leaders to consider long-term impacts. “We must understand that every decision we make, not only the impact it has on us here and now, but on the next seven generations to come,” the resident said. “I don't hear anybody talking about the future, i hear people trying to make a profit quick and dirty," she said. City leaders said they would take the next months to revise Boise's city code as well as restrictions and guidelines they would want to put in place in regard to large data centers, with public feedback from the community. Council members also discussed the importance of county and state level elected officials dong their part to put those guidelines in place. Council members voted unanimously on the moratorium, and the ordinance is set to go into effect immediately.

artigo.texto: Google Adds TPU 8tx, 8i Max for Enterprise AI Google Cloud is expanding its TPU lineup with one chip for secure AI workloads and another for higher-capacity inference with large context windows. To meet growing demand for AI inference, Google Cloud on Monday beefed up its Tensor Processing Unit family with two new chips: a more secure version of its TPU 8t accelerator and a higher-capacity version of its TPU 8i inference chip. The new processors are designed to address two emerging enterprise requirements: stronger protection for sensitive AI workloads and better performance for agentic AI applications with large context windows, said Mark Lohmeyer, vice president and general manager of AI and computing infrastructure at Google Cloud. The announcements build on Google Cloud’s eighth-generation TPU chips introduced in April. At that time, the company launched TPU 8t for training, which it said delivers up to 2.7 times better training performance than the prior generation, and TPU 8i for inference, which it said offers 80% better inference price-performance. TPU 8tx Adds Security; TPU 8i Max Boosts Capacity One of the new accelerators, TPU 8tx, is built on the same silicon as TPU 8t and adds hardware-level encryption for secure inference and small-scale training. The chip is paired with custom AMD CPU hosts to help protect and isolate sensitive data and model weights, even while inference is actively running, Lohmeyer said during a media briefing. Google Cloud also introduced TPU 8i Max, a variant aimed at enterprises running increasingly agentic workloads with large context windows. Lohmeyer said the chip is intended to address memory constraints by effectively “adding more lanes to the highway.” To create TPU 8i Max, Google Cloud combined two TPU 8i chips into a single package, doubling compute, SRAM, and HBM bandwidth compared with TPU 8i, the company said. TPU 8i Max delivers 384 GB of high-bandwidth memory, Lohmeyer said. “We’re just seeing tremendous demand for the TPU platform and systems,” Lohmeyer said during the briefing. He added that Google Cloud is also seeing a broadening of AI use cases, including demand for confidential computing and for agentic inference with very large context windows while maintaining strong performance. Custom TPUs Could Sharpen Google Cloud’s Edge Dave McCarthy, group vice president at IDC, said Google Cloud’s move toward more specialized custom AI chips could help it further differentiate itself from rival cloud providers. “The fact that Google was able to launch the 8i and 8t earlier this year, and now they’re coming out with these new ones within the same calendar year, is just showing the pace of innovation,” McCarthy said. “They’re showing their commitment to R&D to build this stuff. And if what they’re saying is true – twice the bandwidth, all these new features – that’s showing they’re potentially outpacing the competition in terms of new product releases.” McCarthy described confidential computing as an emerging requirement for AI workloads. Cloud providers have traditionally focused on protecting data in transit and at rest, he said, whereas confidential computing is intended to protect data in use. “If Google can come out with a strong confidential compute story, it kind of gives them a little bit of an edge,” said McCarthy, adding that Nvidia is still developing its strategy in this area. Google Cloud also said TPU 8i Max allows more silicon to fit within an existing rack footprint, enabling significantly more computing power per square foot and per watt in its data centers. That could help Google Cloud increase capacity without adding more racks or building more data centers, at least in the near term, potentially easing some of the capacity pressures facing the industry, McCarthy said. More broadly, McCarthy said Google Cloud’s strategy of continually enhancing its silicon and making TPUs available through other providers could expand the company’s market reach while creating an additional revenue stream. Oracle recently announced it would make TPU chips available to customers of Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. During the media briefing, Lohmeyer also said Google Cloud would allow select customers to deploy the TPU 8tx in their own data centers.

artigo.texto: The Washington County Chamber of Commerce will host its next Eggs and Issues program on Wednesday, December 2, featuring a discussion about the growth of the data center industry and lessons learned in Loudoun County, Virginia. The program, titled “Data Centers: The Loudoun County Experience,” will feature Joe Kroboth, deputy county administrator for Loudoun County. Breakfast will begin at 6:45 a.m., with the program starting at 7:30 a.m. at Hagerstown Community College in Rooms 211 and 213 of the Career Programs Building. Kroboth brings experience from both sides of the regional data center discussion. He spent seven years as public works director in Washington County, Maryland, before serving 14 years as deputy county administrator in Loudoun County, which is widely known as the “Data Center Capital of the World.” Loudoun County was among the first communities in the country to embrace the data center industry. Today, the county has more than 230 data center facilities operating or in development. The industry has brought significant economic benefits to Loudoun County. Data centers account for nearly 40% of the county’s tax base and generate approximately $1.3 billion in annual tax revenue. County officials say the revenue has helped lower property tax rates for residents every year since 2016. However, the growth has also brought challenges, including concerns about noise, backup diesel generators, electric transmission lines and the placement of facilities near residential neighborhoods. Loudoun County is now revisiting some of its land-use regulations and development standards based on lessons learned over the past two decades. Kroboth will share his firsthand perspective on the opportunities and challenges associated with data center development, including what has worked, what has not and what communities should consider before making decisions with long-term consequences. The Chamber says the program is intended to provide community leaders and residents with an opportunity to learn from a county with extensive experience in the industry. The Chamber is not advocating for or against data center development but hopes to provide a balanced discussion as interest in the industry grows in Washington County and the surrounding region. A question-and-answer session will follow Kroboth’s presentation. Registration is available at www.hagerstown.org. The event will be held at Hagerstown Community College, 11400 Robinwood Drive in Hagerstown. Attendees should use Parking Lot F.

artigo.texto: The Oakland City Council voted unanimously to extend the city's current data center moratorium for nearly a year, keeping restrictions in place that were originally set to expire next week. The decision was met with a standing ovation inside City Hall, as council members approved a 10-month extension to give municipal staff more time to study data center development, energy use, and environmental impacts while drafting potential new regulations. Watch NBC Bay Area News free wherever you are "We need more research and that’s what the community asked for. They want to know the risk of water going up and PG&E going up, and they deserve that," said Tonisha Scott, an Oakland resident. Public commenters at the meeting voiced strong concerns regarding transparency and resource consumption. "We pay taxes here! … and whatever goes on in Oakland, we are supposed to know about it!" said one public commenter. City officials plan to host community meetings over the coming months to allow residents to weigh in. "The importance of extending the moratorium is to give the city the adequate amount of time for our staff… to come back to the council with some firm guidelines," said District 3 City Councilmember Carroll Fife. Local While the extension provides a temporary pause, some community advocates view it as a stepping stone toward a permanent ban. "This is really a first step for a lot of the communities…," said Zoe Jonick, an organizer with 350 Bay Area, a climate group that has advocated for similar local moratoriums across the region. "You heard that a lot at the meeting tonight in Oakland… where a lot of people said yes we want this extended 10 more months, but really we want it extended forever," Jonick added. Oakland's original 45-day moratorium was slated to expire on Nov. 20. Tuesday's vote extends the restrictions through Oct. 5 of next year.

artigo.texto: Grupos da América Latina defenderam a criação de regulamentações específicas para definirem o escopo da expansão dos centros de dados (data centers) e garantir proteção às regiões que recebem essas infraestruturas. A demanda foi apresentada durante o segundo seminário realizado pelo Laboratório de Políticas Públicas e Internet (Lapin), que ocorre em Fortaleza, no Brasil. O encontro, com duração de três dias, reúne pesquisadores, jornalistas, ativistas e representantes de comunidades de diferentes países da América Latina para discutir os impactos do rápido crescimento da infraestrutura digital. Um dos principais pontos do debate é a diferença entre a velocidade com que esses projetos avançam e a capacidade das regulamentações existentes de avaliar seus impactos. Os participantes defendem procedimentos de autorização mais rigorosos e transparentes, que garantam a participação das populações afetadas. Segundo eles, sem essas medidas, os custos ambientais e sociais podem recair inteiramente sobre as comunidades locais, enquanto os benefícios ficam concentrados em outras regiões. Entre os principais temas discutidos estão o consumo de água e energia, a transição energética, o racismo ambiental e o chamado "extrativismo digital". Os centros de dados são infraestruturas físicas essenciais para o funcionamento de serviços online e sistemas de inteligência artificial, mas exigem recursos naturais e grandes áreas para sua instalação. Por isso, conforme destacado durante o seminário em Fortaleza, o planejamento desses empreendimentos não deve ser tratado apenas como uma questão tecnológica, mas também ambiental e social. artigo.texto: O primeiro leilão brasileiro de armazenamento em baterias recebeu 6.091 cadastros, um recorde para contratação de projetos no setor elétrico segundo a Empresa de Pesquisa Energética (EPE). Os certames estão marcados para 2 e 4 de dezembro e somam 296.807 megawatts de potência inscrita. O leilão de 2 de dezembro exige componentes nacionais e terá financiamento de R$ 30 bilhões do Banco Nacional de Desenvolvimento Econômico e Social (BNDES) via Finame. A etapa de 4 de dezembro aceita equipamentos importados, mas ainda não tem linha de crédito público definida. A diferença entre as duas datas transforma o certame em disputa de política industrial, não apenas em compra de reserva de capacidade. O banco público cria demanda para fabricação e montagem de baterias, produção de componentes, engenharia e serviços tecnológicos no país, segundo avaliação de Rosana Santos, diretora-executiva do Instituto E+ Transição Energética. A corrida global ajuda a explicar a pressa brasileira em ter capacidade própria de armazenamento. Em 2025, o mundo instalou 108 gigawatts de baterias, alta de 40% sobre 2024 e volume 11 vezes maior que o de 2021, puxado por China, Estados Unidos e Europa, segundo o relatório Global Energy Review 2026 da Agência Internacional de Energia (IEA). No Brasil, as hidrelétricas não suprem sozinhas a flexibilidade operacional que o sistema elétrico ganha com sistemas químicos de armazenamento. Os conjuntos de baterias entram em operação em um a dois anos e descarregam energia em ciclos de quatro a oito horas, enquanto usinas hidrelétricas reversíveis levam de sete a oito anos para ficar prontas. Esses sistemas ajudam a aproveitar o excesso de geração eólica e solar e a reduzir cortes de geração (curtailment) que hoje não são ressarcidos aos produtores. Rodrigo Sauaia, presidente da Associação Brasileira de Energia Solar Fotovoltaica (Absolar), afirma que os geradores deixam de receber pelo que não injetam na rede e enfrentam prejuízos financeiros. A queda internacional dos custos também viabilizou os sistemas de baterias no mercado brasileiro. Desde 2010, o preço médio global caiu de mais de US$ 1.000 por quilowatt-hora para cerca de US$ 108 por quilowatt-hora em 2025, de acordo com levantamento anual da consultoria BloombergNEF. A Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (Aneel) aprovou os editais em 27 de outubro e reduziu o investimento de referência de R$ 9,8 milhões por megawatt para R$ 6 milhões por megawatt. As garantias de proposta e de fiel cumprimento também caíram, o que diminui a barreira de entrada e amplia a competição. Os contratos valem por 15 anos, com início de suprimento em 1º de agosto de 2028. A bateria precisa garantir potência por quatro horas a cada ciclo diário, com receita anual ajustada pelo desempenho efetivo. A Associação Brasileira de Soluções de Armazenamento de Energia (ABSAE) calcula que a rede básica possui cerca de 56 gigawatts de margem de conexão para baterias, com base em nota técnica do Operador Nacional do Sistema Elétrico (ONS) e da EPE. Esse volume supera em até 12 vezes a necessidade estimada para o período de 2028 a 2030. Nos pontos com bônus locacional, a folga chega a 13,7 gigawatts, concentrada principalmente na Bahia, no Piauí, no Ceará e no norte de Minas Gerais. Para a ABSAE, a infraestrutura de transmissão não deve ser gargalo para os primeiros leilões. Os preços-teto ficaram em R$ 1,76 milhão por megawatt-ano no leilão com exigência de conteúdo nacional e R$ 1,58 milhão no certame aberto a importados. A associação considera os valores alinhados às projeções do mercado e suficientes para atrair investidores qualificados. Os 6.091 projetos cadastrados ainda passarão por análise e habilitação técnica conduzida pela EPE antes da disputa. A proporção final entre equipamentos fabricados no país e sistemas importados nos leilões de dezembro definirá o alcance industrial do financiamento público.

artigo.texto: A resistência à instalação de novos data centers, uma infraestrutura que cria poucos empregos e consome energia e água em volumes gigantescos, está a aumentar em todo o mundo. O exemplo mais recente ocorreu na semana passada nas eleições intercalares nos EUA, onde os candidatos com posições contrárias à instalação de data centers somaram vitórias. Nas sondagens realizadas nesse dia, o eleitorado confirmou que a questão foi determinante para o seu sentido de voto. Além dos danos ambientais, as populações queixam-se do aumento dos preços da eletricidade nas zonas onde foram instalados os centros de dados. Nas dezenas de referendos locais realizados no mesmo dia nos EUA, apenas num caso os eleitores deram a vitória à posição da indústria. Estes megacentros de dados são usados para alimentar modelos de inteligência artificial das grandes empresas tecnológicas. A oposição à construção dos grandes data centers alastra à Europa e o governo norueguês deu o exemplo ao anunciar esta segunda-feira a suspensão de novos pedidos de ligação à rede elétrica por parte destes data centers. A Noruega produz hoje mais energia do que a que consome, mas as estimativas apontam para um défice futuro por causa dos data centers, com a consequente subida do preço da eletricidade. O total de pedidos de ligação feitos este ano ascende aos 26 mil megawatts de nova capacidade, o que é mais do que a capacidade instalada na Noruega, com os data centers a representarem 75% dos pedidos, afirmou o ministro da Energia Terje Aasland, citado pela Reuters. A decisão do Governo, anunciada pelo operador da rede elétrica Statnett, foi justificada pelo ministro da Digitalização Torgeir Micaelsen com o objetivo de “obter um maior controlo sobre o crescimento dos centros de dados e garantir que dispomos dos centros de dados de que realmente precisamos”. Ficam assim suspensos temporariamente os novos pedidos de ligação e o futuro regime de licenças irá favorecer data centers que prestem serviços às áreas da defesa, da polícia e da preparação para emergências, aos serviços de saúde e a outras infraestruturas críticas, tais como a rede móvel e o sistema financeiro, afirmou Micaelsen. De fora ou com restrições acrescidas no acesso a terrenos e eletricidade ficarão as grandes empresas que operam as clouds e também as empresas de criptomoedas. E os novos data centers terão de pagar os custos da rede, podendo ser obrigados a construir centrais elétricas a gás, incluindo sistemas de captura e armazenamento de carbono, para produzirem a sua própria eletricidade, afirmou o governo. Também a Dinamarca aprovou no mês passado no Parlamento uma lei que empurra os data centers para o fim da fila de prioridades no que toca ao acesso à rede elétrica, atrás dos serviços de saúde e segurança, da rede de carregamento de carros elétricos e das habitações.

artigo.texto: Iniciativa transforma benefícios ambientais da reciclagem em créditos de carbono e gera renda para cooperativas de catadores; projeto será apresentado em painéis sobre sustentabilidade e justiça climática na Turquia O Ministério Público de Mato Grosso do Sul (MPMS) levará à 31ª Conferência das Nações Unidas sobre Mudanças Climáticas (COP31) uma experiência que une reciclagem, geração de créditos de carbono e inclusão social. O Projeto Reciclarbono, apoiado pela instituição e finalista dos Prêmios CNMP 2026 e J.Ex., estará entre as iniciativas brasileiras apresentadas nos debates sobre soluções ambientais. A conferência será realizada em Antália, na Turquia. O MPMS será representado pelo promotor de Justiça Luciano Furtado Loubet, integrante do Núcleo Ambiental da instituição e presidente da Associação Brasileira dos Membros do Ministério Público de Meio Ambiente (Abrampa). Loubet foi convidado a compartilhar experiências desenvolvidas no Brasil em painéis sobre gestão de resíduos, economia circular, cidades sustentáveis e justiça climática. Entre os destaques está o debate internacional “The Informal Sector Enabling Climate Action”, promovido pela Zero Waste Foundation e pelo Climate High-Level Champions’ Office. A Abrampa participará como palestrante na Zona Azul da COP31, área destinada às negociações e aos eventos oficiais da conferência. Projeto transforma reciclagem em créditos de carbono Desenvolvido em parceria com instituições públicas e acadêmicas, o Reciclarbono transforma os benefícios ambientais gerados pela reciclagem em créditos de carbono. O valor obtido é convertido em renda para cooperativas e associações de catadores. A iniciativa busca associar a redução dos impactos ambientais à valorização dos trabalhadores da reciclagem, aproximando a economia circular das estratégias de enfrentamento às mudanças climáticas. Debates incluem gestão de resíduos e cidades sustentáveis A programação da COP31 também prevê discussões sobre encerramento de lixões, combate à poluição marinha, economia circular de baixo carbono e gestão de resíduos sólidos. Os painéis incluem ainda experiências municipais para a construção de cidades sustentáveis e temas relacionados à segurança jurídica de políticas climáticas. A participação do MPMS e da Abrampa amplia a presença de experiências brasileiras nos debates internacionais sobre sustentabilidade, inclusão social e políticas públicas ambientais, levando iniciativas acompanhadas em Mato Grosso do Sul para a discussão global sobre mudanças climáticas. artigo.texto: Woodbury County Zoning Commission hears data center concerns in Salix SALIX, Iowa (KTIV) - Woodbury County Zoning Commission continued their tour of Woodbury County, Monday Nov. 9, this time in Salix for one of their data center town halls. Back in June, the Woodbury County Board of Supervisors passed a 12-month moratorium on all potential data centers in the county. And now, the county’s zoning commission is looking for public input on what requirements or regulations they would like to see added to a county data center ordinance. That ordinance would only affect unincorporated areas in the county not incorporated cities or towns. Monday, the commission heard from residents in Salix. There, people voiced their concerns about data centers affecting the environment, water quality, local roads, and noise pollution. Overall, many asked the commission to take their time to creating regulations. “To my mind, the costs and risks far outweigh the benefits. While we do not want woodbury county closed to business the goal would be to ensure that if a hyper scale data center were to be proposed in this county, its residents would be protected from harm,” said Janet Yanek, a concerned resident. Some residents did acknowledge that they aren’t fully against data centers, they just ask the county to have enough regulations in place so they don’t impact residents. “I don’t think there’s anything wrong with data centers if they are in the right spot. I think that resources are a big thing to look at and keeping the costs on the companies that are building them is also a big thing to look at. But keeping the residents first is the biggest things in my eyes,” said Preston Zemanek, a concerned resident. The zoning commission plans to hold another town hall in Correctionville on January 18th. That location has yet to be determined. If you are a resident of Woodbury County and would like to submit your input, you can email dpriestley@woodburycountyiowa.gov or reach out to the Woodbury County Planning and Zoning at 620 Douglas Street, Sixth Floor, Sioux City, IA 51101. artigo.texto: Eletronet aporta R$ 25 milhões em novo Data Center em SP Nomeado ELET1, o Data Center terá capacidade para cerca de 90 racks e potência de 0,5 MW, podendo ser expandida para 1 MW. Lançamento é previsto para o primeiro trimestre de 2027. A Eletronet, uma empresa Axia Energia, anunciou o ELET1, seu novo Data Center em São Paulo, que ampliará a oferta de serviços de colocation, conectividade e interconexão da companhia e fornecerá mais escala ao atendimento de provedores de nuvem, operadoras de telecomunicações e provedores de Internet (ISPs), e hyperscalers. Com investimento de R$ 25 milhões, o centro terá aproximadamente 350 m², capacidade para cerca de 90 racks e potência inicial de 0,5 MW, podendo chegar a 1 MW na segunda fase de expansão. Com as obras já iniciadas, a previsão de lançamento é para o primeiro trimestre de 2027. O projeto acompanha o aumento da procura de empresas dos segmentos de cloud, streaming e telecomunicações por infraestrutura de Data Center em regiões estratégicas de São Paulo, com alta disponibilidade e acesso a um amplo ecossistema de conteúdo. O ELET1 estará em uma localização com elevada concentração de redes de telecomunicações e provedores de conteúdo. O Data Center também abrigará o PIX (Ponto de Interconexão) da Eletronet no IX.br São Paulo, o maior ponto de troca de tráfego de Internet do mundo, tanto em volume quanto em número de participantes. O PIX da companhia se destaca por liderar o volume de tráfego de download entre as operadoras participantes do IX.br São Paulo. Para os clientes, estar nesse ambiente aumenta as possibilidades de conexão com diferentes redes e provedores de serviços digitais. “O ELET1 representa um passo estratégico para fortalecer nossa atuação no segmento de Data Centers. Estamos ampliando nossa estrutura para atender às necessidades dos clientes que já utilizam nossos serviços e abrir novas oportunidades de negócios, em um contexto no qual a hiperconectividade e a disponibilidade se tornam cada vez mais essenciais”, afirma Rogerio Garchet, CEO da Eletronet. Segundo ele, o projeto acompanha o avanço de aplicações em nuvem, inteligência artificial, streaming e serviços digitais, que exigem suporte para volumes cada vez maiores de dados. “Queremos ir além das necessidades atuais e antecipar os próximos ciclos do mercado, fortalecendo nossa capacidade de conectar clientes, redes e ecossistemas digitais”, diz. Com segurança, tecnologia de última geração e resiliência operacional entre os pilares da iniciativa, o ELET1 seguirá as melhores práticas globais de infraestrutura, com soluções voltadas à proteção física e lógica, alinhadas às diretrizes da norma ISO 27001. O Data Center também contará com aplicações modernas e práticas de gestão ambiental e energética, tendo como referência os padrões ISO 14001, ISO 50001 e LEED, apoiando no melhor desempenho energético e na redução do PUE (Power Usage Effectiveness). Entre os recursos previstos estão dois geradores redundantes de 500 kVA, dupla entrada de rede, backbone DWDM protegido, sistema de gerenciamento predial (BMS) atualizado, monitoramento contínuo e um Centro de Operações de Rede (NOC) de contingência.

artigo.texto: NYSERDA Awards Nearly $13 Million to 15 Innovative Energy Storage Projects New York's NYSERDA is distributing nearly $13 million across 15 long duration and advanced battery storage projects, from compressed air to sodium-ion, with grid-scale demonstrations among the goals. The New York State Energy Research and Development Authority (NYSERDA) announced on November 6, 2026 that nearly $13 million has been awarded to 15 projects. The funds come from the Power Generation and Storage Innovation program. They support product development and demonstration of battery storage solutions, including long duration systems. Storage is drawing funding in other markets, as shown by India's approval of a 92 GWh storage program and Anchor Energy Partners' â¬75 million target for its first storage fund. A program focused on alternatives to lithium-ion The program competitively awards funding to long duration energy storage (LDES) projects and other under-utilized alternatives to traditional lithium-ion batteries that have yet to be commercialized. The selected solutions include new designs with a duration of more than 10 hours at rated power. According to NYSERDA, they target grid congestion, hosting capacity constraints and lithium-ion siting limitations. Doreen M. Harris, president and CEO of NYSERDA, says investing in next-generation energy storage technologies is critical to building a flexible and resilient grid. In her view, the projects would advance solutions able to deliver power when it is needed most and help lower costs. The agency highlights three focus areas: enhanced inherent design safety, material innovations for more efficient and longer-lasting battery cells, and diversified battery material composition to improve safety and local supply chains. From compressed air to sodium-ion Aestus Energy Storage LLC receives over $590,000 for a subscale test of approximately 35 kilowatt-hours (kWh) of two alumina-silica ceramic heat sink materials. The materials are intended for the design of a 20 megawatt-hour (MWh) Advanced Compressed Air Energy Storage (A-CAES) system for utility-scale applications. Alsym Energy, Inc. gets over $290,000 to design and test a 10 kWh prototype non-flammable sodium-ion battery energy storage system, in partnership with the Rochester Institute of Technology's Battery Development Center. AlphaEn Corporation receives over $350,000 for a modular, roll-to-roll lithium metal electrode manufacturing platform that uses recycled lithium from retired assets. Daqus Energy, Inc. is awarded nearly $1 million for a completely metal-free organic cathode for lithium-ion batteries, in partnership with Binghamton University's Northeast Center for Chemical Energy Storage. Graphenix Development (GDI) receives over $700,000 to combine 100% silicon anodes with sulfur cathodes. IBEX Materials Inc. gets $750,000 for a silicon-rich, graphite-free anode integrated with solid-state electrolytes. InfinitEnergy, Inc. is awarded $250,000 for solid-state batteries designed to operate without external mechanical pressure. Inlyte and Sprocket receive the largest amounts Inlyte Energy receives over $2.4 million, the largest amount among the winners listed. The funding is meant to deploy an iron-sodium battery of more than 10 hours to address substation peak load growth and distribution-level resilience challenges. Sprocket Power, Inc. gets over $1 million to demonstrate direct current fast charging stations fed from an underground Vanadium Redox Flow Battery. LiBAMA Power Corporation receives over $400,000 to develop and test advanced metal anodes with Elementium, a nonflammable electrolyte supplier. LiNova Energy, Inc. gets nearly $720,000 for a lithium-ion battery with critical-mineral-free polymer cathodes. Orion Polymer Corp. is awarded $250,000 to demonstrate the technical viability of its membranes for lithium sulfur batteries through a prototype pouch cell. Respire Energy, Inc. receives over $850,000 to further develop its metal-air battery with Binghamton University, Intertek and Bettergy Corp. - Gas42.5 % - Nuclear17.2 % - Coal14.2 % - Wind10.3 % - Solar10.1 % - Hydro3.9 % - Bioenergy1.0 % - Other fossil0.5 % - Other renewables0.4 %

artigo.texto: As ações da AAON Inc (NASDAQ:AAON) subiram aproximadamente 22% nas negociações pré-mercado de terça-feira, após a fabricante de equipamentos de aquecimento, ventilação e ar condicionado (HVAC) divulgar resultados do terceiro trimestre e receita acima das expectativas dos analistas, além de elevar sua projeção financeira para o ano de 2026. A empresa reportou lucro ajustado de US$ 0,83 por ação, superando a estimativa de consenso dos analistas de US$ 0,56 em US$ 0,27. A receita trimestral aumentou 84,1% em relação ao ano anterior, atingindo o recorde de US$ 707,4 milhões, comparada a US$ 384,2 milhões no mesmo período de 2025 e às expectativas dos analistas de US$ 599,7 milhões. O aumento da receita refletiu a demanda pelas linhas de produtos AAON e BASX da empresa, maior produção e maior utilização da capacidade produtiva recentemente ampliada. A receita do terceiro trimestre subiu 84,1%, atingindo o recorde de US$ 707,4 milhões A AAON reportou vendas líquidas de US$ 707,4 milhões no terceiro trimestre, representando um aumento de US$ 323,2 milhões em relação ao mesmo período do ano anterior. O resultado superou a estimativa consensual dos analistas em aproximadamente US$ 107,7 milhões. O lucro ajustado por ação atingiu US$ 0,83, em comparação com as expectativas do mercado de US$ 0,56, refletindo a maior receita e o melhor desempenho operacional da empresa durante o trimestre. O lucro bruto aumentou 76,4%, atingindo US$ 188,5 milhões, enquanto a margem bruta alcançou 26,7%, uma melhoria de 60 pontos base em comparação com o segundo trimestre. O lucro operacional mais que dobrou, aumentando 129,3% para US$ 100 milhões. A empresa atribuiu os resultados ao aumento da produção, às medidas de precificação e à maior utilização de suas instalações fabris. A receita da BASX aumentou 218,3%, impulsionada pela demanda por data centers A AAON registrou crescimento de receita em ambas as suas principais marcas de produtos. As vendas de produtos da marca AAON aumentaram 19,6%, atingindo US$ 310,2 milhões, enquanto a receita da marca BASX subiu 218,3%, para US$ 397,2 milhões. O aumento na receita da BASX refletiu a demanda por equipamentos de refrigeração e controle ambiental utilizados em centros de dados, incluindo instalações operadas por grandes provedores de computação em nuvem. A expansão da capacidade de produção da empresa também contribuiu para sua capacidade de atender a pedidos adicionais de clientes durante o trimestre. Os analistas da William Blair destacaram o desempenho da unidade de negócios BASX, observando que os pedidos aceleraram durante o terceiro trimestre. Os analistas disseram que as encomendas do quarto trimestre deveriam “igualar ou superar” o “resultado excepcionalmente forte de 586 milhões de dólares do ano anterior”. Segundo sua avaliação, a demanda foi sustentada por pedidos repetidos de clientes de computação em hiperescala e pela adição de novos clientes. AAON eleva sua previsão de crescimento de vendas para 2026 para 72% a 75% Após a divulgação dos resultados trimestrais, a AAON aumentou sua previsão de crescimento das vendas líquidas para o ano de 2026 para entre 72% e 75%, em comparação com a previsão anterior de 55% a 60%. O ponto médio da faixa revisada é de 73,5%, representando um aumento de 16 pontos percentuais em relação ao ponto médio da previsão anterior. A empresa também atualizou suas expectativas de rentabilidade e despesas operacionais. A AAON agora prevê uma margem bruta anual de aproximadamente 26%, em comparação com a projeção anterior de 25% a 26%. Prevê-se que as despesas com vendas, gerais e administrativas representem aproximadamente 13% das vendas, em comparação com a previsão anterior de 13% a 14%. A revisão das perspectivas reflete as expectativas da administração em relação à atividade de produção, à demanda por produtos e aos custos operacionais durante o restante do ano. Analistas destacam o crescimento dos pedidos e a melhoria das margens Analistas da William Blair afirmaram que a AAON “superou dois obstáculos importantes” com seu relatório financeiro do terceiro trimestre. O primeiro fator foi uma aceleração nos pedidos da BASX, impulsionada pela demanda de operadores de data centers e por novos relacionamentos com clientes. O segundo fator foi a melhoria na margem bruta, que os analistas atribuíram a ações de precificação e maiores volumes de produção. A empresa indicou que as ações da AAON poderiam atingir US$ 100 sob uma estrutura de avaliação que aplica 18 vezes o EBITDA projetado para 2027 ao negócio da marca AAON e de 10 a 11 vezes o EBITDA estimado para 2027 da BASX. A avaliação representa a análise dos analistas, e não uma previsão da empresa ou um preço futuro garantido das ações. A William Blair também identificou uma melhoria adicional na margem bruta em 2027 como um “fator essencial para a criação de mais valor”. Os comentários refletem as expectativas da empresa em relação ao desempenho operacional futuro da companhia e à contribuição de suas duas principais linhas de produtos. AAON reformula resultados do primeiro semestre após identificação de erros contábeis Juntamente com os resultados do terceiro trimestre, a AAON divulgou que identificou erros em suas demonstrações financeiras referentes ao primeiro e segundo trimestres de 2026. Os erros foram descobertos durante a preparação do relatório financeiro do terceiro trimestre da empresa. Como resultado, a AAON revisou seus resultados financeiros do primeiro semestre, aumentando as vendas líquidas anteriormente divulgadas em US$ 10,7 milhões e o lucro diluído por ação em US$ 0,09. A empresa também identificou uma deficiência material em seu controle interno sobre os relatórios financeiros. A AAON afirmou estar implementando medidas destinadas a corrigir as deficiências de controle identificadas. artigo.texto: Missoula company CubCloud AI has sued the city of Missoula over a recent zoning change that blocks data center development within the city limits, citing the state’s Right to Compute Act. The company, represented by the Arizona-based Goldwater Institute through the Big Sky Legal Project, argues in the lawsuit filed Nov. 4 that the city’s rules preventing it from expanding its business are not supported by a “compelling governmental interest,” nor are they narrowly tailored as required by the Right to Compute Act. “The City’s new ordinance targets data centers because it considers them the wrong type of business,” said the Goldwater Institute’s Dave Roland in a press release. “The fact that the ordinance’s blanket restrictions sweep in CubCloud shows they are not narrowly tailored toward protecting the public from excessive noise, light, pollution, etc., as the Right to Compute Act requires.” Missoula City Attorney Ryan Sudbury told Montana Free Press that, as of Monday morning, the city had not been served with the lawsuit but that he was aware of the case. Sudbury said city officials had internal discussions about the Right to Compute Act while crafting the zoning amendment and that the city plans to defend the change. “Nobody knows what the law is intended to do or what it means,” Sudbury said. “It has not been tested in court. … If we get served, we will defend the city’s action.” The Montana Legislature passed the Right to Compute Act in 2025. The law links the development of computational resources, such as data centers, to constitutional rights, including property and freedom of expression. As with other constitutional rights, government infringement of the right to compute is limited except when driven by a compelling governmental interest, such as the preservation of public health and safety. While some local governments have argued the law prevents them from regulating data centers, others, including Missoula County, have moved forward with crafting new rules. Large data center proposals have received significant pushback from residents. Missoula County’s recently released data center study found even small-scale operations can have some significant impacts on energy demand, water use and air and water pollution. The city adopted a new zoning code in late 2025 that went into effect earlier this year. While the new code allowed data centers in heavy industrial areas — which are not included on the zoning map — the rules inadvertently permitted data centers citywide if they took up less than 50% of a facility. The amendment approved in October closed that loophole by revising the definition of a data center and regulating the facilities based on how the equipment is used rather than how much floor space it occupies. CubCloud AI was founded about a year ago and has 18 employees, according to the complaint. The business provides private computational resources, remote data processing, server hosting and cloud computing services. CubCloud operates a facility on Kestrel Drive near the Missoula Montana Airport that previously met the city’s requirements because the computational resources occupied about 20% of the floor area, the complaint said. Joshua Rhines, CubCloud CEO, planned to build a new stand-alone building on the site that would house additional computing resources. Under the city’s updated rules, the business could not build similar facilities on its existing site or anywhere else within city limits. The complaint argues the facilities do not generate noise, odors, physical intrusions or other adverse conditions that would constitute a nuisance or unreasonably interfere with neighboring properties. The complaint argues the zoning amendment violates the Right to Compute Act by restricting the company’s ability to own or use computational resources and is not supported by a compelling government interest. Even if a compelling government interest was identified, the rule is not narrowly tailored to fulfill that interest, the complaint states. RELATED How Montana’s ‘Right to Compute Act’ stymies data center regulation While the goals of public pushback against data center development are clear, a 2025 state law — the Right to Compute Act — has effectively tied the hands of county commissioners whose constituents are pushing for regulation. “We are between a rock and a hard spot right now,” Yellowstone County Commission Chair Mark Morse said in a September interview. “We don’t know what we have the power to do.” Rhines and CubCloud request the court declare the city rule violates the Right to Compute Act and enjoin the city from enforcing it. “A victory in this case will affirm that free expression and property rights apply just as vigorously to modern digital infrastructure as they do to printing presses and traditional brick-and-mortar commerce,” said Roland, with Goldwater Institute, in the press release. The Goldwater Institute is a public policy research and litigation organization focused on limited government, individual liberty and free speech, according to its website. The organization has partnered with the Montana-based Frontier Institute, a conservative think tank, on the Big Sky Legal Project to provide free legal services to Montanans “whose rights are being violated by federal, state, or local government.” Missoula City Council Member Kristen Jordan argued last month that the zoning code is insufficient to prevent data center development, which could be approved through a rezoning request. artigo.texto: The project will help to support Meta's Eagle Mountain data centre operations, as well as supporting grid reliability in Utah. It consists of a standalone, four-hour lithium-iron-phosphate (LFP) battery system and delivers 600 MWh of contracted storage capacity to PacifiCorp under a long-term energy storage agreement. It is situated on an approximately eight-acre site adjacent to the 525 MW Faraday solar facility and shares that facility's substation and interconnection, allowing Lydian to add storage using existing infrastructure. Lydian took Faraday BESS from mobilisation to commercial operation in approximately 10 months. “Faraday BESS shows what a mature platform like Lydian's can deliver” said Kim Smith, Chief Operating Officer of Lydian. “Bringing it online on an extremely tight timeline took close coordination across our own team and our supply chain, construction, and financing partners, from acquisition through commissioning. When a wildfire threatened the area in June, our team put safety first while keeping the project on track. Faraday BESS enhances PacifiCorp’s reliable, contracted capacity for Utah customers.” The completion of Faraday BESS draws on Lydian's integrated platform, which spans development, capital markets, and project delivery. Lydian is also developing Faraday BESS 2 at the Utah site, which would add up to 375 MW/1,500 MWh of storage with a targeted in-service date of the fourth quarter of 2028. artigo.texto: BHP World's largest miner by market cap A new report from DLA Piper indicates that price volatility in critical minerals is holding back a significant share of energy storage projects, according to Mining.com. The study, based on interviews with 550 participants across the energy storage, investment and mining sectors, found that 23% said projects that had appeared viable were deferred or cancelled because of unpredictable commodity prices shaped by tariffs, wars and other geopolitical tensions. A further 12% of respondents described price volatility as a dealbreaker for project development. DLA Piper natural resources partner Alex Jones said unpredictable pricing pressures were producing a cascading effect across the sector, weakening investor confidence, limiting financing and structuring, and contributing to delays, repricing and, in some cases, abandoned projects. The report identifies the reluctance to commit capital amid uncertain and volatile future commodity prices as the leading obstacle to investment. More than half of respondents called price volatility a major constraint on mining or processing investment, with consequences felt across the project lifecycle. Among them, 28% reported difficulty securing bankable long-term offtake agreements, 27% had postponed investment decisions and 26% faced a higher cost of capital. The impact varies by region. Participants in the United Kingdom and the United States reported the strongest effects, with 16% and 18% respectively calling volatility a dealbreaker for project development. German participants stood apart, being the only group to say volatility was not a dealbreaker, with just 8% treating it as a major problem. Australian participants viewed volatility as one of several material considerations rather than a major roadblock. DLA Piper partner Oliver Wright suggested that capital is likely to concentrate in regions seen as offering execution credibility and proximity to supply chains and demand, as developers seek locations where they can exercise more control and stay closer to the supply chain through market cycles. Companies are increasingly adopting vertical integration to limit exposure to volatile commodity markets and to pricing benchmarks influenced by China, the report found. At least 37% of surveyed developers and 32% of mining and raw materials producers have taken this route, which lets businesses control more stages of production, from extraction and refining to manufacturing and recycling. Wright said companies had long depended on supply chains they did not control, and that recent volatility had demonstrated how quickly pricing and supply terms can change. He said developers and miners are now working to hold the parts of the chain they rely on most, from mine through refinery to recycling plant, so that an upstream squeeze no longer disrupts operations. Participants are also reconsidering how prices are set. Some 37% believe component-linked pricing would work better than raw material spot prices, while 48% of mining and raw materials producers favor long-term fixed pricing with periodic resets. Rare Earth Americas chief executive and president Donald S. Swartz II said in the report that strategic mineral supply chains carry value beyond the daily spot price. Wright added that the industry is expected to shift what contracts are priced against, whether component-linked pricing, price floors or hybrid structures. artigo.texto: At a consultation workshop held on November 10, the Carbon Market Division under the Department of Climate Change (the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment) provided updates on key proposed regulations. Regarding climate change adaptation, the draft mandates announcing climate change scenarios every five years. These scenarios will serve as the foundation for impact assessments and risk identification across development strategies and plans. Ministries, sectors, and localities will assess losses and damages while developing tailored adaptation solutions. The draft also introduces a monitoring framework linking implementation results with investment resources and management responsibilities, prioritizing water security, food security, ecosystems, and key infrastructure. For greenhouse gas emission management, facilities emitting 3,000 tons of CO2 equivalent or more annually must conduct inventories. Select facilities in energy, transport, industrial, commercial, and waste treatment sectors will also fall under this mandate based on specific technical thresholds. The draft adds a Measurement, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) mechanism based on national standards to ensure accurate and verifiable data, which is essential for allocating quotas and facilitating carbon market transactions. Quota allocation for applicable facilities will continue through the 2027-2028 period under the proposed roadmap. Starting in 2029, an auction mechanism will supplement standard allocation methods. According to the Department of Climate Change, auctions aim to enhance transparency while encouraging businesses to adopt clean technologies and improve energy efficiency. The draft includes market stabilization measures for instances of abnormal price fluctuations or severe supply imbalances. Solutions include adjusting the timing and volume of auctioned quotas, utilizing reserve quotas, and enhancing transaction monitoring. Establishing national carbon credit standards will ensure emission reduction results are verifiable and prevent double-counting. At the workshop, Deputy Minister of Agriculture and Environment Le Trong Yen highlighted Conclusion 75-KL/TW dated July 28, 2026, issued by the 14th Central Party Committee, as a key political basis for perfecting environmental protection laws. The goal is building a modern governance system supporting a green and circular economy targeting net-zero emissions by 2050. On decentralization, the draft proposes that sectoral management ministries monitor Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs). Localities will directly issue and update the list of facilities subject to greenhouse gas inventories, replacing the current role of the Prime Minister. Delegates also discussed the pilot quota allocation for thermal power, steel, and cement plants, where inconsistent input data previously created challenges. A representative from the Ministry of Industry and Trade stressed evaluating pilot outcomes and completing database systems. A representative from the Energy and Environment Consulting Joint Stock Company recommended requiring independent verification only for facilities participating directly in the quota system to reduce compliance costs for businesses. In response, the drafting committee stated it would adjust regulations to exempt non-quota facilities from mandatory independent verification. The Department of Climate Change will coordinate with the Ministry of Industry and Trade to refine calculation methods and review regulations on carbon credit standards to align with international commitments and domestic operating conditions.

artigo.texto: The CRU published a decision on the initial procurement of Long Duration Energy Storage (“LDES”): Long Duration Energy Storage Decision Paper. This follows an earlier consultation, which we looked at in our insights blog post: Energy update: Long Duration Energy Storage. The CRU now approves the core framework for the initial procurement of up to 500 MW through a technology-neutral, service-based procurement, progressed through the ECP connection process (for more detail, see our briefing: New Connection Policy for Onshore Generators and Storage). EirGrid proposes a two-stage procurement: qualification followed by a tender phase. Which projects can participate? To qualify, projects must have: - a minimum four hours’ import and export duration on the transmission system, - a 1:1 ratio of maximum export capacity (“MEC”) to maximum import capacity, - a minimum capacity of 20 MW for hybrid projects or 75 MW for standalone projects, - a maximum capacity of 100 MW, and - round-trip efficiency of at least 75%. At qualification stage, projects must hold a connection offer at 110 kV or above. At tender stage, projects must have a connection agreement, planning consent for the facility and grid connection, evidence of land rights for the grid connection, maps and AutoCAD drawings of the grid infrastructure, and a detailed connection programme. Co-located sites must have at least 30 MW of TSO-connected renewable generation, with separate market registration and sub-metering. How will projects be selected? At qualification stage, company and project requirements will be assessed on a pass/fail basis. Company requirements include financial turnover (to be confirmed through further consultation), relevant experience and cyber-security requirements. Qualifying tenders will be scored on cost (50%), impact (30%) and connection method (20%). - Impact scoring evaluates a project’s ability to reduce renewable dispatch down and remain available to provide wider system value, using data from hourly ECP modelling. - Connection method scoring is intended to incentivise efficient use of grid. EirGrid’s proposal is that new standalone transmission connections will receive zero points, while the maximum of 20 points will be given to existing standalone connections at tender closing date or to hybrid connection arrangements (with at least 30 MW of renewable generation). EirGrid does not propose MEC sharing for this initial procurement, considering it infeasible within the required timeframe. We touch on some of the issues in our insights blog post: Energy Update: Sharing Maximum Export Capacity at electricity grid connection points. Highest-ranked projects will progress to a Best and Final Offer stage and a Deliverability Assessment, aspects of which are to be further consulted upon. What revenue support will be available? Service duration will be ten years. The CRU has approved in principle a competitively bid revenue floor, subject to an LCOS-informed bid limit. EirGrid proposes that the floor be set on a pay-as-bid basis and remain fixed over the contract term, subject to indexation, with a true-up payment where eligible market revenues fall below it. The storage asset will retain 70% of revenues above the floor, with 30% shared with consumers. EirGrid proposes returning the consumer share through transmission use-of-system charges. The cost of electricity bought for charging (and therefore the round-trip efficiency losses) will be netted off against gross eligible market revenues, but the asset’s other operating, commercial and financing costs will not be deducted. Open-book accounting will be required. EirGrid proposes quarterly interim settlements and annual reconciliation. Full approval of this framework remains subject to EirGrid demonstrating its effective interaction with other mechanisms, as noted further below. How will assets operate? Contracted assets will retain full SEM market access, subject to Trading Envelope compliance. The CRU supports the Trading Envelope model in principle and has approved initial issuance of dynamic import/export limits at 10:00 on the day before the Trading Day. EirGrid must publish a Trading Envelope methodology in advance of the tender and house the methodology and issuance timing in a protocol document so that any material changes are subject to public consultation and CRU approval. The CRU supports in principle non-compliance charges (for taking positions outside a Trading Envelope) and a Trading Non-Activity Scalar (which would reduce the floor for insufficient participation or cycling). Methodologies remain to be consulted on, including treatment of inactivity caused by TSO instructions or Trading Envelope limits. Next steps Many of the revenue and operational design features are subject to final approval by the CRU following demonstration by EirGrid that these mechanisms operate together as a coherent and financeable package providing effective incentives for assets to operate and deliver system value. Before tenders are invited, EirGrid must consult on and finalise the Trading Envelope methodology, Trading Non-Activity Scalar, Deliverability Assessment methodology, contractual arrangements and governance and change-control provisions. The consultation on contractual arrangements is to include timelines. Before contracts are awarded, EirGrid is required to notify the CRU of the proposed selected portfolio, aggregate volume and expected costs.

artigo.texto: Uma falha de partida pode custar à frota mais do que a substituição de uma bateria. O veículo que deixa de sair pode exigir socorro, reprogramação de entregas ou reorganização de viagens. Com mais equipamentos elétricos e eletrônicos a bordo de caminhões e ônibus, escolher a bateria exige considerar não […] 11 de novembro de 2026, às 13:27 Uma falha de partida pode custar à frota mais do que a substituição de uma bateria. O veículo que deixa de sair pode exigir socorro, reprogramação de entregas ou reorganização de viagens. Com mais equipamentos elétricos e eletrônicos a bordo de caminhões e ônibus, escolher a bateria exige considerar não apenas a partida, mas também o consumo ao longo da operação e o tempo disponível para recarga. Na Fenatran 2026, a Moura apresenta suas tecnologias para atender a diferentes perfis de uso no transporte pesado e responder aos novos desafios das frotas cada vez mais eletrônicas. “Um caminhão não deixa de consumir energia quando o motor é desligado. Dependendo dos equipamentos em uso, a bateria continua trabalhando durante o descanso do motorista e precisa manter reserva para a próxima partida. Para o gestor de frota, a pergunta não é apenas qual bateria cabe no veículo, mas qual atende à sua rotina de consumo e recarga”, afirma Felipe Godoy, diretor de Negócios Corporativos e Novos Mercados da Rede Moura. Nos caminhões de longa distância, geladeiras, iluminação e equipamentos eletrônicos podem permanecer ligados durante os períodos de descanso. Nessas condições, o desafio é conciliar o consumo com o motor desligado, a reserva necessária para a partida e a recuperação da carga quando o veículo volta à operação. Nos ônibus, as exigências variam conforme o serviço. Transporte urbano, rodoviário e fretamento têm diferentes rotinas de funcionamento, períodos de espera e equipamentos de bilhetagem, monitoramento e conforto. Por isso, a escolha da bateria precisa considerar quais sistemas ela alimenta, por quanto tempo e em quais condições de recarga. EFB: tecnologia para operações mais exigentes A EFB, sigla de Enhanced Flooded Battery, utiliza uma construção inundada aprimorada para suportar ciclos de descarga e recarga mais exigentes. A tecnologia foi desenvolvida para aplicações que demandam maior robustez energética e desempenho em condições operacionais mais severas. No mercado de reposição, a tecnologia EFB vem ganhando espaço em aplicações que exigem maior disponibilidade operacional e desempenho energético. A Moura EFB 225 é a primeira tecnologia do tipo 100% nacional, desenvolvida para caminhões e veículos comerciais, garantindo maior capacidade e durabilidade para operações que exigem robustez e confiabilidade energética. O impacto da parada vai além da manutenção Quando a falta de energia impede a partida, os efeitos podem alcançar toda a programação do veículo. Além de diagnóstico, atendimento e eventual substituição da bateria, a ocorrência pode exigir remanejamento de veículos, alterar horários e comprometer entregas ou viagens. A indicação depende das especificações do veículo e das condições de trabalho. Além da capacidade nominal, a avaliação deve considerar a frequência e a intensidade das descargas, as oportunidades de recarga, a resistência à vibração e os requisitos de partida. “A bateria precisa ser avaliada pelo que entrega à operação. A especificação correta deve caminhar com a verificação do sistema elétrico e com a manutenção. É esse conjunto que ajuda a enfrentar os riscos, que podem ganhar escala rapidamente, decorrentes de uma parada”, acrescenta Godoy. artigo.texto: Home › Energy Storage ›Tata Power Deploys 60 MWh BESS Across Three Locations in Mumbai Tata Power Deploys 60 MWh BESS Across Three Locations in Mumbai Tata Power has operationalised 60 MWh of BESS across Mahalaxmi, Saki and Mankhurd in Mumbai, with the installations serving a distribution network covering over 8 lakh consumers and supporting peak demand management. November 10, 2026. By Mrinmoy Dey Tata Power has operationalised 60 MWh of battery energy storage systems (BESS) across Mahalaxmi, Saki and Mankhurd to strengthen Mumbai’s electricity distribution network, which serves over 8 lakh consumers. The installations store electricity during lower-cost solar generation hours and discharge it during evening peak demand, helping optimise power procurement costs, improve energy utilisation and reduce dependence on expensive peak-hour electricity, the company stated. Equipped with fast-response and high ramp-rate capabilities, the systems support dynamic load management and enable the distribution network to respond to fluctuations in demand. Operating at approximately 1–1.5 cycles per day, the installations also support peak load management and power procurement optimisation. The decentralised, grid-connected systems provide localised energy storage and dispatch capabilities, while their black-start functionality supports grid restoration during power system disturbances. The operational capacity forms part of Tata Power’s larger plan to modernise Mumbai’s electricity infrastructure. In April 2025, the company received approval from the Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory Commission (MERC) to deploy 200 MWh of BESS across 10 strategic locations in the city. The larger deployment is aimed at strengthening grid stability, managing peak demand, improving reactive power management and supporting faster restoration of electricity supply to critical infrastructure, including hospitals, Metro services, airports and data centres, the company stated. artigo.texto: Last week, Ohio had more data center-related measures on the ballot than any other state, and voters from Piqua to Grove City, Conneaut to Urbana, overwhelmingly voted to restrict the hyperscale developments. Barry Blankenship started leading a data center resistance group in Trenton in southwest Ohio after two projects were proposed near his home. He says the ballot measure results send a message to local leaders about where residents stand. “That shows when the power of the people comes together, we can beat money and we can beat big tech,” Blankenship said. Note: election results are unofficial until confirmed by each county’s Board of Elections. Find more detailed information about local results below. The Ohio Newsroom’s Erin Gottsacker spoke with WVXU Environment Reporter Isabel Nissley about the types of ballot measures voters considered and what the results say about public sentiment. On why voters favored restricting data center developments Nissley: Data centers really connected to this larger election issue of affordability. The computing facilities require massive amounts of electricity, which is driving up energy costs statewide, and people in several communities told me they're already having to make tough choices with their finances. They're scared for what they'll have to cut next if electricity bills keep climbing up. Other people say they don't want this resource-guzzling big tech infrastructure as a neighbor. They say they're worried about data centers' noise, pollution, water use, a lack of transparency about projects from government officials and more. Those concerns are bipartisan, and they drove Ohioans to the polls to deliver an overwhelming rebuke of data centers last week. Ballot measures to limit the developments passed with a large margin of support statewide, from Sunbury in central Ohio, which passed a ban on large facilities with 79% of the vote, to Perry in Northeast Ohio, which approved restrictions with 87% of voters in favor. On how Ohio election results compared with other parts of the country Nissley: About a dozen other states had data center-related measures on the ballot, and like in Ohio, many passed with large margins of support. What's different here is the number of data centers. There are more than 200 projects planned or under construction in Ohio. That's the fifth highest number in the nation. On the impact on future developments Nissley: Organizers say last week's vote is just the start of getting more restrictions on data centers in Ohio. A statewide coalition made up of lawyers and everyday people worked with the dozen plus communities to draft ballot language. Now, Conserve Ohio says it's looking to expand its efforts in more communities and help more people amend their city charters to ban data centers. The group is also collecting signatures for a statewide petition to amend the Ohio Constitution to prohibit the construction of large-scale data centers. In terms of projects that are permitted or under construction, it looks like they'll largely proceed as planned. But future projects won't have as easy of a path forward if they're allowed to build at all. On the consequences of limiting data center development Nissley: Organizations like the Ohio Chamber of Commerce see data centers as major economic drivers. A Chamber of Commerce Research Foundation study says $40 billion have been and will be invested in data centers around the state through 2030, as well as jobs and state and local tax revenue. With new restrictions on these projects, they say communities will lose out and suffer economically. How ballot measures fared Data center ballot measures ranged from outright bans, to new regulations, to recalls of elected officials who supported data centers. Southwest Ohio City of Trenton: a charter amendment to prohibit the construction of data centers over 25 megawatts within city limits passed with 80% of the vote. City of Piqua: a charter amendment to ban the construction of data centers larger than 25 megawatts of peak power demand passed with 67% of the vote. City of Piqua: recall of commissioners in the city’s 1st, 3rd and 5th wards. All three were recalled with at least 70% of the vote. City of Urbana: a charter amendment to ban the construction of data centers larger than 7.5 megawatts of peak power demand passed with 77% of the vote. City of Urbana: a recall of Mayor Bill Bean passed with 73% of the vote. City of Wilmington: four referendums to reverse the February rezoning of four parcels totaling more than 500 acres near U.S. 68 from “rural residential” to “light industrial” adjacent to proposed data center campus. Each zone change was reversed with support from at least 79% of voters. Monroe Township (Adams County): a resolution establishing a zoning review process for “higher-impact development” passed with 60% of the vote. Sprigg (Adams County): a resolution establishing a zoning review process for “higher-impact development” passed with 53% of the vote. Northeast Ohio City of Hubbard: a blanket ban on all data centers in the city passed with 76% of the vote. City of Conneaut: a charter amendment prohibiting data centers larger than 25 megawatts in the city passed with 64% of the vote. Village of Perry: an ordinance requiring that data center development companies seeking tax incentives provide financial backing to commitments around jobs and tax revenue. Developers must post a bond to back those claims before receiving any incentives. The measure also implements noise requirements. It passed with 87% of the vote. Village of Monroeville: a pro-data center ballot issue FAILED with 87% of the vote. It was an advisory ballot question regarding an ordinance to allow data center development in the village. Because it is advisory, this question does not mandate the village to take any particular action but informs them of community sentiment. artigo.texto: Demand for Battery Storage and String Inverters Growing in India: Interview Grid-forming inverter adoption will depend on policy support and planning by grid operators November 12, 2026 Follow Mercom India on WhatsApp for exclusive updates on clean energy news and insights As battery energy storage systems (BESS) become a key focus for India’s solar inverter market, string inverters are seeing wider adoption in utility-scale projects because of their modularity, lower maintenance needs, and potential to reduce generation losses. In an interview with Mercom India at the recently concluded Renewable Energy India (REI) Expo 2026, Aniket Sawant, Country Head at GoodWe India, discussed emerging trends in India’s inverter market, the growing importance of battery storage, technological developments, component supply challenges, and the company’s expansion plans. What is GoodWe’s current inverter portfolio, and what are the company’s plans for the next two to three years? GoodWe has completed 10 years in India. Our business primarily focuses on on-grid inverters, and we serve residential, commercial and industrial (C&I), and utility-scale customers. Our residential portfolio includes single-phase inverters starting at 3 kW and three-phase inverters up to 10 kW. For C&I applications, we offer inverters ranging from 12 kW to 150 kW, while our utility-scale portfolio includes 350 kW inverters. Looking ahead, we anticipate significant growth in energy storage demand, which will be an important part of our future business. What major trends are emerging in India’s solar inverter market? Battery energy storage is one of the most significant trends in the Indian solar market. Initially, the focus was on generating solar electricity and consuming it immediately or injecting it into the grid. However, the market is shifting towards storing electricity generated during the day and using it at night. Government policies are increasingly addressing the need for energy storage across residential, C&I, and utility-scale applications. We see substantial potential for battery storage as the industry transitions from generation-focused installations toward integrated solutions. Are utility-scale solar developers shifting from central inverters to string inverters? What is driving this transition? Utility-scale projects are clearly shifting toward string inverters. Three to four years ago, central inverters dominated approximately 90% of the utility-scale market. However, developers are increasingly recognizing the technical and operational advantages of string inverters. One advantage is installation flexibility. String inverters can be mounted directly on structures, while central inverters generally require dedicated civil foundations, adding to installation costs. String inverters also offer operational and maintenance advantages because of their modular design. For example, if a central inverter serving a 1 MW block fails, the entire block can go offline, resulting in generation losses. In comparison, if a 300 kW string inverter fails, only the capacity connected to that inverter is affected. This reduces the impact of equipment failures on electricity generation and project revenue. String inverters also integrate effectively with solar trackers, supporting improved generation performance. For projects operating over 10 to 20 years, modularity, maintenance flexibility, and reduced downtime can provide long-term operational benefits. How are advancements in solar module technologies influencing inverter design and technical specifications? Solar module technology is evolving rapidly, and inverter manufacturers must continuously upgrade their products to remain compatible. A few years ago, solar modules typically had power ratings of approximately 400 W to 450 W. Today, modules with capacities reaching around 700 W are available. Inverter manufacturers must adapt their technical specifications, particularly maximum power point tracking (MPPT) current capabilities. For example, newer heterojunction modules may require MPPT current ratings of about 40 A. Inverter manufacturers must increase current handling capabilities and ensure their products remain compatible with emerging module technologies. Monitoring technological developments in solar modules and upgrading inverter specifications accordingly will remain critical. What are the major challenges in inverter manufacturing, particularly regarding semiconductor and IGBT availability? The availability of critical electronic components remains an important challenge for inverter manufacturers. India’s annual renewable energy installations have increased substantially, from approximately 9 GW to 10 GW a few years ago to around 25 GW to 30 GW. As installations increase, demand for semiconductors and insulated gate bipolar transistors (IGBTs) also rises. The global market has relatively few major suppliers of these components, including Infineon, Fuji, and established Chinese manufacturers. Large inverter manufacturers with strategic relationships with component suppliers are generally better positioned to manage supply constraints. However, fluctuations in demand and component availability can still affect procurement costs and inverter prices. How do you see grid-forming inverter technology developing in India over the next two to three years? Grid-forming inverter technology has already gained traction in markets such as the U.S. and Europe. India has its own grid requirements and project-specific challenges. Currently, grid-following inverters remain widely used because they align with existing grid requirements. Grid-forming technology can help improve grid stability through active and reactive power management. However, wider adoption will depend on clear policy direction and coordinated planning involving policymakers, the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, grid operators, and distribution companies.
