artigo.texto: The Aurora City Council moved forward with a ban on giving tax incentives to data center developers on Monday. The ordinance, proposed by Aurora Mayor Mike Coffman, was approved unanimously by the council in a study session and will go to a future regular meeting for an official vote. Recommended Stories Aurora’s city code allows the city to use retail tax revenue and construction material use tax revenue generated by qualifying development projects to help finance public improvements and attract businesses. It also allows the city to waive sales or use taxes for certain developers. The ordinance, if passed at a future regular meeting, would prohibit data center incentives entirely. “There is an unprecedented amount of money behind data centers largely driven by AI and they do not need our tax dollars,” Coffman said about his proposed ordinance Monday. No councilmembers opposed the ordinance, but several brought up concerns or alternative proposals. The council already has the ability to vote on every sales and use tax incentive, including those for data centers, Councilmember Alison Coombs said, adding that if the council does not want to give incentives to a data center, it can vote against them. If the council wants to have a broader conversation about whether its oversight procedures work well, that conversation should go to a policy committee, Coombs said. Coffman countered that the process, which happens in executive sessions, is not transparent to the public. “I don’t think it’s wise to bind the hand of future councils,” Councilmember Curtis Gardner said, adding that creating a sweeping rule for one industry “is not a good way to do governance.” Four tax incentives have been issued for data centers totaling $83 million. As of earlier this year, about $9 million had been paid out against that potential, City Manager Jason Batchelor said. After some debate, the mayor stood firm on his proposal, saying he was putting it forward for a recorded vote as-is. “If somebody else wants to have a discussion on process and procedure, you’re welcome to do that, but you will vote on this issue,” Coffman said. None of the councilmembers present opposed the ordinance. Data centers have been a major topic of discussion in recent council meetings, during which the council has passed several data center regulations but twice denied a data center moratorium. Dozens of residents have attended recent meetings to oppose data centers in Aurora, specifically the Trident Data Center from Vantage Data Centers, which was planned for an area near Green Valley Ranch communities.

artigo.texto: ‘Para reduzir emissões, precisamos de confiabilidade econômica’, diz executivo brasileiro que integra aliança empresarial na COP31 Ricardo Mussa avalia que o foco deve estar nas alternativas com melhor retorno e disponíveis atualmente, como a combinação entre solar, eólica e baterias Ex-CEO da Raízen, Ricardo Mussa atua como líder da Sustainable Business COP (SB COP), uma aliança global do setor empresarial que leva aos negociadores da COP31 exemplos de inciativas sustentáveis. Da Turquia, onde está sendo realizado o encontro, ele destaca a necessidade de apresentação de um modelo econômico viável para atrair apoio de nações à transição energética. O foco, diz, devem ser as alternativas com melhor retorno e disponíveis atualmente, como a combinação entre solar, eólica e baterias. Mussa avalia, no entanto, que substituir os combustíveis fósseis num horizonte de dez anos é “utopia”. Como o setor empresarial atuará pela transição energética na COP31? Influenciar os textos decisórios em COPs é um processo muito difícil. Há um desenho com 197 países, todos com o mesmo peso de voto, e as discussões são por consenso. Por outro lado, aprendemos que a melhor forma de realizar esse trabalho é levando exemplos, que ajudem a trazer o porquê de estarmos pedindo mudanças. O que fazemos na SB COP é buscar, no setor privado mundial, os melhores exemplos de casos de sucesso. Fizemos um concurso e recebemos 1.400 inscrições. Para ser selecionada, é preciso que a iniciativa tenha retorno econômico, histórico verificável, além de ser replicável e escalável. Quais casos concretos estão sendo levados para a Turquia? Estamos levando 50 exemplos para mostrar aos negociadores. E temos brasileiros. Um é o caso da Vale em Carajás. Há 40 anos, ela recebeu uma área no meio da Amazônia de quase um milhão de hectares para exploração de minério de ferro. Passado esse período, a empresa já exportou mais de R$ 2,6 trilhões, criou 200 mil empregos e preservou 98% da área. Outro exemplo é a Fazenda Roncador, no Mato Grosso, que é modelo para o mundo de junção de pecuária com lavoura. Há uso de biofertilizantes e biodefensivos. O dono dela fala: “Olha, busquei sustentabilidade e encontrei produtividade”. A coalizão reúne 57 milhões de empresas de 123 países. Quais os pontos de convergência e de divergência entre empresários destas nações? A maior convergência é que precisamos encontrar mecanismos sustentáveis com rentabilidade, focar naquilo que tem melhor probabilidade de sucesso. Outro ponto em que todos concordam é a necessidade de eficiência energética. A eletrificação é muito relevante. Também há convergência quanto à busca de mecanismos para melhorar o financiamento. Já as divergências ocorrem quanto à velocidade das metas energéticas e à melhor forma de conduzir o mercado de carbono no mundo. A Turquia, que divide a presidência da COP31 com a Austrália, lidera uma proposta de aceleração da eletrificação para 35% da matriz energética até 2035. É viável? É uma meta muito ambiciosa, mas avalio que parte do processo das COPs é realmente elevar a barra. É um consenso que a eletrificação é um caminho cada vez mais forte para todos os países. Esquecendo até a questão do clima, o contexto geopolítico fez com que os países olhassem a questão energética de forma diferente. Dois terços das nações não produzem petróleo, são importadoras ou dependentes dele. A geração de energia elétrica é mais descentralizada. Por uma questão de segurança energética, portanto, muitos países tem feito esse investimento em eletrificação. Mas seria uma utopia falarmos que o mundo consegue substituir os combustíveis fósseis nos próximos dez anos. Ainda precisaremos do petróleo por um bom tempo. A grande pergunta que temos hoje é se a velocidade de implementação da eletrificação é suficiente para mitigar ou reduzir os riscos climático, uma vez que não dá para abrir mão dos combustíveis fósseis no curto prazo. O senhor avalia que a exploração de petróleo na Margem Equatorial brasileira deve ser ampliada? O Brasil está passando por uma mudança na matriz energética, e o petróleo daqui é de baixa emissão. O país não pode abrir mão do que a Margem Equatorial traz. O que o Brasil precisa é discutir como fazer o investimento de forma segura, sustentável. Debater o destino e o uso desses recursos ao longo do tempo para políticas públicas, inclusive para renovação do parque industrial. Temos excedente de energia, mas ainda assim ela é muito cara para indústria e consumidor final. Qual a avaliação do senhor sobre o mapa do caminho global apresentado pela presidência brasileira na COP30 para afastamento do uso de combustíveis fósseis? Acho muito bem-vinda toda essa discussão. O Brasil não se acanhou em colocar no papel. Mas, na minha visão, o presidente Lula não deveria deixar de explorar a Margem Equatorial por conta desse documento. Muito pelo contrário, entendo que o Brasil reconhece a adicionalidade da energia, o papel dela nesse mundo de demanda geopolítica, defendendo a realização de forma segura. O petróleo subiu muito com a guerra da Ucrânia e, depois, com a do Irã, incentivando investimentos no setor. O cenário atrapalha as metas globais de redução de CO2? O sinal de preço é importante. Quem está no mercado de combustíveis fósseis vai ganhar hoje mais dinheiro no curto prazo. Mas vejo que as decisões estratégicas tomadas atualmente pelos países vão no sentido de reduzir a dependência do petróleo. Isso é perceptível na COP31, o choque que ocorre agora incentiva a produção de fontes renováveis. Não há uma redução no interesse em diversificar a matriz energética, em buscar alternativas. A biomassa é hoje uma saída viável para as indústrias se descarbonizarem? O Brasil tem uma excelente matriz e grande produção de biomassa. Podemos nos beneficiar muito mais do que outras nações. A biomassa é como se fosse uma grande bateria e isso é uma vantagem com relação à eletricidade. Sempre fui defensor de que deveríamos eletrificar uma parte do parque industrial par

artigo.texto: The deployment of renewable energies is advancing at a historic pace. However, as they become more prevalent in the energy system, large-scale storage systems are required to prevent electricity generated during solar and wind production peaks from being lost. Global investment in these technologies continues to grow., and in the most dynamic markets, about 80% of new large-scale developments already combine solar energy with battery systems. Nevertheless, the international supply chain faces major challenges due to dependence on metals such as lithium and cobalt. To diversify these solutions, the scientific community has turned its attention to a highly abundant resource: saltwater from the seas. This search for new formulas complements stationary storage methods investigating everyday, low-impact materials, such as sand batteries for thermal storage. This opens up a range of solutions that allow renewable energy generation to be decoupled from the time of consumption. Although the development of lithium-ion batteries marked a historic turning point in the electrification of transportation and electronics, for which the Nobel Prize in Chemistry was awarded in 2019, grid storage requires innovation in other areas. One of the most promising technologies in this field is seawater batteries (SWBs), which are currently in the research phase and have great potential in terms of storage. They represent a technological shift because they use the salts present in the aquatic environment—specifically sodium ions (Naâº)—as the active material for storing energy. Rather than being sealed cells from start to finish, they have an open part that interacts with the seawater and oxygen in the environment. When charged with renewable electricity, the battery traps sodium from the saltwater and accumulates it at its negative pole. When discharging, the process naturally reverses, returning the sodium to the sea and releasing the stored electricity to the grid. To keep this reaction stable and prevent water from degrading the internal components, these cells use a NASICON-type solid separator (sodium super-ionic conductor), a high-strength ceramic material. Unlike conventional plastic membranes, this ceramic component acts as a selective filter, allowing only sodium ions to pass through. This prevents two common problems associated with equipment submerged in seawater: the build-up of encrusted salts (scaling) and the adhesion of algae or microorganisms (fouling). A three-in-one solution: renewable energy, water reuse, and carbon capture Seawater batteries’ greatest potential lies in their ability to integrate various sustainability-contributing applications within a single operating cycle: - Integrated water desalination: By combining the NASICON ceramic separator with a complementary membrane to capture chloride, the battery separates the salt from seawater while simultaneously storing electricity. This advantage is strategic for coastal regions subjected to periods of water stress. According to the Spanish Desalination and Reuse Association (AEDyR), Spain is leading the way in water reuse in Europe with rates between 10% and 13% of the flow treated through advanced systems, highlighting the energy efficiency of water treatment. - Passive COâ capture: During discharge, the system naturally generates sodium hydroxide. This alkaline substance spontaneously reacts with the carbon dioxide (COâ) dissolved in seawater and with minerals such as calcium or magnesium, causing the gas to transform into stable solid carbonates. This carbon sequestration mechanism operates without the need for heat or additional energy consumption. The road towards industrial scale Testing in laboratories and research centers has progressed from tiny button batteries to larger prototypes assembled in independent modules. This modular structure allows cells to be stacked like blocks, enabling adaptation to industrial facilities, docks, and generation parks at sea. The European Union is seeking to increase its capacity in this environment. Although technical challenges remain to advance its commercial implementation, seawater battery research demonstrates how innovation can expand energy storage alternatives. Exploring new materials, resources, and applications creates opportunities for developing more efficient and sustainable solutions that can complement the advancement of renewable energies and utilize available resources more effectively.

artigo.texto: Rivian and Redwood Materials Expand Partnership to Span the Lifecycle of the Battery Redwood will now recycle Rivian’s battery scrap and end-of-life packs as well as provide energy storage for its manufacturing plant IRVINE, Calif.–(BUSINESS WIRE)–American automaker Rivian (NASDAQ: RIVN) and energy technology company Redwood Materials today announced a major expansion of their partnership, establishing Redwood as one of Rivian’s key partners to enabling end-to-end energy solutions—recycling Rivian’s production scrap and end-of-life EV batteries, as well as providing stationary battery storage at its manufacturing plant in Normal, Illinois. Through the partnership, Redwood collects Rivian EV battery packs through Rivian’s nationwide network of service centers when they are no longer suitable for in-vehicle use. Redwood then evaluates each battery pack to determine whether to repurpose it for energy storage—deployed directly at Rivian’s manufacturing facilities or at other locations—or to recycle it. Redwood will now also recycle battery scrap generated at Rivian’s manufacturing operations. This new scope of the partnership builds on the existing work, announced in April 2026, that is deploying 10 megawatt-hours (MWh) of battery energy storage from repurposed Rivian battery packs at the automaker’s manufacturing plant in Normal, Illinois. RJ Scaringe, Rivian Founder and CEO, said: Giving Rivian battery packs a second life in stationary storage is a massive unlock for the energy transition, “By partnering with JB and the Redwood team, we’re turning retired EV batteries into a powerful tool to make the grid more reliable and lower energy costs for everyone.” JB Straubel, Redwood Materials Founder and CEO, said: Every Rivian battery pack that comes back to us is a potential source of domestic grid energy storage in addition to critical materials, “Redwood’s unique ability to integrate and redeploy Rivian batteries with our technology is an opportunity to enable fast, flexible and more cost-efficient energy storage. As the demand and cost for energy keeps rising, working with companies like Rivian is how we help meet these challenges.” When EV batteries reach the end of their useful lives in vehicles, they often still have substantial useful energy capacity for second-life applications, such as stationary storage. Energy storage applications with repurposed batteries can ease stress on the grid during periods of high electricity demand, improving grid reliability while reducing energy costs for the user, as well as the grid at large. During periods of low demand or when low-cost renewable energy is most productive, these packs can store electricity for easy dispatch during periods of higher demand. When paired with Rivian—and other—EV battery packs, Redwood’s proprietary technology architecture offers an integrated system that can respond intelligently to the needs of the facility it is serving. Once batteries are no longer useful in energy storage applications, or where scrap is generated during manufacturing, they can be recycled. Redwood’s advanced process is capable of recycling and recovering critical minerals like lithium, nickel, cobalt, and copper at rates exceeding 95 percent, encouraging the development of a circular, domestic supply chain for battery materials in the United States. This expanded partnership reflects a broader shift underway in how American manufacturers source power. As grid connections take years to secure and conventional infrastructure remains supply-constrained, companies increasingly need partners who can solve more than one piece of the problem—recovering materials, managing recycling, and deploying storage as a single system rather than separate vendors. Rivian’s work with Redwood is a model for that approach: one partnership spanning the full lifecycle of a battery, built to move faster than the grid alone can. artigo.texto: Data centers no Brasil: Como o Redata reforça o papel estratégico da análise imobiliária O regime tributário estabelece incentivos ao setor, mas exige análise prévia dos imóveis para garantir a viabilidade dos empreendimentos. quarta-feira, 11 de novembro de 2026 Atualizado às 14:58 A criação do Redata - Regime Especial de Tributação para Serviços de Datacenter, pela lei 15.504, sancionada em setembro de 2026, trouxe importantes benefícios tributários para estimular a instalação e expansão de data centers no Brasil. Além da dimensão tributária, porém, a estruturação desses projetos exige uma análise imobiliária prévia e criteriosa. Essa análise é determinante para a viabilidade dos data centers e para a adequada alocação dos riscos de implantação. Antes de adquirir um terreno, celebrar uma locação ou estruturar um contrato de BTS - Built to Suit, é indispensável avaliar não apenas a segurança jurídica, mas também a capacidade do imóvel de suportar a operação pretendida. No caso de data centers, a due diligence imobiliária assume um escopo significativamente mais amplo. Além da análise tradicional de titularidade e restrições, é preciso avaliar se o imóvel reúne condições operacionais efetivas, como disponibilidade e capacidade de energia, infraestrutura de telecomunicações, recursos hídricos e potencial de expansão. São variáveis que impactam diretamente a viabilidade do projeto e cujo mapeamento exige conhecimento que vai além do registro imobiliário. Os requisitos do Redata ilustram bem esse ponto. Embora os incentivos estejam concentrados na aquisição de equipamentos e infraestrutura tecnológica, o regime impõe condições de energia, sustentabilidade e eficiência operacional que recaem diretamente sobre o imóvel. O atendimento integral da demanda energética por fontes renováveis ou de baixa emissão, somado às exigências de eficiência hídrica, pode tornar um terreno aparentemente adequado inviável na prática, seja pela incapacidade da infraestrutura local, por prazos de conexão incompatíveis com o cronograma ou pela impossibilidade de expansão. Na prática, isso significa que a due diligence imobiliária precisa ocorrer antes da decisão de investimento, e não apenas para confirmá-la. Em projetos de grande escala, uma restrição identificada após a aquisição do terreno pode comprometer significativamente o cronograma e o custo do empreendimento. Essa abordagem se reflete diretamente na estruturação das operações imobiliárias relacionadas a data centers, seja na aquisição de terrenos, na celebração de locações, na elaboração de contratos de Built to Suit ou em operações de investimento. Em qualquer dessas modalidades, as condições de infraestrutura são determinantes para a operação e precisam ser tratadas como riscos contratuais. Responsabilidades pela obtenção de licenças, implantação de infraestrutura, conexão de energia, investimentos adicionais, cumprimento de requisitos técnicos e ambientais e consequências de alterações regulatórias devem ser adequadamente distribuídas entre as partes envolvidas. O Brasil já ocupa posição de destaque no mercado global de data centers, com volumes expressivos de investimento sendo direcionados ao país. A rápida expansão do setor, impulsionada pela crescente demanda por infraestrutura capaz de suportar aplicações de inteligência artificial, reforça a urgência dessa análise. A escala e a densidade tecnológica exigidas por operações de IA ampliam significativamente os requisitos de energia, refrigeração e conectividade. Esse movimento já se reflete na expansão geográfica dos empreendimentos, evidenciando que a escolha da localização depende não apenas da disponibilidade de terrenos, mas também da infraestrutura necessária para suportar operações de alta densidade. A escolha do site para um data center, portanto, não é mais uma decisão puramente imobiliária. Localização, capacidade energética, conectividade, disponibilidade hídrica e possibilidade de expansão compõem uma equação de viabilidade que precisa ser resolvida antes, e não depois, da contratação. Embora o Redata tenha natureza predominantemente tributária e tecnológica, seus incentivos tendem a impulsionar a demanda por áreas aptas à instalação de data centers, reforçando a relevância de uma due diligence imobiliária que vá além da verificação registral e abranja regularidade fundiária, urbanística, ambiental e de infraestrutura. Os benefícios do regime não eliminam os desafios de implantação; ao contrário, reforçam a necessidade de uma análise integrada, conduzida antes da aquisição ou contratação do imóvel, capaz de orientar a decisão de investimento, a estruturação dos contratos e a alocação dos riscos do empreendimento. Os benefícios do Redata podem estar nos equipamentos, mas as condições para viabilizá-los começam muito antes: na escolha e na análise do imóvel. Mariana Araujo Ozanan Advogada do Machado Meyer Advogados.

artigo.texto: Jefferson County residents weigh extending data center moratorium at public meeting MONTICELLO, Fla. -- Jefferson County residents and leaders gathered for a public workshop to weigh the potential impacts of data centers and to discuss whether the county’s one-year moratorium should continue. County leaders said the workshop was intended to give both commissioners and the public a clearer understanding of how data centers could affect the area, including electricity and water consumption, runoff and noise. The meeting was also framed as an educational session, not a vote on any specific project. “You should always be concerned about anything that we are not very sure about. That’s the reason for this workshop, Tonight their not voting on anything the board of county commissioners is just educating themselves as well as the public so that they can make an informed decision once the moratorium expires in June of 2027,” said Doug Baber, county manager for Jefferson County. Some residents voiced skepticism about whether data centers would be a good fit for the community, including concerns about who would ultimately pay for the infrastructure and utility demands associated with large facilities. “People in the community were paying for the data centers utility usage and I need to know..My light bills are high enough, I don’t need to pay for a billionaires data center,” said Mary Harris, a Jefferson County resident. Jefferson County leaders agreed on June 18 to a one-year moratorium on data centers to allow time to consider their impact. Baber said the technology and the public perception around it can shift quickly. “Data centers change every day, through the good on some things, the bad on other things and a lot of times their the boogie man. So the things that you don’t know and you don’t respect often you think the worst of,” Baber said. During the workshop, electricity usage and the size of potential facilities were among the sticking points discussed. The forum also gave county commissioners and residents a chance to consider possible guardrails for data centers moving forward, as environmental concerns continue to be raised statewide about the pros and cons of data centers locating near neighborhoods.

artigo.texto: A massive data center development proposed in Sutton could bring nearly $28 million a year in property tax revenue to the Massachusetts town, but the project is already drawing concerns from residents about its potential impact on their community. The proposal calls for a 10-building data center campus off Boston and Providence roads. Each building would be roughly 250,000 square feet, bringing the development to approximately 2.5 million square feet at full build-out — the equivalent of about 43 football fields of floor space. Stream NBC10 Boston news for free, 24/7, wherever you are. The project is associated with the Kraft Group and Unified Global Packaging Group, which owns the property. The development could represent approximately $16.75 billion in investment and require about 900 megawatts of electricity at full build-out, according to the town's preliminary review. That amount of power would put the proposal among the larger data center developments being planned nationwide. For Sutton, the financial implications could be significant. Town projections estimate the first two buildings could generate about $10.4 million in annual property taxes by fiscal year 2031. Once all 10 buildings are assessed, the town estimates annual property tax revenue could reach approximately $27.8 million by fiscal year 2035. The town's financial modeling also predicts that the average single-family homeowner could pay approximately $5,800 less annually by fiscal year 2035 than under the town's projected tax bills without the development. The possibility of financial relief comes as Sutton projects a structural budget deficit that could grow to approximately $9.1 million by fiscal year 2033 without corrective action. But some residents say the potential financial benefits do not outweigh their concerns. Neighbors raised questions Tuesday about noise, water and electricity use, generators, traffic and potential costs for municipal services. The town's review identifies several of those issues as areas requiring further study, including water supply, wastewater, noise, lighting, traffic and emergency response. "This is just the very, very beginning of this," Jonathan Anderson, chair of the Sutton Select Board, told residents. No final approval has been granted. Town officials expect additional technical review and negotiations over zoning regulations and a community benefits agreement. A zoning change would require a Planning Board hearing and approval by a two-thirds vote at Town Meeting. Residents made clear Tuesday that scrutiny of the proposal is just beginning. "I have a 3-year-old grandson," longtime resident Mario Giamie told NBC10 Boston. "And I'm not going to subject him to this if I can fight it, and I will fight it."

artigo.texto: From Nov. 9 to 20, Antalya, Türkiye, is hosting the 31st Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31). Its main themes are climate finance, adaptation, the energy transition, reducing the energy intensity of buildings and reporting on commitments made. Since the first days of its independence, Kazakhstan has been an active and responsible participant in global processes on sustainable development and climate change: it signed and ratified the Kyoto Protocol in 2009 and subsequently joined the Paris Agreement in 2016. This was preceded by extensive expert and analytical work by the Ministry of Environmental Protection, renamed the Ministry of Ecology and Natural Resources in 2021, with support from the World Bank, the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), the Asian Development Bank (ADB), the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), the United Nations Development Program (UNDP), national experts and the National Chamber of Entrepreneurs of Kazakhstan. Today, Kazakhstan positions itself as a leader in advancing the green energy transition not only in Central Asia but also across the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS). Kazakhstan was the first country in the region to adopt a Strategy for Achieving Carbon Neutrality by 2060. This year, by Sept. 1 order of the Prime Minister, a Plan of Organizational Measures for implementing the Strategy was approved. The plan will help integrate decarbonization principles into all areas of the national economy, including sectoral planning systems and the monitoring, reporting and accounting of greenhouse gas emissions on an innovative, digital basis. The initiative of President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev to harness the potential of artificial intelligence (AI) is especially relevant to resetting the country’s national emissions trading system. Speaking at the BRICS+ summit on Sept. 13, he again underlined the role of AI in global development and noted that “Kazakhstan regards AI as a strategic priority and is ready to use its advanced computing infrastructure, as well as national and UN digital centers, to expand effective cooperation” for the country’s sustainable development. COP31 experts note a revival of global carbon trading, particularly in the submission of projects to the voluntary carbon market, which undergo a multi-stage review by the Integrity Council for the Voluntary Carbon Market (ICVCM). As regards the regulated greenhouse gas market – existing national emissions trading systems and their participation in global carbon trading – discussions continue on avoiding double counting and on building the necessary carbon infrastructure. Among Asian countries, Kazakhstan was one of the first to launch an emissions trading system (KazETS). It covers 220 installations in the six basic sectors of the economy and is now undergoing a transformation through the development and introduction of auctioning and of production benchmarks drawing on EU and OECD experience. At the same time, full participation of Kazakh enterprises in global carbon trading and access to the carbon markets of other countries require, first and foremost: a gradual phase-out of free allowances; a higher price per tonne of greenhouse gases; the transfer of the existing MRV (monitoring, reporting and verification) system to a digital platform. For Kazakh exporters, the absence of a modern, internationally recognised infrastructure for monitoring, reporting and verifying CO₂ emissions, and of verifiers accredited in line with international requirements, is currently a serious challenge. At the same time, the experience of leading carbon market players and platforms such as Sylvera, BeZero Carbon, Isometric and Calyx Global shows that AI makes it possible to assess the integrity and risks of carbon projects, to evaluate the carbon footprint and the contribution of enterprises and sectors to the Sustainable Development Goals, and to build digital solutions, including under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement. At COP31, the National Pavilion of Kazakhstan will also present a number of digital solutions for resetting the national ETS and creating a regional digital climate hub with the support of the UNFCCC. We hope that this initiative, developed by experts of Astana Hub together with Green Academy, the University of Central Asia and the Kunayev Institute of Mining, with the support of the Swedish company Planboo and SagtaAI, will be supported by the delegations of the Central Asian countries and included in the outcome document of COP31. The author is Professor Dr. Bakhyt Yessekina, a member of the Green Council under the President of Kazakhstan. Yessekina is the head of the Green Academy Scientific Research and Education Center. artigo.texto: Mercado global de etiquetas para fios: Tamanho, Tendências e Previsão até 2035 - Relatório completo em PDF · pacote de dados Excel · documento Word · apresentação executiva - Entrega por e-mail 24/7, inclusive fins de semana e feriados - Copiar e colar habilitado · formato pronto para impressão - Rodadas ilimitadas de esclarecimentos após a entrega Mercado de etiquetas para fios até 2035: demanda por cabeamento de data centers impulsiona o crescimento Resumo Segundo o mais recente relatório da IndexBox sobre o mercado global de Etiquetas para Fios, o mercado entra em 2026 com fundamentos de demanda mais amplos, comportamento de compras mais disciplinado e uma arquitetura de suprimento mais diversificada regionalmente. O mercado global de etiquetas para fios é um componente essencial, ainda que muitas vezes negligenciado, do setor mais amplo de soluções de identificação elétrica e industrial. No período de análise de 2026, o mercado se caracteriza por demanda estável, sustentada por exigências obrigatórias de segurança, conformidade e eficiência operacional nos setores de infraestrutura, manufatura e tecnologia. Este relatório oferece uma avaliação abrangente do estado atual do mercado, de suas cadeias de suprimento complexas e da dinâmica competitiva entre fornecedores globais de materiais e fabricantes especializados. As trajetórias de crescimento estão fundamentalmente atreladas ao investimento global em eletrificação, expansão de data centers, automação industrial e infraestrutura de energia renovável. O mercado não é monolítico: segmenta-se por tipo de material, tecnologia de impressão e indústria de uso final, cada qual com drivers de demanda e cenários competitivos próprios. Embora a sensibilidade a preço continue sendo um fator, a proposta de valor das etiquetas para fios está cada vez mais ligada à durabilidade, à legibilidade e à integração com sistemas digitais de gestão de ativos. O período de análise até 2035 prevê um mercado em evolução, respondendo à integração tecnológica e às pressões por sustentabilidade. Este relatório oferece uma base granular e orientada por dados para que as partes interessadas compreendam os fluxos de volume e valor, identifiquem oportunidades estratégicas e naveguem pelos desafios logísticos e competitivos que definirão o desenvolvimento do mercado na próxima década. O cenário-base para o mercado mundial de etiquetas para fios até 2035 pressupõe expansão contínua em ritmo moderado, com valor e volume globais crescendo de forma constante a partir da base de 2025. A demanda é ancorada por exigências obrigatórias de identificação em instalações elétricas, cablagem de dados e telecomunicações e painéis de controle industrial, nos quais as etiquetas apoiam a conformidade com normas de segurança, a eficiência da manutenção e a rastreabilidade. O driver concreto mais forte é a rápida expansão de data centers e de infraestrutura de cablagem de alta densidade, que exige grandes volumes de marcadores de fios duráveis e legíveis para instalação, comissionamento e manutenção contínua. A automação industrial e a fabricação de painéis de controle acrescentam demanda, à medida que montadores de painéis e integradores de sistemas especificam etiquetas que atendem às normas UL, IEC e outras. Instalações de energia renovável, incluindo parques solares e eólicos, contribuem com crescimento incremental por meio de suas extensas redes de fiação. Do lado da oferta, o mercado permanece fragmentado, com fornecedores globais de materiais e conversores especializados competindo em desempenho de material, durabilidade da impressão e velocidade de personalização. A volatilidade dos preços de matérias-primas para polímeros e adesivos representa um risco persistente de margem, enquanto a transição para impressão digital e kits de etiquetas pré-impressas está remodelando os canais de distribuição. Regionalmente, a Ásia-Pacífico mantém a maior participação no consumo, apoiada pela fabricação de eletrônicos e pelo investimento em infraestrutura, enquanto a América do Norte e a Europa priorizam produtos de alto desempenho e certificados. A previsão aponta para um índice de mercado de 142 em 2035 (2025=100), equivalente a uma CAGR de 3,6%, com potencial de alta decorrente da aceleração dos gastos com data centers e eletrificação e risco de baixa associado à fraqueza industrial cíclica. Drivers e restrições da demanda Principais drivers de demanda - A rápida construção de data centers e a cablagem de fibra e cobre de alta densidade exigem etiquetas para fios duráveis e legíveis para instalação e manutenção. - As normas de segurança elétrica e conformidade exigem identificação clara de fios em instalações industriais, comerciais e de infraestrutura. - A automação industrial e a fabricação de painéis de controle ampliam a demanda por marcadores de fios pré-impressos e imprimíveis. - Instalações de energia renovável, incluindo parques solares e eólicos, envolvem extensas redes de fiação que exigem etiquetagem. - O crescimento da fabricação de chicotes automotivos e aeroespaciais aumenta as exigências de rastreabilidade e identificação. - A automação predial e os sistemas inteligentes de gestão de instalações impulsionam a demanda por cabeamento estruturado e etiquetagem. Possíveis restrições ao crescimento - A volatilidade dos preços de matérias-primas de polímeros e adesivos pressiona as margens dos fabricantes e pode adiar decisões de compra. - A concorrência de produtores regionais de baixo custo limita o poder de precificação em segmentos sensíveis a preço. - A adoção de sistemas digitais e de gestão de ativos baseados em RFID pode reduzir a demanda por alguns tipos convencionais de etiquetas. - A fraqueza cíclica da produção industrial e da construção pode reduzir temporariamente o consumo de etiquetas para fios. artigo.texto: Company proposing battery storage facility, data center infrastructure site in South Bend SOUTH BEND, Ind. (WSBT) — An energy center development could be in South Bend's future. The company nextNRG is planning to develop 27 acres into a data center infrastructure, battery storage, and pharmaceutical site. The multi-million-dollar proposal is in its early stages and the deal has not officially been closed. The proposed development, would be called the Lone Wolf Energy Center. The company nextNRG is planning to acquire 33-acres located on Lone Wolf Drive near the Toll Road and US 31 on South Bend's Northwest side. This announcement came as a surprise for neighbors who live nearby. “Well, I'm very shocked first of all. What is going on, Will it affect us? So, we're, I'm sure most of my neighbors out here are going to be very not happy. You know, they're upset already that no one contacts them and stuff,” said Tom Bayer. 27 acres would be used for data center infrastructure and battery storage. It's expected to support up to 70 megawatts of capacity, but could potentially go up to 100 megawatts. But it leaves neighbors with concerns about the potential long-term effects of this development. “So we'd like to know, are we protected? I heard about water issues, you know, I've heard about noise, which noise pollution, you know. So, there's a lot of issues that haven't been come forward to us," said Bayer. The city of South Bend says they have also had no communication with NextNRG and said in a statement: "The City learned of NextNRG’s involvement and the larger project scope from Inside Indiana Business on Friday. If accurate, the city will hold this project to protections and standards in the Neighborhood’s-First framework, including zero local incentives or subsidies and a requirement that the developer pay its own way for any infrastructure and energy needs." The existing 50,000 square-foot building would be leased separately to a pharmaceutical company for 10-years. NextNRG says the proposed acquisition remains subject to negotiation and execution of transaction documents. Meaning the deal has not officially closed for the $22 million purchase. WSBT sent a list of questions to NextNRG: What does the timeline look like for this project? - What does the timeline look like for this project? - How will the company address potential noise, emissions, water use, and traffic from this project? - Why is this location being chosen in South Bend? - What can those who live in South Bend expect from the company and completion of this data center? - How does the size of this data center and impact compare to other locations the company owns? - Some residents are calling for transparency about this project. Do you plan to hold a public, in-person meeting to address potential concerns? - What are the potential costs of this project? NextNRG response: Statement: NextNRG was founded to make energy smarter and cleaner, and the Lone Wolf Energy Center in South Bend is designed to meet growing technology demand without putting the cost on the community. When our November 5 announcement referred to a data center, it meant the amount of power the site can support, not the development of a traditional hyperscale facility. Lone Wolf aims to generate its own power on site to support compact, modular computing units, so it won’t strain the local grid, raise utility rates, draw on local water or seek local tax incentives. The project remains in its early stages, with negotiations ongoing and no final agreements in place. We look forward to working alongside South Bend residents to pioneer a greener model that the community can be proud of as we spearhead the future of energy, together. FAQ Is NextNRG building a data center in South Bend? No. Lone Wolf is intended as an energy project that will generate power on site and use it to support modular computing units. These are container-sized systems set on concrete pads, with no large building, no water use and no major construction. Our announcement used the term “data center” to describe the site’s power capacity, not the type of facility. How is modular computing different from a traditional data center? Modular computing units are compact, quiet, and self-contained. They have their own cooling systems, need only limited construction, and run at a fraction of the scale of hyperscale campuses, which can span millions of square feet, draw hundreds of megawatts from the local grid, and use large amounts of water for cooling. Will this affect my utility bills, water or taxes? Lone Wolf is designed to produce its own power, so it is not expected to strain the grid or raise residents’ utility rates. It does not draw on local water and is not seeking local tax incentives. It is expected to add to the local tax base, not take from it. How will this impact the surrounding community? Lone Wolf would add to South Bend’s tax base and bring local construction jobs to the area. Because the project will generate its own power, it would reduce reliance on the local grid and would not increase residents’ utility rates. It would also not draw on local water or rely on local tax incentives, and construction would be limited to site preparation. Where does the project stand? The project is in its early stages, with negotiations ongoing and no final agreements in place. NextNRG looks forward to working openly with residents as plans develop. It’s unclear what the timeline is or when the approval process could be finalized.

artigo.texto: Proposed Auburndale data center draws scrutiny over power demand, water use and impact AUBURNDALE, Fla. - Hundreds packed a public workshop Tuesday night as Auburndale residents and local leaders challenged developers over the massive power and water demands of a proposed hyperscale data center. Auburndale technology center proposal The backstory: The proposed data center would sit on 75 acres along Pace Road. The project is part of the Florida High Tech Corridor, an innovation district established about 30 years ago. In December 2023, Auburndale city commissioners approved a new land-use designation and rezoning for the property, allowing for industrial and certain technology uses, including a data center. Construction on the first two of four approved buildings began in early 2024. The property was purchased in December 2025 by Pace Road DC Development LLC, the company behind the current proposal. Some current commissioners acknowledged they were not in office when the original land-use and zoning decisions were made. City Commissioner Sean Levy said, "I will not allow a rubber stamp process to jeopardize our resources, economy or the peace of our schools." Power grid and water concerns By the numbers: One of the biggest questions surrounding the project is how much electricity it could require. TECO would supply the power, with demand expected to start at 350 megawatts and eventually increase to 700 megawatts. That's enough electricity to power an estimated 350,000 to 500,000 homes. Residents also raised questions about water use and noise. Teresa Detweiler said, "People put their whole life savings into their property and homeownership, and you have a data center that's coming in and your property drops by 10 percent." Polk County economic impact The other side: The developer estimates the facility would use more than 4,600 gallons of potable water per day, compared with as much as 10,000 gallons for a warehouse of the same size. The company says it plans to use a closed-loop cooling system and limit noise at the property line to 50 decibels, about the level of a quiet office. They are also projecting 292 permanent jobs and say the project will not receive financial incentives. The first two buildings are expected to be operational by 2029. State utility cost regulations What's next: The developer submitted a building permit application and interior retrofit site plan on November 4. The city still needs to review those plans. There are also questions about who will pay for the electricity and infrastructure needed to serve the data center. Florida Senate Bill 484, signed into law this year, requires data centers to cover their electricity and infrastructure costs rather than pass them on to other ratepayers. However, TECO still needs approval from the Florida Public Service Commission for its new tariff, which will govern how those costs are charged. The Source: FOX 13 attended the public workshop and heard from Auburndale city commissioners, residents, the developer, Pace Road DC Development LLC, and TECO. Project details and estimates were presented during the workshop.

artigo.texto: Chinese battery giant CATL has confirmed that it is currently in the very early process of researching lithium-air battery technology, a battery format which could bring dramatic improvements to energy density – potentially enough to allow an EV fitted with a lithium-air battery pack to travel up to 2,000 kilometres (1,240 miles) between charges. Lithium-air batteries – will they be the next big thing for premium EVs of the future? Right now, the electric car industry is dominated by lithium-ion batteries. Nickel-rich NMC (nickel manganese cobalt) packs are the most common choice, though LFP (lithium iron phosphate) packs are also rapidly growing in popularity. LFP offers lower energy density than NMC, but it is cheaper to produce and avoids the use of critical materials like nickel and cobalt, while technological advances have narrowed the range gap between the two. Solid-state batteries, which replace the liquid electrolyte found in today’s lithium-ion cells with a solid one, are widely seen as the next big development, with major gains in range, charging speed and safety, and fully solid-state batteries are expected to arrive in high-end EVs over the next few years. Looking even further ahead, however, lithium-air technology could offer another leap forward, although CATL’s research remains in its early stages. While conventional lithium-ion batteries work by moving lithium ions between an anode and a cathode through a liquid or gel electrolyte, a lithium-air battery pairs a lithium-metal anode with a lightweight, porous cathode that draws in oxygen from the surrounding air. During discharge, lithium ions react with that oxygen to form lithium peroxide, releasing energy. Because one of the key ingredients is taken from the air rather than carried inside the cell, the chemistry is far lighter than conventional lithium-ion, allowing much more energy to be stored in a battery pack of the same weight. CATL hasn’t placed an official figure on what energy density they expect to see in their lithium-air research, but current data puts that at a best-case scenario of 3,500Wh per kg. In comparison, the average lithium-ion battery has an energy density between just 250-300Wh per kg. CATL have also made clear that it is a ‘long-term’ research project, rather than something coming around the corner. If such battery technology does eventually make it to the EV market however, expect it to be limited to high-end expensive EVs at first.

artigo.texto: China has officially connected the world’s largest liquid air energy storage (LAES) facility to the electricity grid in Golmud, Qinghai Province, marking a major development in long-duration energy storage technology. The 60 MW project is located in the Qaidam Basin, adjacent to a large solar power facility, and is designed to improve renewable energy integration and grid stability. The facility aims to address the challenge of balancing electricity supply and demand as solar and wind generation fluctuate throughout the day. It uses surplus electricity generated during periods of high renewable energy production to store energy for later use when demand increases. The storage process begins with ordinary air, which is purified and compressed using a multi-stage centrifugal compressor. During compression, the system captures and stores the generated heat in insulated tanks. The compressed air is then cooled to approximately minus 194 degrees Celsius, converting it into liquid form. This liquid air is stored in large tanks under near-atmospheric pressure until electricity is required. When power demand rises, the stored liquid air is pumped and heated before being converted back into gas. The expanding gas drives turbines, generating electricity that can be supplied to the grid. This process allows the facility to store surplus renewable energy and release it during periods of higher electricity consumption. The project can absorb approximately 600 MWh of surplus electricity per day and is expected to deliver around 180 GWh of electricity annually. Its capacity could support the electricity requirements of tens of thousands of households while helping reduce the challenges associated with intermittent renewable energy generation. Unlike conventional battery storage systems that depend on minerals such as lithium, liquid air energy storage uses ordinary atmospheric air as its primary storage medium. It also does not require specific underground geological formations, making the technology more flexible in terms of project locations and deployment. Another important feature of the facility is its 100% domestic equipment localization rate. The project uses locally developed intellectual property, equipment and manufacturing supply chains, highlighting China’s efforts to strengthen its domestic energy storage industry. The commissioning of the Golmud facility represents an important milestone for large-scale energy storage. Its operational performance is expected to provide valuable experience for future projects and demonstrate how long-duration storage technologies can support renewable energy expansion, improve grid flexibility and strengthen electricity supply reliability. artigo.texto: Trending LANSING -- Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel has filed a petition for rehearing before the Michigan Public Service Commission (MPSC) in case U-22058, wherein the Commission approved DTE's special contracts to service a Google hyperscale data center in Van Buren Township. The Attorney General repeatedly demonstrates in her petition where DTE failed to meet its legal burdens, the MPSC ruled in error by applying incorrect standards of review and acting without reason or regard for ratepayer protections, and how the consequences of both are unnecessary risks of cost-shifting from DTE and Google to the utility's household, business, and other classes of customers. Attorney General Nessel raises in her petition several proposals for strengthening DTE's cost recoveries from Google, establishing sufficient cost and benefit tracking mechanisms, and ensuring adequate cost backstops by Google and DTE that won't ultimately fall on DTE's existing ratepaying customers. "These are massive, twenty-year, billion-dollar contracts between one of the wealthiest businesses on the planet, and one of the most powerful companies in the State," said Attorney General Nessel. "The MPSC simply didn't do their job here – failing to protect DTE's existing residential and business customers, and accepting lousy contracts with weak terms to yet again appease a utility they're supposed to keep in check. Sweetheart deals for data centers and unaccountable utilities run amok is not responsible government, and it's not good business for the State. In this petition we've outlined serious concerns about how these contracts set up DTE customers to be burned." Among the Attorney General's most significant concerns is the MPSC's decision to adopt DTE's contract-long "aggregation" approach to assessing projected ratepayer benefits against the utility's actual costs to serve the Google data center. This decision presumably accepts years-long periods where DTE's other customers will directly subsidize the operation of the hypserscale data center, and the MPSC itself concedes this will certainly happen, at least for a four-year period from 2035 to 2038. DTE proposed to the MPSC a 20-year term-long "aggregation" standard for evaluating costs and benefits to and from its other customers, and assumes only to evaluate or demonstrate whether other customers bore any net-negative cost of serving the Google data center in view of the entire 20-year term, indicating that DTE expects its other customers to pay costs to support the data center and makes difficult any challenge to those costs until the contract term concludes. The MPSC order establishes the precedent and the expectation for their acceptance of DTE passing on data center costs to other ratepayers in any number of years under the presumption of a longer-term benefit that has not been adequately supported throughout the case and that may not ever be realized. "The most shocking part of these contracts is that DTE and the MPSC are seemingly signing off on unknown ratepayer costs to support the Google data center, as long as DTE's benefit projections can keep pace for 20 years" added Attorney General Nessel. "It's imperative to keep DTE from charging Michigan households their own costs to fuel Google's data center, and that we insist that costs and benefits be accounted for and reconciled annually. This aggregation standard, on a twenty-year contract, simply swings the doors wide open for customer cost-shifting, and that's how the data center crash-lands onto your electric bill." The MPSC additionally adopted a collateral cap limiting Google and parent company Alphabet's liability for costs of service, which the Attorney General urges the MPSC to reject outright on rehearing. As it did when considering the DTE contracts to service the Oracle and Open AI data center in Saline, the MPSC also ignored in this case significant transmission costs identified by the Attorney General that DTE has refused to account for in its contracts and assessments. For these reasons, and more articulated within the petition, the Attorney General asserts the MPSC's order demonstrates a litany of errors, such as by applying an incorrect burden of proof and an incorrect standard of review, by failing to meaningfully engage with or outright ignoring important arguments from the Attorney General's briefing, and by repeatedly defaulting to acceptance of DTE's proposed terms despite DTE's failures to support the reasonableness and prudence of those terms. The consequence of these errors, argues Attorney General Nessel, is the imposition of mistaken and unnecessary cost-shifting risks onto Michigan ratepayers. The Attorney General argues that, given DTE's repeated failure throughout the contested case to meet its burden of proof under Michigan law, the MPSC must adopt on rehearing the recommendations made in her petition or instead reject the contracts outright.

artigo.texto: Microsoft pressiona Trump contra veto a componentes chineses para data centers | Vero NotíciasMicrosoft pressiona Trump contra veto a componentes chineses para data centers A Microsoft pressiona o governo de Donald Trump a abandonar os planos de proibir a importação de transceptores ópticos chineses, componentes essenciais para data centers de inteligência artificial. A empresa alerta que a medida pode atrasar a expansão da infraestrutura tecnológica dos EUA. A gigante de tecnologia possui 35 data centers em construção e outros 134 planejados no país. A empresa argumenta que a proibição pode comprometer a cadeia de suprimentos e deixar chips de IA sem utilização por falta de componentes para conectá-los. O governo americano avalia o veto por preocupações de segurança nacional, incluindo riscos de espionagem e ataques cibernéticos atribuídos à China. A Comissão Federal de Comunicações (FCC) trabalha na restrição, enquanto empresas do setor alertam para possíveis prejuízos à competitividade. O bitcoin recuava 1,94% nesta terça-feira (10), a US$ 73.570, às 17h15, segundo a Binance. Durante o dia, atingiu o menor nível desde agosto. O ethereum caía 3,93%, cotado a US$ 2.051,06. A queda ocorreu após dados de inflação dos Estados Unidos reforçarem expectativas de aumento dos juros em dezembro. Antes da divulgação, o diretor do Federal Reserve, Christopher Waller, havia defendido considerar uma alta de 0,5 ponto percentual. O dólar comercial subiu 1,48% nesta terça-feira (10) e fechou a R$ 5,58, maior cotação de 2026. A moeda norte-americana também atingiu o patamar mais elevado desde 31 de julho de 2025. A alta ocorreu após a inflação ao consumidor dos Estados Unidos avançar 0,4% em outubro, acima dos 0,3% esperados pelo mercado. O indicador influencia as decisões do Federal Reserve sobre os juros americanos. A operação pode avaliar a desenvolvedora de IA em aproximadamente US$ 1,03 trilhão. A companhia colocou à venda cerca de 801,4 milhões de ações da Classe A. A avaliação total considera também outras classes de papéis e a possibilidade de compras adicionais pelos bancos responsáveis pela oferta. Deputados afirmaram nesta terça-feira (10), após reunião com o ministro da Fazenda, Dario Durigan, que não há negociação para adiar a reforma tributária. Segundo eles, o governo mantém o início da CBS em janeiro de 2027. O presidente da Frente Parlamentar do Empreendedorismo, deputado Joaquim Passarinho (PL-PA), disse que a prioridade é implementar a mudança. A CBS substituirá PIS e Cofins, enquanto a CNI defende adiar o início para 2028. A Petrobras registrou lucro líquido de R$ 39,75 bilhões no terceiro trimestre de 2026, alta de 21,5% na comparação anual. O balanço foi divulgado nesta terça-feira (10). A receita da estatal somou R$ 169,3 bilhões, crescimento de 32,4% em relação ao mesmo período de 2025. A produção de petróleo também avançou, com aumento de 11,9%.

artigo.texto: TREX Energy, an Indian energy storage solutions company, has inaugurated its lithium battery manufacturing facility at E-City, Raviryal, Maheshwaram, Hyderabad. The facility is equipped with a 12 PPM automatic module assembly line designed to manufacture 52S battery packs for energy storage applications, including 261 kWh configurations and 5 MWh systems. The new facility marks an important step in the company’s efforts to strengthen domestic manufacturing capabilities and address India’s growing demand for Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS). With renewable energy adoption expanding across the country, energy storage solutions are becoming increasingly important for managing fluctuations in power supply, supporting peak-load requirements and providing reliable backup across residential, commercial, industrial and utility-scale applications. The automated assembly line, with a production capability of 12 parts per minute, is designed to improve manufacturing efficiency, consistency and quality control. It will support the production of battery modules and packs for TREX Energy’s portfolio of energy storage solutions, ranging from 5 kWh to 5 MWh. Bharat S Chhittarka, Director, TREX Energy, said, “We’re focused on reducing financing costs to make BESS more affordable and reliable for the Indian market. Energy must be available when it’s needed, and BESS is a key solution.” Roshan Shaik, Technical Director, TREX Energy, said the 12 PPM automatic module assembly line would strengthen the company’s manufacturing capabilities and enable efficient, consistent production. He added that the facility would support scalable energy storage solutions for India’s expanding market requirements. TREX Energy’s product portfolio caters to a wide range of applications. Its Commercial and Industrial (C&I) BESS solutions are designed for factories, offices and commercial establishments seeking to manage energy consumption, improve operational resilience and access backup power. Its utility-scale systems address requirements associated with grid applications and large renewable energy projects. The company also offers residential energy storage systems, home inverter batteries and customised battery packs. As part of its expansion plans, TREX Energy is preparing to establish a second manufacturing facility in Madhya Pradesh. The Madhya Pradesh Government has allotted four acres of land to the company for the proposed Phase 2 facility. Further details on its production capacity, development schedule and commissioning will be announced in due course. The Hyderabad facility reflects TREX Energy’s focus on developing local manufacturing and technology capabilities to serve India’s evolving energy storage ecosystem. Through its expanding product range and planned investments, the company aims to support energy storage adoption across homes, businesses and large infrastructure projects. TREX Energy is a Hyderabad-based energy storage solutions company focused on designing and delivering Battery Energy Storage Systems for commercial, industrial and utility applications. Operating under the tagline “We Store Electrons”, the company aims to support India’s clean energy transition through reliable and intelligent energy storage technologies. It has registered offices in Hyderabad, Telangana, and Pune, Maharashtra.

artigo.texto: Karpowership acquires UK 100MWh BESS site for development The Turkish renewable energy company has bought a fully consented plot near Birmingham in the UK's Midlands for a 100MWh BESS installation. Anglo Renewables has sold a fully consented 50MW/100MWh battery energy storage system (BESS) project near Birmingham to Kinetics Energies for an undisclosed sum. The 2-hour project, dubbed Kitwell, is expected to connect to the grid in 2028. Northamptonshire-based Anglo Renewables is a micro-business (having a turnover of less than £1 million annually) that enters into agreements with landowners and steers appropriate permitting for change of land use and planning permission for battery energy storage system or solar PV installations. In the case of the Kitwell site, it is presumed any agreement between the landowner and Anglo Renewables passes to Kinetics Energies, part of Karpowership, the Turkish energy group. The head of commercial at Karpowership and CEO of Kinetics Energies, Mehmet Katmer, said: "Battery storage has an important role to play in keeping the grid flexible and reliable, and we look forward to delivering an operating BESS project as part of our strategy to deliver 800MW of low and zero carbon assets across Europe." In England and Wales, BESS sites are not considered to be nationally significant infrastructure regardless of their size, and permission for development is subject to approval by the relevant local planning authority. artigo.texto: Ohio Chamber study: Data centers added more than $9B to state economy in 2025 COLUMBUS, Ohio (WSYX) — Ohio’s growing data center industry added more than $9 billion to the state’s economy last year, according to a new study commissioned by the Ohio Chamber of Commerce. The study found that data centers and the construction needed to build them supported nearly 70,000 jobs in Ohio last year. About 14,000 people work directly in the data center industry, with average pay and benefits of about $148,000 a year, the report said. Looking ahead, the study estimated that planned construction and equipment spending through 2030 could support more than 257,000 jobs for a year. The report also examined the fiscal impact of incentives and investment tied to the industry. It said the state gave up more than $1.5 billion in tax revenue, but that the investment has generated a $2.7 billion fiscal surplus.

artigo.texto: Statesboro’s city government, through City Attorney Cain Smith, filed a response Oct. 19-21 in Bulloch County Superior Court to a lawsuit seeking to reverse the city’s Aug. 18 rezoning of a 27-acre tract on Burkhalter Road to “O” or office at the request of data center developers. Meanwhile, Smith says that processing by the city of any further application by the property owner and potential developer, 4AM Development LLC, for a special use permit required for a data center “would continue to be stayed.” In other words, unless the court upholds the zoning or until it issues some other go-ahead, the mayor and council apparently won’t be holding a hearing to consider issuing a permit, even if 4AM Development, whose publicly identified partners are Bobby Bagwell and Charles C. Way, try to submit a completed application. The Data Centers Ordinance, enacted in June by a 3-1 vote of City Council as an amendment to the Statesboro Unified Development Code, allows data centers as a special use in four non-residential zoning classifications. However, “special use” means that a data center will not be automatically allowed. Instead, plans for any particular site must meet special requirements for a permit to be issued by the council on a majority vote. Way and Bagwell, whose company reportedly includes two other investors, propose locating a 230,000-square-foot data center on the site at 6539 Burkhalter Road, and have applied to Georgia Power for an up to 99-megawatt electrical supply. City Council’s Aug. 18 vote approving the rezoning from “R-4” high-density residential to “O” was 3-2, including the mayor’s tiebreaker. Original complaint But on Sept. 17, the nonprofit organization Coastal Communities United and 11 named individuals, including some adjacent property owners and other nearby residents, filed a petition in the county Superior Court for review of the rezoning and a declaratory judgment against the city’s action. Although worded in some ways like a standard lawsuit, the “petition for review” signed by attorney Robert Abney Fricks Sr. of Warner Robins identified his clients as petitioners rather than plaintiffs. But it named both the city, as a municipal corporation, and 4AM Development as defendants. It asserted that the petitioners would suffer damages “to be determined” but asserted no monetary amounts. In the closing paragraphs of the 30-page complaint, the petitioners asked that the court declare the city zoning decision “invalid, void or stricken.” Citing a provision of state law, the complaint also asserts that filing such a challenge should “stay all legal proceedings in furtherance of the action.” 4AM’s previous answer As previously reported, 4 AM Development LLC, though William J. Keogh III, of the Augusta-based Hull Barrett law firm, then replied with an Oct. 6 "motion to dismiss and request for expedited hearing.” Points of that motion were reported by the Statesboro Herald in an Oct. 12 story. At that time city officials had not filed a separate answer, but Smith said the city would have to do so or face a “default judgment” and would answer by a 30-day deadline from having been served notice of the suit. Notice had been served Sept. 21 at City Hall. The city’s answer, signed by Smith as submitted to the court Oct. 19 and stamped at the clerk of court’s office Oct. 21, runs to 16 pages. It parallels the 4AM Development response in some ways, such as by asserting that the nonprofit organization and the 11 property owners or neighbors at various distances from the site lack legal standing to challenge the zoning decision. The city’s answer But the city’s response differs from the developers’ in other ways, such as by asserting a defense of sovereign immunity. The city’s “first defense” is simply: “The Petition fails to state a claim upon which relief can be granted and thus should be dismissed.” The “second defense” is that the petitioners allegedly lack standing. “Petitioner Coastal Community United should be dismissed from this action,” Smith has asserted in the city’s written answer. “An organization cannot obtain standing merely by asserting its members’ rights. It must establish a cognizable violation of its own rights under an available standing theory.” He cites the 2025 opinion of the Georgia Supreme Court in a case called Republican National Committee v. Eternal Vigilance Action Inc. in support of this. Smith then cites the state high court in a different decision, from 2006, as holding “that a plaintiff cannot avoid zoning-standing requirements merely by seeking equitable relief or asserting an interest in enforcing zoning laws.” The city’s fourth defense, the one claiming sovereign immunity, is aimed at an assertion in the petitioners’ complaint that the rezoning decision amounts to an “inverse condemnation” by reduction of nearby property values. “Petitioners do not allege and cannot show that private property has been taken for public use, nor does the City maintain any control or interest in the rezoned property; the city is therefore immune from claims for inverse condemnation,” the answer asserts. The city’s “fourth defense” briefly echoes a point of the developers’ motion, that petitioners “are barred from making a Constitutional attack for the first time before the Superior Court.” In other words, the defendants assert that the citizens should have stated a constitutional basis for their objections during the rezoning hearings. But then the city’s “fifth defense” claims that the petitioners’ complaints “are not ripe for adjudication” because the data center project “cannot be undertaken without the issuance of a special use permit by the Mayor and Council.” The city’s answer continues through 12 stated “defenses,” most very short and direct. But the 12th goes on to list 115 specific points from the petitioners’ complaints as “denied” or “admitted.” It ends with a request to the court dismiss the petition and require the petitioners to pay all costs of the act

artigo.texto: Publicidade O Ministério das Comunicações informou nesta segunda-feira (9) que o governo federal planeja investir R$ 46,3 milhões no desenvolvimento de uma plataforma de gerenciamento e distribuição de dados entre mini data centers no Brasil. Batizado de Prisma, o projeto utilizará inteligência artificial para identificar onde e como os dados devem ser processados, distribuindo automaticamente os recursos computacionais entre diferentes infraestruturas. Na prática, o Executivo espera que a tecnologia reduza gastos com energia e custos operacionais, acelere o acesso às informações e aumente a proteção de dados estratégicos. Os recursos serão administrados pela Financiadora de Estudos e Projetos (Finep), e o projeto será executado pelo Centro Brasileiro de Inovação em Tecnologias da Informação e da Comunicação (CPQD). O prazo de execução é de 36 meses, a partir da celebração do convênio de pesquisa, desenvolvimento e inovação entre a Finep e o CPQD. O ministro das Comunicações, Frederico Filho, afirmou que o projeto possibilitará maior autonomia e soberania no tratamento de dados no País. “Investir em tecnologia nacional é garantir que o Brasil tenha mais autonomia para proteger suas informações e desenvolver soluções para os desafios do futuro. Estamos fortalecendo a inovação brasileira e criando condições para uma infraestrutura digital mais moderna, segura e sustentável, reduzindo nossa dependência de tecnologias desenvolvidas no exterior”, afirmou em nota.

artigo.texto: Analysis: One of the biggest challenges when it comes to wind and solar power is how to store this energy for later use Energy storage is arguably the biggest challenge in green energy adoption. It is critical if we are to balance our national grid and reduce dependency on imported energy. Currently, we are wasting 15% of green energy produced in Ireland, which is enough to power 660,000 homes. This is primarily caused by high generation of wind farms at night when demand is low. This creates a problem that is simple in concept, but extremely challenging at a national grid level: how do we store this energy for later use? Ireland has some examples of success in this regard. We have created multiple large scale batteries including pumped hydro storage in the Wicklow mountains and one of the world's largest fly wheel systems at Moneypoint in Clare. These types of storage differ from the lithium-ion batteries that power most of our devices. They essentially store energy by moving mass. Both have different strengths and weaknesses, but if we are to meet our emissions targets and secure our energy security more storage using different forms of technology is needed. Rust battery A recently launched project in partnership with US company Form Energy and Irish company FuturEnergy will use a new approach to storage in the form of the Ballynahone Energy Storage iron-air battery project. The battery system will be located southwest of Buncrana, near the Trillick substation in Co Donegal and will create 1,000 MWh which could power approximately 87,000 homes for 24 hours. While grid scale battery systems are not unusual, the technology used in Donegal is unique and very different to more common lithium ion systems. This battery technology, in the simplest terms, is able to draw electricity from iron as it rusts (oxidises). Recharging the battery reverses this chemical reaction. Please review their details and accept them to load the content.Manage Preferences From RTÉ Radio 1's Morning Ireland, why the move to renewable energy has been so slow? Because the battery is mainly made of iron, air and water they are very cheap to manufacture and easy to recycle at end of life, which is approximately 20 to 30 years of use. The graph compares the cost of different energy storage technologies per kilowatt-hour, highlighting a wide range of expenses across various systems. Iron-air batteries by Form Energy emerge as the most cost-effective option at an estimated €30 per kWh, while standard lithium-ion (LFP) and pumped hydro systems occupy the mid-range. In stark contrast, mechanical flywheels stand out as significantly more expensive than the rest, but are useful in specific grid balancing applications. The very low cost of storage makes this look like the ideal solution. So what's the catch? As with all technological solutions, there are advantages and disadvantages. These need to be carefully considered, especially when technology has not yet been widely proven beyond manufacturer testing. One of the main draw backs for iron air batteries is the amount of energy lost during a charge and discharge cycle. This is often referred to as round trip efficiency. Early reports suggest that iron air can achieve approximately 50% efficiency which means that half the electricity used to charge the battery is lost. By comparison, lithium ion can achieve 85-95% efficiency in grid scale use and pumped hydro can achieve approximately 75% efficiency. Iron air also has a lower discharge rate than lithium ion. It is designed to discharge over 50 to 100 hours. You could consider iron air like a tractor that can draw a large load of electricity to the grid slowly, where lithium ion is the expensive sports car that can get there quickly, but with a much smaller load. These are two very different technologies used for different energy needs. Both of these battery types, in addition to a wide range of other energy storage devices, will be needed in order to create a reliable green energy system that can cope with intermittent generation. We urgently need to develop more wind and solar, but without supporting storage systems like the project in Donegal we will not be in a position to reduce our dependence on fossil fuel generation that is currently the primary solution to intermittent energy generation. While the round trip efficiency issue remains, it is important to remember that oil and gas electricity generation ranges from 40-60% efficient and results in considerable CO2 emissions. No energy generation or storage option is perfect, and we cannot afford to allow perfect to be the enemy of the good when it comes to securing Ireland’s energy independence.
