artigo.texto: ZTE Powers High Efficiency AIDC with Robust Energy Infrastructure AI's growth depends on stable, efficient, green energy—the foundation powering every model training run and inference call. November 11, 2026 Sponsored by ZTE As the AI wave surges forward, computing power is reshaping industries at an unprecedented pace. Yet behind every model training run and every inference call, what truly sustains continuous computing output is a stable, efficient, and green energy foundation. As per-rack power consumption climbs from 10–20 kW to 100 kW, 600 kW, and even 1 MW, as air cooling approaches its engineering limits and losses in traditional power supply links become increasingly prominent, the benchmark for AIDC competition is shifting from "computing scale" to "computing efficiency". In this "energy efficiency battle" crucial to the sustainable development of computing power, ZTE is reconstructing the "energy foundation" of AIDC with a systematic approach—ensuring every kilowatt-hour is converted into tokens more efficiently. Computing Power Sprints Ahead, Electricity Becomes a "Scarce Resource" Computing demand is growing explosively, and electricity consumption in computing centers is rising rapidly. The problem goes far beyond total electricity use: traditional data centers typically have a per-rack power consumption of 10–20 kW, while in the AIDC era, high-density deployment of GPU clusters has become the norm. Per-rack loads are quickly exceeding 100 kW, and high-end intelligent computing scenarios can reach 600 kW or even 1 MW. The shortcomings of traditional power supply architectures are now exposed: significant losses occur across the multi-stage conversion chain from transformer to server, resulting in extra annual operating costs. Such architectures can no longer meet the needs of high-density racks, making power supply architecture innovation urgent. Cooling challenges are equally severe: the engineering limit of air cooling is approximately 20–30 kW per rack, beyond which cooling capacity drops sharply. When the heat flux density of GPU clusters far exceeds the boundaries of air cooling, liquid cooling is no longer an "option" but a "mainstream solution"—the core guarantee for high-value computing power to operate stably at full load. The competitive benchmark for AIDC is shifting from "computing scale" to "computing efficiency". The long-term development of AI computing power increasingly depends on the upper limit of energy supply and on the end-to-end conversion efficiency from Energy to Token. This is precisely the core proposition ZTE is addressing. 800V High-Voltage DC System: Tackling Power Loss from the Source ZTE's first answer is the 800V high-voltage DC system, a fundamental innovation in traditional power supply architecture. With an efficient topology design, DC/DC intelligent battery management, diverse application modes, and excellent scalability, it delivers high-density, high-efficiency, green, and reliable DC power supply, solving the core power supply challenges of high-density computing infrastructure. Intelligent management has also achieved a leap forward: it supports one-stop full-link management and full-system visibility and controllability, covering functions such as fault recording, temperature measurement at key locations, and selective protection simulation. Predictive maintenance is carried out across three levels—module faults, system faults, and battery lifespan—making O&M more worry-free. Relying on dual-standard compatibility and modular elastic design, the system can flexibly switch voltage standards (±400V/800V), supporting smooth transition between old and new scenarios. Capacity can be expanded on demand, reducing initial investment pressure. It fully covers centralized large-scale computing bases and distributed edge computing upgrade scenarios, meeting the needs of all types of customers, including operators, internet companies, and professional computing power investors. Megawatt-Level Liquid Cooling CDU: Innovation Breaks Through the "Thermal" Ceiling While efficiency on the power supply side leaps forward, the cooling side also requires capability reconstruction. ZTE has launched a cold plate liquid cooling CDU to achieve optimal cooling costs across the full lifecycle and all-weather cooling safety assurance for equipment rooms. The CDU has a single-unit cooling capacity of 1.5 MW, expandable to 2.4 MW, with flexible configuration of 2–5 CDU cabinets. Auxiliary modules can be selected on demand and upgraded as business grows, greatly reducing initial investment and later retrofit waste. Based on the integration of multiple sensors for flow, pressure, temperature, and more, the 1500 kW liquid cooling CDU achieves precise temperature control of ±0.5°C and pressure control of ±0.05 bar, ensuring stable operation of high-density equipment. It is equipped with health indicators and status visualization for intelligent O&M, and features multiple safety designs such as N+X redundant hot backup and dual power feeds, supporting 7×24-hour uninterrupted operation. The combination of 800V high-voltage DC and the 1500 kW liquid cooling CDU outlines an efficient "inbound" and "outbound" channel for AIDC: the power supply side delivers every kilowatt-hour to the server with minimum loss, while the cooling side expels heat with maximum efficiency, keeping PUE stably within 1.15. Real-world application is the only benchmark for validating technological effectiveness. The Nanjing Binjiang Data Center was among the first to deliver demonstration results from its upgrade and transformation: It implemented a liquid-cooling integrated solution with a power density of up to 60 kW, adopting high-efficiency HVDC power distribution and busway, 32°C air supply, and group control optimization, achieving a PUE of only 1.15. artigo.texto: Funttel destina R$ 46,3 milhões ao CPQD para desenvolver tecnologia nacional de data centers Projeto Prisma, do Funttel, terá duração de 36 meses e usará inteligência artificial para distribuir processamento entre data centers. O Conselho Gestor do Fundo para o Desenvolvimento Tecnológico das Telecomunicações (Funttel) aprovou na sexta, 6, um investimento de R$ 46,3 milhões no desenvolvimento de uma plataforma nacional de gerenciamento de data centers e infraestruturas de processamento distribuído. O projeto, denominado Prisma, será executado pelo CPQD, com recursos administrados pela Financiadora de Estudos e Projetos (Finep). A iniciativa prevê o uso de inteligência artificial para definir onde os dados deverão ser processados e distribuir recursos computacionais entre diferentes instalações, incluindo mini data centers localizados em diversas regiões do país. O projeto terá duração de 36 meses, contados a partir da celebração do convênio de pesquisa, desenvolvimento e inovação entre o CPQD e a Finep. O comunicado não informa a data prevista para a assinatura do instrumento. A proposta busca desenvolver uma tecnologia nacional capaz de gerenciar ambientes distribuídos de processamento, com aplicações previstas em telecomunicações, saúde, defesa, segurança pública e educação. Inteligência artificial para distribuir processamento O Prisma utilizará inteligência artificial para identificar a infraestrutura mais adequada ao processamento de dados e realizar a distribuição dos recursos computacionais entre diferentes instalações. Uma das frentes do projeto é o uso de mini data centers em arquiteturas de computação de borda (edge computing), nas quais parte do processamento ocorre mais perto dos locais de geração e utilização das informações. Essa arquitetura permite reduzir a distância percorrida pelos dados entre os dispositivos e os centros de processamento, com potencial para diminuir o tempo de resposta de aplicações digitais. Para o diretor de Tecnologia e Inovação do CPQD, Gustavo Correa Lima, o processamento distribuído também permite ampliar o controle sobre as informações mantidas nessas estruturas. “Além de tornar mais rápidos o processamento e o acesso às informações, essa arquitetura permite maior controle sobre o dado que está na borda”, afirmou. No setor de telecomunicações, a plataforma está prevista entre as soluções que poderão utilizar infraestrutura distribuída de processamento. Eficiência energética e continuidade dos serviços Outro objetivo do Prisma é desenvolver mecanismos para reduzir o consumo de energia e o impacto ambiental dos data centers. A proposta contempla o gerenciamento de recursos computacionais e soluções de armazenamento de energia elétrica para ampliar a autonomia das instalações em situações de instabilidade no fornecimento. Entre os resultados esperados estão a redução da pegada de carbono, o aumento da resiliência a falhas de energia e a proteção contra ataques cibernéticos. O projeto também prevê mecanismos de governança de informações críticas, observando padrões internacionais de segurança e as diretrizes da Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados Pessoais (LGPD). Funttel financiará desenvolvimento tecnológico Os recursos foram aprovados pelo Conselho Gestor do Funttel, fundo vinculado à política de desenvolvimento tecnológico das telecomunicações e cuja atuação envolve o Ministério das Comunicações. A Finep ficará responsável pela gestão financeira dos recursos, enquanto o CPQD executará as atividades de pesquisa, desenvolvimento e inovação previstas no projeto. Segundo a superintendente da Área de Saúde e Transformação Digital da Finep, Joana Meirelles, a proposta é disponibilizar uma plataforma nacional para aplicações em diferentes setores. “O objetivo é desenvolver e disponibilizar uma plataforma nacional segura e sustentável para setores como saúde, defesa, segurança pública, educação e telecomunicações”, afirmou. O ministro das Comunicações, Frederico de Siqueira Filho, relacionou o investimento à ampliação da capacidade nacional de desenvolvimento tecnológico e à soberania nacional. “Com o apoio do Funttel, estamos fortalecendo a inovação brasileira e criando condições para uma infraestrutura digital mais moderna, segura e sustentável, reduzindo nossa dependência de tecnologias desenvolvidas no exterior”, afirma o ministro das Comunicações, Frederico de Siqueira Filho. *Com assessoria de imprensa

artigo.texto: Hannah Pingree says she wants strict rules in place before data centers are built in Maine JAY (WGME) -- Developers of a proposed data center in the town of Jay say they've submitted permit applications to the Department of Environmental Protection. The local developer and its national partner, Sentinel Data Systems, have revived plans to replace the closed paper mill in Jay with a $550 million AI data center. However, Governor-Elect Hannah Pingree says strict rules must be in place before any data centers are built in Maine. "We have talked about implementing a moratorium until we have rules in place to protect ratepayers, to protect the environment and ensure community benefits. And that will continue to be my position," Pingree said. "The development of data centers in Maine without very strong regulations in place is not something that people are interested in." Developers plan to hold a public meeting next month in Jay to talk about the project. The governor-elect says she looks forward to learning more from the town and the developer about the proposed data center.

artigo.texto: O Partido Democrata assumirá o controle do Congresso e da maioria dos governos estaduais nos EUA em janeiro de 2026, após vencer as eleições de meio de mandato. A nova maioria planeja uma ofensiva rigorosa contra a expansão de data centers, inteligência artificial e as grandes empresas de tecnologia (big techs), motivada por preocupações com o meio ambiente e os altos custos de energia da rede elétrica. Quais são as principais medidas planejadas contra os data centers? Parlamentares democratas pretendem exigir que os operadores de grandes data centers arquem com uma fatia maior dos custos de melhorias na rede elétrica. Um projeto de lei em andamento visa agilizar novas usinas, mas impõe responsabilidades financeiras diretas às empresas. Além disso, nomes influentes, como o senador Bernie Sanders, defendem uma moratória nacional para impedir a construção de novas unidades. O argumento central é que essas estruturas consomem energia de forma desproporcional e podem prejudicar os consumidores comuns e o meio ambiente se não houver um controle rígido. Como a inteligência artificial será afetada pelas novas regras? A agenda democrata prioriza uma pausa no desenvolvimento de sistemas de inteligência artificial avançada e a proibição da chamada superinteligência. Deputados e senadores articulam propostas que exigem auditorias independentes para esses sistemas e formas de responsabilizar as empresas por eventuais danos causados pela tecnologia. Parlamentares reeleitos já sinalizaram que o primeiro dia do novo Congresso será marcado por intimações contra executivos das big techs, forçando o setor a prestar contas sobre o impacto de suas inovações na segurança nacional e na estabilidade social. Qual é a posição de Donald Trump sobre essas restrições tecnológicas? O presidente Donald Trump critica duramente as propostas da oposição e alega que esse cerco regulatório pode fazer os Estados Unidos perderem a corrida tecnológica para a China. Para o republicano, frear o avanço de data centers e da inteligência artificial é um erro estratégico que compromete a competitividade americana no cenário global. Após a vitória democrata nas midterms, que resultou em queda nas ações de empresas de tecnologia, Trump responsabilizou os eleitores, afirmando que a culpa pela instabilidade do mercado e pelo possível atraso tecnológico do país recai sobre eles. Existe o risco de as novas regras favorecerem a China? Analistas econômicos alertam que o fator decisivo na disputa com a China não é apenas o software, mas a capacidade computacional e a oferta de energia. Se a regulamentação se tornar uma barreira que impeça sistematicamente a construção de infraestrutura, os EUA podem perder espaço. Embora os democratas defendam que a fiscalização garante concorrência e segurança, o risco real é transformar leis em restrições de oferta. Caso o investimento seja desestimulado, a China poderá conquistar uma vantagem competitiva difícil de reverter, já que depende de energia e hardware para liderar a IA. artigo.texto: A City-County Council committee voted 11-2 Monday to recommend the full council reject about $113 million in tax breaks for data center developer DC Blox. The company previously won approval to build a two building campus on Indianapolis’ east side. The recommendation is not binding. The full council, which must also approve the tax abatements, is expected to vote in December. More than two dozen people spoke at the meeting in council chambers — nearly all opposed the tax deal. Indy Economic Development CEO Andrea Richter-Garry, whose organization negotiated the deal for the city, told the committee the project would bring in about $58 million to the local community during the abatement period: roughly $28 million in taxes plus the company’s $30 million pledge. DC Blox has not fully committed to building the $1.8 billion data center project at 305 Fintail Drive near Irvington. Asked by Councilor Andy Nielsen whether it would build the first building without the abatements, David Armistead, the company's senior vice president of sales, said it has no full tenant commitments on that building and none on the second, citing a court challenge to its land use approval. The Atlanta-based company said the project is planned to be built in two phases — a one-story, 70,000-square-foot building expected to be completed within two years, followed by a two-story, 250,000-square-foot building, in the next five years. The development would create hundreds of temporary construction jobs and 21 permanent positions. Data centers have become a major target of Indiana's economic development strategy, but the industry's need for electricity has put it at odds with a separate fight over rising utility costs. Gov. Mike Braun signed a law this year aimed at reining in utility rates, and critics argue large-scale power consumers like data centers make that harder. Members of the council’s Metropolitan and Economic Development Committee considered two abatements: a 10-year, 50% break on real property taxes on land and buildings, and a 10-year, 85% break on personal property taxes on high-tech equipment like servers. The site of the data center is on the border of two districts represented by two members of the City-County Council — Nielsen and Michael-Paul Hart. Nielsen rejected the plan. “The presentation we got is clear as mud,” he said. “It is speculative.” If the project is built as planned, the company said it would still pay about $28 million in property taxes during the abatement period. It also pledges $30 million for east side projects on top of the local taxes, including park and trail upgrades, a fire station and $5.7 million in redevelopment of Washington Square Mall. Councilor Hart, who sponsored the proposals, said the vote is about east side investment, not whether to allow a data center, which the Metropolitan Development Commission already approved. “You see convention centers in Noblesville and in Fishers — all those things are starting to take the people away from Indianapolis because we're not investing in our townships,” he said. “We're going to become a downtown of nothing if we don’t start doing it.” Residents who testified opposed the breaks. Sue Beecher, president of the Irvington Community Council, said the group voted unanimously against any abatements. Others cited concerns over contamination or said the company could afford to build the campus without tax breaks. DC Blox is one of three data centers in the city approved before the Metropolitan Development Commission voted in August to temporarily ban new developments in Marion County through 2027. The other approved centers are Sabey Data Centers’ $4.3 billion project in Decatur Township, which received more than $240 million in tax breaks in September, and Metrobloks’ project in Martindale-Brightwood. artigo.texto: Changan and CATL to collaborate on 1,500 km solid state cells, establish 75 GWh battery lines Chinese automaker Changan has officially announced plans to deepen its partnership with battery giant CATL. The two firms have committed to expanding joint battery production capacity to 75 GWh and collaborating on solid-state batteries (SSBs) and sodium-ion cells. Like its previous statements on its in-house SSBs, Changan made its announcement on an interactive platform owned by the Shenzhen Stock Exchange. The automaker also expressed commitment to prospective industries, including humanoid robots and China’s “low-altitude economy”. More cells with CATL Changan and CATL are not new partners in China’s automotive sector, having established a joint venture (JV), CATL-Changan (时代长安, Times Changan), earlier in 2023. The JV supplies cells to Changan’s in-house NEV brands, including Avatr, Deepal, and Nevo. Libattery.net, a Chinese battery industry outlet, reports that CATL-Changan is on track to reach 50 GWh of battery production capacity, a plan Changan revealed at an investor relations event in May 2025. The announcement means CATL-Changan will receive an additional 25 GWh of capacity and new production lines. The JV plans to establish a 700,000-square-meter facility and invest 5 billion yuan (~750 million USD) in the expansion. According to Changan, the new facility will integrate the “latest generation of CATL battery tech” and supply cells to the automaker’s NEV brands. It’s planned to start operations in 2027 and meet the 25 GWh goal in three years. It will be situated in a high-tech zone between Chongqing City and Sichuan Province. The automaker expects the expansion to bring in annual revenue of 10 billion yuan (~1.5 billion USD), create 2,500 jobs, and generate 300 million yuan (~45 million USD) in tax revenue for the local community. Changan may also see this move as a way to cut costs. ZAKER News, a Chinese automotive outlet, reports that the Chongqing-based automaker is only earning 68 yuan (10 USD) per car, and is under heavy pressure to boost profits. A JV with CATL would give it access to cheap in-house cells, and avoid high acquisition costs for battery packs,which is one of the priciest components in an NEV. More on Changan’s SSBs Changan has joined the race for SSBs in China, announcing its Golden Bell (Jinzhongzhao) cells in November 2023. The automaker says it’s aiming for an energy density of 400 Wh/kg and claims it will be 70% safer than rivals because it uses “AI remote diagnosis technology”. It also claims the new Golden Bell cells will help EVs reach ranges over 1,500 km and says cell degradation won’t be noticeable for at least 600,000 km. Cell life will exceed 5,000 cycles, and Golden Bell packs will support 6C charging, enabling a 30-80% charge in 9 minutes. The automaker has also reiterated its development schedule for the Golden Bell cells, aiming for vehicle road tests in 2026 and ramping up to commercial production in 2027. artigo.texto: Fort Worth leaders receive data center recommendations that could lead to moratorium on development FORT WORTH, Texas - Fort Worth leaders could put a temporary moratorium on data center developments as the city learns how to manage the industry's growing impact. Fort Worth data center moratorium Local perspective: On Tuesday, November 10, the Fort Worth Data Center & Infrastructure Commission, a commission appointed by the Fort Worth City Council in August, delivered recommendations on data center development in the city. The commission gave 19 recommendations in total after studying four areas of data center development: electricity, water use, land use and neighborhood impacts, and economic impacts. Some of the commission's recommendations include: - Requiring closed-loop cooling systems to recirculate water rather than draw in new water - Increase the distance from homes to data centers from 50 feet to 350 feet - Enforce noise regulations on data centers The recommendations could lead to a 90-day moratorium on data center development in the city, something that has been in the works since the committee was created in August. Such a moratorium would allow the city to review the commission's recommendations and decide whether changes are needed to the city's zoning rules and development codes. You can find the commission's full report below. No action was taken on the commission's findings at Tuesday's meeting. What they're saying: Michael Slattery, the chair of the commission, tells FOX 4's Vania Castillo these recommendations would give the city a "roadmap" on how to move forward with data centers. "It would give data center developers much more certainty. It's certainly not going to please everybody, and I think ever does. And I think that I think it starts to put some certainty around how to move this forward," Slattery said. Some residents at Tuesday's city council meeting said the recommendations don't go far enough. "Two months is not enough time to consider all of the issues involved with a data center," resident Julie Waters said. "Today, you have an opportunity to save your seat in the next election. Listen to the cries of your people who have come before you, meeting after meeting, asking for a moratorium. If not for your people, then for then at least to wipe away the stain of corruption on your reputation and legacy." The backstory: Fort Worth leaders have been considering their position on data center development since this past summer. In early July, Fort Worth's zoning commission voted against new restrictions on future data center projects in the city, citing the need for more information on the rapidly-changing industry. Several days later, five Fort Worth City Council members called for a moratorium on data center construction. They say the pause would allow the city to discuss and refine regulations on data centers. That call led to the creation of the committee that gave today's findings. Fort Worth currently has four operating data centers, with at least four more in development. What's next: Fort Worth city staff say the next public hearing is planned for January 12, 2027. The earliest a data center moratorium could be enacted is February 2027. Officials noted that existing sites and projects already moving through the application pipeline would be exempt from the moratorium if the policy is formally adopted next year. The Source: Information in this story comes from a Fort Worth City Council meeting and previous FOX 4 reporting.

artigo.texto: Hazle Township residents press for tougher data center zoning limits on revised ordinance HAZLE TOWNSHIP, LUZERNE CO. (WOLF) — A packed auditorium at Hazleton Area High School Monday night, as Hazle Township residents voiced their concerns over a proposed 40-page zoning ordinance that could determine where data centers are allowed to be built. Township supervisors are considering revisions to the ordinance, including a designated overlay district for data center developments. But the proposal is drawing pushback from residents who say they want a say in how these projects could impact their community. The township recently posted an updated version of its proposed data center ordinance, dated November 5, along with a map showing a proposed area called the Energy and Technology Overlay District. Under the proposal, data centers would be allowed within that designated area without needing a special exception from the zoning hearing board. However, developers would still have to meet township requirements and obtain the necessary approvals. Residents raised concerns and suggested stronger protections, focusing on noise levels, decibel limits, and potential environmental impacts. The proposed data center zoning amendment would allow the residential setback requirement to be reduced to 500 feet. One resident spoke out in favor of increasing the setback requirement to provide greater protection for nearby residents. “The 1,250 feet requirement should be enforced, if this is going to go through. 500 feet is not enough to protect property and or people from the noise, the pollution, and the activities of an active data center area,” said Margaret. Another resident stressed the importance of giving residents a voice before any decisions are made on the amendment. “We believe residents deserve a meaningful opportunity to understand, question, and discuss the proposed regulations,” said Michael Reilly. One resident cited a statistic that 71% of people oppose local AI data centers, questioning why Project Hazelnut is still being considered and referencing a recent debate involving Governor Shapiro. “Governor Shapiro stood up at his debate, and say any community that’s not for this, they will not go through with these data centers. So, I don’t even know why we’re still having this conversation,” said Jane Tadlock. The revised amendment also outlines additional approval requirements for battery storage facilities and sets standards for roads, utilities, fire protection, noise and water systems. Developers would also need to complete necessary infrastructure improvements before buildings could be occupied. The board has until December 7 to finish the amendment process.

artigo.texto: Property tax breaks for Nebraska data centers exceed $300 million By Fred Knapp , Senior Reporter/Producer Nebraska Public Media and Maddie Ames , Reporter Nov. 11, 2026, 3:34 p.m. · In the last four years, data centers in Nebraska received personal property tax breaks worth more than $300 million, according to a Nebraska Public Media News analysis of data from the Nebraska Department of Revenue. A tax incentives report released by the agency last month shows that data centers were exempt from property tax on nearly $22 billion worth of equipment from fiscal year 2023 through 2026. Over 99% of last year’s exempted property is located in Nebraska’s three largest counties – Douglas, Sarpy, and Lancaster. Data centers in those three counties received tax exemptions on more than $10 billion worth of equipment last year, according to the Nebraska Department of Revenue (NDOR). Using the average tax rates NDOR listed for those three counties, Nebraska Public Media News calculates data centers saved $196 million last fiscal year. Those exemptions are expected to continue. The report said “significant capital investment in data centers is anticipated to yield substantial tax credits.” In July, Gov. Jim Pillen issued an executive order aimed at denying further state tax incentives for data centers. “We just simply believe that we do not need to bring people together by incredible tax incentives,” Pillen said at the time. “We need to make sure that we attract givers, not takers.” But Pillen’s order does not change the law that allows data centers to exempt “computer systems and peripherals’’ – the guts of data centers – from property taxes, which pay for everything from local schools and police departments to county roads. Taxes that data centers don’t pay may shift to the other taxpayers in the counties where those data centers are located. But the department said the credits will be limited going forward. “Due to tax liability constraints, the utilization of these credits will be restricted,” the NDOR report said. The future impact of data centers and tax exemptions for them is expected to be a major consideration for policymakers when the Legislature reconvenes in January.

artigo.texto: Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB), IOI Corp Bhd and a consortium of small and medium enterprises (SMEs) have partnered to develop a 500 MW solar power project integrated with a battery energy storage system (BESS) in Bahau, Negeri Sembilan, Malaysia. The project represents a major renewable energy investment, with TNB planning to inject up to RM424.4 million into the joint venture (JV). According to a filing with Bursa Malaysia, TNB’s subsidiary, TNB Renewables Sdn Bhd (TRe), has signed a shareholders’ agreement with IOI Corp’s subsidiary, Luminous Aspect Sdn Bhd, and CSP 500MW Sdn Bhd. The project will be developed through Bahau Energy Ventures Sdn Bhd, the joint venture established by the three partners. The proposed development will comprise a 500 MWac solar photovoltaic (PV) power plant and a 250 MW/1,000 MWh BESS. It will operate under Malaysia’s Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme (CRESS), which enables renewable energy developers to supply green electricity to corporate consumers. Under the agreed ownership structure, TRe will hold a 70% stake in the joint venture, making it the largest shareholder. Luminous Aspect will own 25%, while CSP will hold the remaining 5%. CSP represents a consortium of 12 SMEs that have established the special purpose company to participate in the development and implementation of the project. The JV has a maximum equity capitalisation of RM606.2 million. TRe will contribute RM424.4 million, while Luminous Aspect and CSP will invest RM151.5 million and RM30.3 million, respectively. The project financing is expected to combine shareholder equity and third-party project financing, with a debt-to-equity ratio of up to 80:20, subject to market conditions and funding availability. The project will be supported by TNB’s long-term renewable energy offtake agreement with DayOne Data Centres Ltd, a Singapore-headquartered digital infrastructure company. Under the agreement announced on June 11, 2025, DayOne is expected to procure up to 500 MWac of renewable energy over 21 years to support its data centre operations in Malaysia. TRe will act as the project’s asset manager and oversee engineering and procurement arrangements. Meanwhile, IOI will participate as an investor and provide the project site through a land lease arrangement. IOI Group Managing Director and Chief Executive Datuk Lee Yeow Chor said the partnership would support the company’s renewable energy portfolio and generate stable long-term recurring income. For TNB, the project is expected to strengthen its renewable energy portfolio and support Malaysia’s energy transition. The company highlighted growing corporate demand for renewable electricity and the implementation of CRESS as important factors supporting the project’s prospects. TNB also stated that the transaction is not expected to have a material impact on the group’s earnings per share, net assets per share or gearing for the current financial year. The eventual financial impact will depend on the final project cost, financing arrangements and commercial operations. The partnership also aligns with IOI’s Five-Year Strategic Roadmap for 2025–2029, which aims to expand its renewable energy business and strengthen its participation in Malaysia’s low-carbon energy transition. artigo.texto: The Bihar Electricity Regulatory Commission (BERC) has approved a proposal by Bihar State Power Holding Company Limited (BSPHCL) to procure 300 MW of solar power integrated with a four-hour Battery Energy Storage System (BESS), marking an important step towards strengthening the state’s renewable energy supply and improving electricity availability during peak demand periods. The approval will enable Bihar’s distribution companies, North Bihar Power Distribution Company Limited and South Bihar Power Distribution Company Limited, to secure renewable electricity through a long-term power procurement agreement for 25 years. The electricity will be procured through NHPC Limited, which will act as the intermediary procurer. SAEL Industries India Limited has been selected as the project developer to supply 300 MW of power from a larger 1,200 MW interstate transmission system-connected renewable energy project. Under the approved arrangement, the discovered tariff is ₹3.13 per kilowatt-hour, while NHPC will receive an additional trading margin of ₹0.07 per kilowatt-hour. The Central Electricity Regulatory Commission had previously adopted the competitively discovered tariff in April 2026. The project includes a four-hour battery storage facility designed to provide 150 MW of firm electricity during evening peak demand hours, between 6:00 PM and midnight. This arrangement is expected to help Bihar manage its rising electricity demand and improve the reliability of power supply when solar generation is unavailable or reduced. The storage component will play an important role in shifting renewable electricity to periods when consumption is higher. The commission has also established strict performance requirements to ensure reliable electricity delivery. The developer must maintain at least 70 percent of the contracted peak capacity on a monthly basis and 85 percent annually. Failure to meet these requirements will attract financial penalties calculated at 1.5 times the applicable tariff rate for the shortfall. These provisions are intended to ensure that the project delivers the required electricity consistently. The regulatory approval was granted by a commission comprising Chairman Amir Subhani, Member Legal P. S. Yadav and Member Technical Manoj Kumar. While examining the petition, the commission considered the national Resource Adequacy framework and Bihar’s growing electricity requirements. It observed that the procurement would help the state address its Renewable Purchase Obligation requirements through FY 2029-30. The project is also expected to reduce Bihar’s dependence on expensive short-term electricity purchases, particularly during evening peak hours. By securing long-term renewable power supported by battery storage, distribution companies will have an additional source of reliable electricity, potentially reducing the need for load shedding and improving consumer supply conditions. SAEL Industries India Limited is expected to operationalise the project on or before June 30, 2028. Achieving this deadline will allow the state to benefit from transmission charge waivers, including a 25 percent waiver on interstate transmission charges for the solar component and a 100 percent waiver for electricity supplied from the co-located battery storage system. Additionally, BERC has approved a modified Power Sale Agreement incorporating consumer protection provisions. These provisions will account for potential tariff reductions arising from future changes in Goods and Services Tax rates. The decision is expected to support Bihar’s renewable energy transition while balancing electricity supply reliability, procurement costs and consumer interests.

artigo.texto: Nove ONGs, incluindo o Greenpeace, exigem suspensão de projetos de data centers no Brasil até que sejam feitos estudos de impacto e criadas leis rigorosas. Ações ocorreram em Fortaleza, Belém e Pindamonhangaba para alertar sobre os altos consumos de água e energia. Nove organizações da sociedade civil lançaram a mobilização nacional "Parem os mega data centers! O Brasil não é colônia das Big Techs". O grupo pede que nenhum projeto de centro de dados de hiperescala avance no país enquanto não houver estudos de impacto, licenciamento ambiental completo e uma lei que garanta participação das comunidades atingidas. O lançamento aconteceu em 6 de novembro com atos em Fortaleza (CE), Belém (PA) e Pindamonhangaba (SP), onde há projetos desse tipo. A iniciativa integra o Dia de Ação Global contra mega data centers, que mobilizou mais de 100 organizações de diferentes países nos dias 6 e 7 de novembro. - Nove ONGs assinam o manifesto: Instituto Terramar, Amazônia Sem Data Center, CTRL+Z, Data_Labe, Instituto Decodifica, Mulheres pelo Clima do Vale do Paraíba, Coding Rights, Filha do Sol e Greenpeace Brasil. - As entidades exigem o fim das isenções fiscais concedidas ao setor pelo regime Redata. - Ações ocorreram em Fortaleza, Belém e Pindamonhangaba, cidades com projetos de data centers em andamento. - Os projetos consomem grandes volumes de energia e água, gerando preocupação com a fatura de luz e abastecimento. - O movimento faz parte de uma ação global que envolve mais de 100 organizações internacionais. Críticas à falta de transparência e impactos sociais As organizações pedem ainda o fim das isenções fiscais concedidas ao setor pelo Regime Especial de Tributação para Serviços de Datacenter (Redata). Esse regime foi sancionado em setembro e deve ser regulamentado pelo Governo Federal ainda neste ano. Na avaliação das entidades, o país oferece benefícios fiscais, energia e água a essas empresas antes de ter análise dos riscos, planejamento territorial, regras socioambientais e contrapartidas sobre a soberania digital. Julia Catão, especialista em Tecnologia do Greenpeace Brasil, alertou para a interferência dos bilionários da tecnologia no processo eleitoral. "Acabamos de testemunhar a interferência dos bilionários da tecnologia no nosso processo eleitoral. Se por um lado precisamos regulamentar essas plataformas, por outro, precisamos impedi-las de construir suas casas de máquinas - os data centers - no nosso território da forma como têm feito, transferindo para a nossa população os seus custos socioambientais, sem ganho nenhum pro país", disse Catão. Vozes locais repudiam projetos na Amazônia e no Rio João Paulo Guimarães, ativista do Amazônia Sem Data Center, declarou: "É um absurdo um data center na Amazônia. O Pará já lidera números de mortes pelo calor extremo. Nós repudiamos esse projeto.". Mariana Ceres, ativista da Mulheres pelo Clima do Vale do Paraíba, ressaltou a falta de participação social. "A principal questão para nós está na falta de transparência e total ausência de participação social. Em 2026, é inaceitável um empreendimento desse porte e com grande impacto ambiental, sem que haja um rigoroso licenciamento ambiental", afirmou Ceres. Andréa Camurça, coordenadora de Incidência Política do Instituto Terramar/CE, destacou a questão energética. "A ação é fundamental para que as vozes dos territórios cheguem ao mundo e denunciem a ofensiva das big techs sobre os bens comuns do Sul Global. Não podemos gerar insegurança energética num país que ainda enfrenta pobreza energética: queremos água e energia para o povo, não para big techs!", declarou Camurça. Polinho Mota, diretor do Data_labe, comentou sobre a situação no Rio de Janeiro. "Aqui no Rio de Janeiro estamos acompanhando a chegada de um mega empreendimento que vai afetar a vida de toda a população da cidade, mas que em momento nenhum ouviu o que tínhamos para falar. Por isso, junto com o Decodifica e Coding Rights, estamos enfrentando a falta de transparência e exigindo mais estudos de impacto", relatou Mota. Detalhes das ações em três capitais brasileiras As mobilizações no Brasil começaram no dia 6 pela manhã, em Belém. A campanha Amazônia Sem Data Center esteve na comunidade Residencial Miramar Shalon, para uma roda de conversa com os moradores que podem ser impactados pelo projeto BEL1, da Elea Data Centers e Axia Energia. No Ceará, onde o data center do TikTok está em fase avançada de construção, ativistas se reuniram para conversar com a população na orla da Praia de Iracema, em Fortaleza. A atividade foi realizada pelo Instituto Terramar e Greenpeace Brasil. Um caminhão de LED percorreu as ruas da cidade com informações sobre os impactos no aumento da conta de luz e na poluição sonora. O caminhão exibiu ainda o documentário "Inteligência Natural", realizado pela Coding Rights sobre o empreendimento que está sendo construído pelas empresas Omnia e Casa dos Ventos em território indígena Anacé, em Caucaia, na região metropolitana. Já em Pindamonhangaba, a ação foi organizada pelas Mulheres pelo Clima do Vale do Paraíba. Moradores da região se reuniram em uma praça de grande circulação para alertar a população sobre o projeto Riverhook Village 18, planejado para a cidade. O que são data centers e por que geram preocupação Os mega data centers, ou centros de dados de hiperescala, são complexos industriais voltados sobretudo ao treinamento de modelos de Inteligência Artificial (IA) pelas grandes empresas de tecnologia, as Big Techs. Funcionam sem pausa, ocupam áreas extensas e consomem volumes muito altos de energia e água para refrigeração. Nas cidades que recebem esses projetos, a preocupação dos moradores vai do barulho contínuo das máquinas à pressão sobre o abastecimento de água e a conta de luz.

artigo.texto: Lydian Energy has brought its 150 MW/600 MWh Faraday battery energy storage system (BESS) into commercial operation in Utah County, adding four hours of contracted electricity storage capacity to the power infrastructure supporting Meta’s Eagle Mountain data center. The facility began operating on September 18, 2026, under a long-term energy storage agreement with PacifiCorp, according to Lydian’s November 10 announcement. The project adds battery storage alongside Lydian’s existing 525 MW Faraday solar facility, using the solar plant’s substation and grid interconnection rather than requiring a separate connection. The arrangement allows the developer to expand the site’s energy infrastructure while making use of existing grid facilities. Faraday BESS occupies approximately eight acres and uses lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery technology. Its 150 MW power rating and 600 MWh storage capacity provide a four-hour duration at full rated output. Lydian said it completed the project in approximately 10 months from mobilization to commercial operation. The project also establishes the first operating phase of a larger battery storage development at the site. Lydian is developing Faraday BESS 2, which could add another 375 MW/1,500 MWh by the fourth quarter of 2028. Battery storage supports Meta’s Eagle Mountain operations Faraday BESS operates under a Schedule 34 arrangement supporting Meta’s Eagle Mountain data center. PacifiCorp receives the project’s contracted storage capacity under a long-term agreement, placing the battery within a utility-contracted arrangement rather than making it an exclusively dedicated power supply physically connected to Meta’s campus. The project has a longer development history than its commercial operation announcement suggests. In January 2023, PacifiCorp executed a power purchase agreement for 525 MW of solar generation from Faraday Solar and a separate battery storage agreement for a 150 MW, four-hour system. A March 2023 filing before the Utah Public Service Commission identified the two agreements as serving a single Schedule 34 customer. At that time, PacifiCorp expected the solar facility to enter commercial operation on September 30, 2025, and the battery system on June 1, 2026. The battery ultimately began operating on September 18, 2026, approximately three and a half months after the original target recorded in that filing. Lydian’s reported 10-month construction and commissioning period refers to the period from mobilization, not the entire development history dating back to 2023. Meta subsequently identified its involvement directly. In a September 14, 2026, update, the company named Lydian’s 150 MW Faraday battery as part of its investments in energy resources supporting the Eagle Mountain data center. Meta said its Utah energy investments had added more than 1.7 GW of clean and renewable energy and 600 MWh of battery storage across 13 sites. It also said it pays the full costs of its data centers’ electricity use and funds new and upgraded infrastructure needed to support its operations. This arrangement connects three distinct participants. Lydian develops, owns and operates the battery, PacifiCorp contracts for its storage capacity, and Meta supports the energy arrangement as part of its strategy for the Eagle Mountain data center. Shared solar infrastructure supports the battery installation One of Faraday BESS’s most important infrastructure features is its integration with the existing Faraday solar facility. The battery occupies approximately eight acres adjacent to the solar development and shares its substation and grid interconnection. This allows Lydian to add a substantial storage installation without developing an entirely separate grid connection. The solar facility began commercial operation on September 30, 2025, under the associated PacifiCorp agreement. The battery’s September 2026 commissioning therefore adds storage to an existing generation site rather than establishing an entirely new energy development. The technical arrangement also requires an important distinction when assessing the site’s combined capacity. Faraday Solar has a stated capacity of 525 MW, while the battery can discharge at up to 150 MW. These ratings should not automatically be combined to suggest that the shared interconnection can export 675 MW simultaneously. The actual combined export capability depends on the approved interconnection limits and operating arrangements. Lydian has not disclosed the site’s detailed export constraints or how PacifiCorp coordinates solar generation and battery dispatch. Nevertheless, reusing the existing substation and interconnection provides a clear infrastructure advantage. It allows the developer to expand the site’s energy capabilities using facilities already established for the solar project. Faraday BESS 2 could add another 1.5 GWh Lydian is developing a second battery installation, Faraday BESS 2, at the Utah site. The proposed expansion would add up to 375 MW of power capacity and 1,500 MWh of storage, with commercial operation targeted for the fourth quarter of 2028. If completed at its announced maximum capacity, the second phase would increase the site’s combined battery storage to 525 MW and 2,100 MWh. That would establish a substantially larger storage development alongside the existing 525 MW Faraday solar facility. The expansion would also increase the amount of electricity that can be shifted across different periods, subject to charging availability, grid conditions and contractual dispatch requirements. artigo.texto: Starpointe data center hearings to continue into December The Hanover Township Board of Supervisors scheduled two additional hearings in the ongoing review process for a proposed 350-megawatt data center in Starpointe Business Park after the developer announced that they have two additional witnesses to present. The board has been reviewing the conditional use permit submitted in May by Dallas, Texas-based developer Prime Data Centers LLC since August 2026, with over 20 hours of total testimony across a dozen hearings hampering the pace of proceedings. Prime has called acoustic, civil, electrical, mechanical and natural gas engineers that have worked on the project to testify regarding numerous aspects of the preliminary design, plus the Project Lead Kate Nolan Bryden. Bryden provided an overview of the project during direct testimony at the start of the hearing process, and has been called back for cross-examination several times by a group of attorneys representing concerned residents who live near the proposed site. Thomas Steele, a local attorney representing Prime, said that while the developer has called several witnesses to the stand, their direct testimony only took up less than five hours so far, and that the residents’ attorneys cross-examination has occupied more than 15 hours of hearing time. In addition to the attorneys, several other residents who were granted party status to the hearing have cross-examined Prime’s witnesses, often using the platform to voice their concerns with the potentially harmful environmental impact of the proposed 350-megawatt, seven-building data center campus and attached natural gas power plant. Prime representatives have repeatedly highlighted that the project will create hundreds of jobs to build and maintain the data center campus, and emphasized that Prime will fully comply with all applicable environmental regulations and the commonwealth’s Governor’s Responsible Infrastructure Development (GRID) standards, which were signed into law earlier this year. The board was to continue its review of the conditional use application on Wednesday, and again on Nov. 18, plus Dec. 9, all at 6 p.m. at the Hanover Volunteer Fire Department at 9 Starck Drive in Burgettstown.

artigo.texto: Foto: Divulgação A prefeita de Uberaba, Elisa Araújo, reuniu-se nesta quarta-feira, 11, em São Paulo (SP), com representantes da Atlas Renewable Energy para avançar nas conversas sobre as condições para a instalação de infraestrutura para data centers na Zona de Processamento de Exportação (ZPE) de Uberaba. Na ocasião, foi assinado o documento que formaliza o interesse da companhia na instalação do empreendimento na ZPE de Uberaba. A agenda integra a estratégia da Prefeitura de posicionar o Município como destino de investimentos em infraestrutura digital e energia, setores estratégicos para o desenvolvimento econômico de Uberaba e de toda a região do Triângulo Mineiro. De acordo com os estudos preliminares, a iniciativa tem potencial de investimento inicial superior a R$ 10 bilhões em edificações, instalações de conexão e infraestrutura. Com o avanço do projeto, poderão ser acrescentados cerca de R$ 30 bilhões em equipamentos de tecnologia da informação, o que poderia elevar o investimento total estimado a aproximadamente R$ 40 bilhões. Se concretizado, o empreendimento estará entre os maiores da história do Município. O projeto encontra-se em fase de avaliação e depende ainda de etapas técnicas, regulatórias e de aprovação, entre elas a análise pelo Conselho Nacional das Zonas de Processamento de Exportação (CZPE), órgão do Governo Federal responsável por autorizar a instalação de empresas nessas áreas. “Uberaba reúne condições muito favoráveis para receber investimentos dessa natureza: localização estratégica, infraestrutura energética e logística, e uma ZPE alfandegada e pronta para operar. O nosso papel é criar o ambiente para que projetos como este possam se concretizar, com planejamento, segurança jurídica e responsabilidade ambiental. E queremos fazer isso de mãos dadas com empresas que tenham trajetória sólida em infraestrutura energética e compromisso real com o meio ambiente e com as comunidades. Nosso compromisso é transformar o potencial de Uberaba em empregos e oportunidades para a nossa gente”, destacou a prefeita Elisa Araújo. A demanda por capacidade de processamento de dados e inteligência artificial cresce de forma acelerada no Brasil e no mundo, e a combinação de energia renovável, disponibilidade de área e incentivos à exportação coloca a região em posição de destaque para atrair esse tipo de empreendimento. Caso se concretize, a iniciativa poderá gerar empregos diretos e indiretos durante as obras e a operação, estimular a participação de fornecedores locais, promover a capacitação profissional da população e fortalecer a infraestrutura energética regional. Além disso, a concretização da iniciativa abriria caminho para a chegada de novos investimentos ao Município e posicionaria Uberaba como um polo competitivo, em nível internacional, para o desenvolvimento de infraestrutura de data centers. As ZPEs, enquanto áreas de livre comércio com o exterior, oferecem benefícios tributários, administrativos e cambiais à exportação de bens e serviços. A Zona de Processamento de Exportação de Uberaba é uma das quatro do Brasil alfandegadas pela Receita Federal e prontas para receber investimentos. A Atlas Renewable Energy, empresa que avalia a iniciativa, possui trajetória consolidada no desenvolvimento, financiamento, construção e operação de projetos de infraestrutura de energia renovável de grande escala na América Latina e atua com elevados padrões de responsabilidade ambiental e social em seus projetos. Na frente social, a companhia desenvolve iniciativas voltadas à capacitação profissional, à inclusão de mulheres no mercado de trabalho, à educação e ao apoio à infraestrutura comunitária, com o objetivo de deixar um legado positivo e duradouro nos territórios onde atua. “Uberaba tem características que a tornam uma região de grande potencial para o desenvolvimento de infraestrutura digital sustentável no país. Seguimos avaliando a iniciativa em diálogo com o Município e com os órgãos competentes”, afirmou Fábio Bortoluzo, presidente da Atlas Renewable Energy no Brasil. Também participaram da reunião, na capital paulista, o secretário de Governo, Caio Presotto, o secretário adjunto de Desenvolvimento Econômico, Turismo e Inovação, Alexandre Cury, a diretora Comercial e de Assuntos Aduaneiros da ZPE Uberaba, Maria Letícia Mesquita, e do sócio da Cassu Participações, Mário Renato Palmério. A Atlas Renewable Energy é uma empresa internacional de infraestrutura de energia limpa, fundada em 2017, com mais de 10,8 GW em sua base de ativos renováveis. Líder no segmento na América Latina, a empresa é controlada pela Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP), da BlackRock.

artigo.texto: Not all technology companies stand to lose from a slowdown in data center construction. In fact, it could be exactly what Amazon needs to pull ahead, according to Jim Cramer . "If it's going to be slower, that does work for the incumbents, hence why I would buy Amazon," Jim said Monday morning on CNBC. A divide in the artificial intelligence trade has become increasingly apparent since last week's midterm elections , as growing opposition to new projects raises concerns about future infrastructure spending. Amazon shares have surged 7% since the election, including Monday's intraday gains. Other cloud incumbents such as Microsoft and Google parent Alphabet are solidly higher too. Meanwhile, semiconductor and neocloud stocks have suffered steep losses, with Micron tumbling 14.1%, Sandisk plunging 21.2% and CoreWeave falling 8.9%, when including Monday's intraday bounce-back rallies. The strength in hyperscalers has helped fuel a broader technology rebound following last week's sell-off. Despite weakness in Nvidia and other chipmakers, the Nasdaq has gained a combined 3.3% over Friday and Monday, recovering much of Thursday's 5.5% plunge. "I think the Amazon move is very right," Jim said. "I was talking about it going to $300." That would represent nearly 10% upside from current levels. The recent rally marks a turnaround for Amazon, which had slumped over the last few months as investors grew tired of enormous AI spending. The stock briefly got hot in late July and into August, following the forced unwind of Situational Awareness and an encouraging second-quarter earnings report . But after closing at $284 apiece on Aug. 3, shares lost more than 15% through the end of October, ending that month at roughly $240. Cramer argued that a slowdown in development could benefit established cloud providers, which already operate extensive data center networks and could have the corporate heft needed to navigate any new bureaucratic obstacles. He compared the situation to a yellow flag in Formula One racing. "Everyone has to go slower, no one's allowed to pass," he said. "If that's the case, that's Microsoft and that's Amazon winning." Demand for AI computing power isn't going away, even if new data centers become harder to build. Unlike smaller neocloud providers that rely on continued expansion to grow, Amazon and Microsoft already have massive infrastructure networks in place, positioning them to capture a larger share of demand as new capacity becomes harder to bring online. Jim also said that he likes that Amazon has been less reliant on neocloud providers to secure extra capacity to meet demand. A slower buildout would also ease pressure on the hyperscalers to keep accelerating capital spending, potentially allowing their free cash flow to recover and improving returns on their existing infrastructure investments. For investors, that makes the established hyperscalers better positioned to weather a slowdown than companies whose growth depends more directly on new data center construction. artigo.texto: How data center demand is reshaping electricity costs across the US By Lucas Winter for Shipley Energy Three years ago, U.S. utilities expected peak electricity demand to grow by about 24 gigawatts over the following five years. Their most recent forecasts put that figure at roughly 166 gigawatts, 6.9 times the earlier estimate, and about 90 gigawatts of the increase is tied to data centers. That growth is beginning to show up in electricity costs for businesses and households, though the effect looks very different depending on where a customer is located. Data centers used about 4.4% of U.S. electricity in 2023, according to Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, and the lab projects that share could reach 6.7% to 12% by 2028. The U.S. Energy Information Administration expects record national electricity sales in 2026, driven by data center development and manufacturing, with the average U.S. residential price rising from 17.3 cents per kilowatt-hour in 2025 to 18.2 cents in 2026. Whether data centers raise costs in a given area depends on three things: - How much spare power supply the region had before they arrived - How its electricity market recovers the cost of new demand - What rules regulators have set for very large customers Before looking at how those factors play out region by region, it helps to understand how data center demand turns into charges on an electricity bill. For instance, if you’re doing business in Pennsylvania, Ohio, Maryland, or D.C., capacity charges are now one of the fastest-growing parts of commercial electricity bills in the PJM region. Below, Shipley Energy explains what the latest auction results mean for your next budget. A large data center campus can need as much power as a small city, running around the clock. Grid operators and utilities have to secure generation and build transmission for that demand, often years before the facility opens. Those costs reach customers through three main channels. The first is capacity costs, which pay power plants to be available during the hours when demand peaks. Some regions buy this capacity through auctions held years in advance, so forecasts of future data center demand can raise prices before the facilities exist. The second is wholesale energy prices, which rise when added demand calls more expensive power plants into service. Researchers at the Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas estimate that existing data centers have already raised wholesale electricity prices by 2% to 6% on average nationwide. The third is transmission and distribution, the lines and substations needed to deliver power to new load, which are often paid for by all customers in a utility’s territory. Because wholesale power typically makes up about half of the retail price of electricity, a given increase in wholesale prices reaches retail bills at roughly half its size. A Region-by-Region Look The same kind of demand growth is producing very different results across the country. PJM The grid operator serving 13 states and Washington, D.C., runs a capacity auction about three years ahead of delivery. Its clearing price rose from $28.92 per megawatt-day for 2024/2025 to $269.92 for 2025/2026, then hit a federally approved cap in each of the next three auctions. The 2028/2029 auction cleared at $325 per megawatt-day and still came in 6,831 megawatts short of PJM’s reliability requirement. PJM’s independent market monitor attributes about 46% of capacity costs across the last four auctions, or $29.4 billion, to data center demand. MISO The Midcontinent grid operator saw summer capacity prices reach a record $666.50 per megawatt-day for 2025/2026 as its surplus shrank. A year later, the picture shifted. Capacity offered into the 2026/2027 auction grew 3.4%, led by solar additions, and annualized prices fell to between $116 and $126 per megawatt-day, down from $212 to $217 the year before. Texas ERCOT has no capacity auction, so data center demand shows up mainly in wholesale prices during high-demand hours and in transmission spending. In August 2026, Gov. Greg Abbott directed state regulators and ERCOT to audit every data center seeking a grid connection before any project moves forward, citing more than 474 gigawatts of requests, more than five times the state’s record peak demand, with about 90% coming from data centers. Southeast Georgia Power’s pipeline of prospective large-load projects grew from about 16,000 megawatts in 2023 to roughly 69,000 megawatts by December 2025, about 80% of it from data centers. The utility and its regulators disagree on the electricity bill impact. Georgia Power projects that new large-load contracts will produce about $950 million a year in customer savings beginning in 2029, while state commission staff cautioned that the related generation buildout could add around $20 a month to residential bills. Pacific Northwest Data centers account for roughly 15% of the current load of Oregon’s investor-owned utilities, according to the state’s utility commission. Under a 2025 state law, Oregon regulators approved new rates for Portland General Electric in July 2026 that raised data center rates by an average of 29% while lowering residential rates by 1.3% and commercial rates by 2.1%. Surplus-Supply States In states that had extra generation before data centers arrived, new demand has often spread fixed grid costs across more customers. North Dakota saw electricity demand grow almost 40% while inflation-adjusted prices fell by about 3 cents per kilowatt-hour. Researchers at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory and The Brattle Group, who documented that pattern, describe the overall relationship between load growth and prices as mixed and uncertain in their 2026 update. Forecasts Versus What Gets Built Not every announced data center will be built, and forecasts disagree about how many will. artigo.texto: 247 – O governo federal planeja destinar R$ 46,3 milhões ao desenvolvimento de uma tecnologia nacional de inteligência artificial (IA) para gerenciar e distribuir dados entre pequenos centros de processamento de informações espalhados pelo Brasil. A iniciativa pretende modernizar a infraestrutura digital do país, reduzir custos operacionais e ampliar a autonomia brasileira no tratamento de informações estratégicas. O plano do Ministério das Comunicações prevê que o investimento seja direcionado ao desenvolvimento do projeto Prisma, uma plataforma capaz de identificar automaticamente onde e como os dados devem ser processados, utilizando inteligência artificial para otimizar a distribuição dos recursos computacionais. A proposta é permitir que diferentes estruturas de armazenamento e processamento de dados operem de maneira integrada, com maior eficiência na utilização de energia e capacidade computacional. O sistema deverá identificar as melhores condições para executar determinadas operações e distribuir as demandas entre os chamados mini data centers. Além da redução de despesas com energia elétrica e manutenção das operações, o governo espera que a plataforma acelere o acesso às informações e fortaleça a proteção de dados considerados estratégicos. Governo busca reduzir dependência de tecnologias estrangeiras Um dos principais objetivos do investimento é ampliar a soberania tecnológica brasileira, diminuindo a necessidade de utilização de soluções desenvolvidas fora do país para administrar infraestruturas digitais. O ministro das Comunicações, Frederico Filho, destacou que o desenvolvimento de tecnologias nacionais é fundamental para garantir maior autonomia no tratamento de informações e preparar o Brasil para os desafios da transformação digital. “Investir em tecnologia nacional é garantir que o Brasil tenha mais autonomia para proteger suas informações e desenvolver soluções para os desafios do futuro. Estamos fortalecendo a inovação brasileira e criando condições para uma infraestrutura digital mais moderna, segura e sustentável, reduzindo nossa dependência de tecnologias desenvolvidas no exterior”, afirmou o ministro, em nota. A declaração coloca a redução da dependência tecnológica externa entre as prioridades do projeto, ao lado da modernização dos sistemas de processamento e da segurança das informações. A iniciativa também busca estimular o desenvolvimento de soluções brasileiras de inteligência artificial aplicadas à infraestrutura digital, área considerada estratégica para o armazenamento, a circulação e o processamento de grandes volumes de dados. Projeto será executado pelo CPQD e terá duração de 36 meses A administração dos R$ 46,3 milhões ficará sob responsabilidade da Financiadora de Estudos e Projetos (Finep), instituição federal de fomento à pesquisa e à inovação. A execução técnica caberá ao Centro de Pesquisa e Desenvolvimento em Telecomunicações (CPQD), instituição brasileira especializada em pesquisa, desenvolvimento e inovação tecnológica. O prazo previsto para a realização do projeto é de 36 meses, contados a partir da assinatura do convênio de pesquisa, desenvolvimento e inovação entre a Finep e o CPQD. Durante esse período, o trabalho será direcionado ao desenvolvimento da plataforma Prisma e de suas funcionalidades de gerenciamento inteligente de dados. A tecnologia deverá permitir que as demandas computacionais sejam distribuídas automaticamente entre diferentes infraestruturas, levando em consideração as condições necessárias ao processamento das informações. Inteligência artificial será utilizada para otimizar recursos O funcionamento previsto para o Prisma tem como elemento central a utilização de inteligência artificial na administração dos recursos computacionais. Em vez de concentrar necessariamente o processamento em uma única estrutura, a plataforma deverá avaliar a distribuição das demandas entre diferentes mini data centers, buscando melhorar o aproveitamento da capacidade disponível. Esse modelo poderá contribuir para reduzir o consumo de energia e os custos associados ao funcionamento dos equipamentos, além de tornar mais eficiente a circulação das informações. A proteção de dados estratégicos também integra os objetivos anunciados pelo Ministério das Comunicações. Ao desenvolver uma solução nacional de gerenciamento, o governo pretende fortalecer a capacidade brasileira de administrar informações em infraestruturas digitais.

artigo.texto: Tsunami democrata tira de Donald Trump o controle da Câmara e do Senado Oposição terá, no mínimo, 54 senadores, caminha para maioria robusta na Câmara e elege governadores em estados importantes e simbólicos. Crédito: Estadão O mercado financeiro focado em tecnologia não tem vivido seus melhores dias recentemente e o índice Nasdaq chegou a registrar sua maior queda diária desde abril de 2025 na última quinta-feira (5). A queda foi de 5,5% e resultou na redução de US$ 2,5 trilhões (R$ 13,4 trilhões em conversão direta) do valor de mercado das principais empresas do setor, influenciadas pelas midterms dos Estados Unidos. O motivo para esse derretimento abrupto tem relação com as recentes eleições de meio de mandato, as midterms norte-americanas. Na última rodada, a expressiva vitória do Partido Democrata contra o Partido Republicano no pleito acendeu o temor de que a expansão da inteligência artificial sofra mais regulações nas mãos dos democratas. A Nvidia, empresa mais poderosa do planeta e absoluta na venda de chips para servidores, viu suas ações caírem 9%. Com a rival direta, a AMD, a queda foi ainda mais chamativa e bateu nos 17%. O índice de semicondutores da Filadélfia (SOX) também registrou uma queda notória de 12%, o nível mais baixo dos últimos seis meses. O clima pesado não está restrito somente aos Estados Unidos e chega a outros países em um efeito cascata. Bolsas asiáticas, como a japonesa Nikkei e a sul-coreana Kospi, operaram em forte queda. O índice VIX, chamado de “termômetro do medo” em Wall Street, registrou seu maior salto desde 2024 e aumentou a apreensão dos acionistas. - 🪧Índice VIX (Termômetro do medo): essa é uma métrica de Wall Street que mede a expectativa de volatilidade do mercado para os próximos 30 dias. Quando o índice dispara, significa que há insegurança por parte de investidores e possibilidade de quedas na bolsa. IA pode esbarrar em decisões políticas Analistas do mercado financeiro mostram que o receio de acionistas e investidores é que os democratas façam força contra a construção de novos data centers em solo americano. Um dos motivos é o fato desses centros de dados exigirem grandes volumes de água para resfriar os servidores, além dos gastos em energia e o barulho. Uma estimativa do UBS aponta que quase 30% da capacidade adicional de data centers esperada para 2028 nos Estados Unidos tem risco de sofrer paralisações. Como o mercado de IA se expandiu rapidamente nos últimos anos, isso se tornou um empecilho para investidores da categoria, que demandam novas instalações para o treinamento dos modelos de IA. Gigantes responsáveis por essas tecnologias, como a Amazon e Alphabet (dona do Google) viram quedas de 2,2%. No caso da Microsoft, o recuo foi de 3,6%. Aliás, a companhia de Redmond já teria começado a apertar a supervisão de projetos terceirizados de data centers. Por falar em IA e problemas financeiros, o caso de infidelidade do CEO da Nvidia pode trazer grandes consequências à empresa e ao mercado global. Não esqueça de continuar ligado no TecMundo para acompanhar outros artigos como esse e não perder as principais informações da indústria de tecnologia. Com informações de Reuters.

artigo.texto: NHPC Limited has issued a tender on behalf of Bundelkhand Saur Urja Limited (BSUL) to select a Battery Energy Storage System Developer (BESSD) for developing two Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS). NHPC's two BESS projects comprise a 300 MW/800 MW/4,800 MWh system and a 600 MW/800 MW/3,200 MWh system. It has sought bids until December 12, 2026. By seeking over 4 hours of supply during non-solar hours, the tender seeks to push the boundaries of solar plus storage in UP for the first time. BSUL is a joint venture between NHPC Limited and the Uttar Pradesh New and Renewable Energy Development Agency (UPNEDA). The selected developer will procure the entire solar energy generated by the existing solar plants, establish co-located BESS projects, and utilise the solar power to charge the BESS. The remaining solar power, along with the power discharged from the BESS, will be scheduled for supply. Scope of Work BSUL intends to integrate BESS with its existing solar power generation capacity to meet the firm and dispatchable power requirements of the End Procurer. It has invited proposals for setting up BESS projects that will use energy generated by the existing solar plants to charge the storage systems and schedule Solar-plus-BESS power under either of the two configurations. The projects are intended to meet the solar and non-solar hour power requirements of the Buying Entity/Distribution Companies (DISCOMs). Under the first configuration, the project involves scheduling 300 MW of solar capacity during solar hours, coupled with an 800 MW/4,800 MWh BESS for supplying power during non-solar hours. Under the second configuration, 600 MW of solar capacity will be scheduled during solar hours, supported by an 800 MW/3,200 MWh BESS during non-solar hours. Under this framework, BSUL, acting as an Intermediary Procurer, has selected Coal India Limited (CIL) and NLC India Renewables Limited as Solar Power Developers (SPDs) to develop a total solar generation capacity of 1,200 MW across Tehsil Orai and Tehsil Madhogarh. BSUL will execute Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) to procure the entire 1,200 MW of solar power generated from the park. Integrating ESS With Solar Projects Energy Storage Systems (ESS) play a critical role in managing fluctuations in renewable energy generation and helping grid operators maintain reliability while facilitating the smooth integration of renewable energy into the grid. Additionally, ESS connected to Solar Photovoltaic (SPV) plants can enhance the utilisation of renewable energy transmission systems. It has been clarified that the BESSD will procure the entire power generated by the co-located solar projects in Jalaun Solar Park from the Solar Power Project Developer (SPPD), BSUL, at the tariff detailed hereunder.

artigo.texto: Plataforma de IA – O Ministério das Comunicações vai aplicar R$ 46,3 milhões no desenvolvimento de uma plataforma nacional de gerenciamento de data centers. Batizado de Prisma, o projeto utilizará inteligência artificial (IA) para distribuir recursos computacionais entre diferentes estruturas, buscando melhorar a eficiência e a segurança do processamento de dados no país. A iniciativa, aprovada pelo Conselho Gestor do Fundo para o Desenvolvimento Tecnológico das Telecomunicações (Funttel), pretende reduzir gastos operacionais, consumo de energia e riscos relacionados à proteção de informações estratégicas. A execução ficará sob responsabilidade do Centro Brasileiro de Inovação em Tecnologias da Informação e da Comunicação (CPQD), em Campinas (SP), com recursos administrados pela Finep. LEIA: Suposto ataque à Polícia Civil de SP envolve venda de dados por US$ 40 mil Funcionamento do Prisma A plataforma identificará automaticamente os locais mais adequados para processar cada conjunto de dados, incluindo estruturas menores distribuídas pelo território nacional. Com isso, as informações poderão ser tratadas mais perto de sua origem, diminuindo o tempo de resposta dos serviços digitais. Segundo a superintendente da Área de Saúde e Transformação Digital da Finep, Joana Meirelles, a proposta é oferecer uma infraestrutura segura e sustentável para áreas como saúde, defesa, segurança pública, educação e telecomunicações. O diretor de Tecnologia e Inovação do CPQD, Gustavo Correa Lima, destaca que a descentralização também amplia o controle sobre as informações: “Além de tornar mais rápidos o processamento e o acesso às informações, essa arquitetura permite maior controle sobre o dado que está na borda”. Eficiência energética e autonomia tecnológica Entre os benefícios previstos estão a redução da pegada de carbono dos data centers, maior resistência a falhas no fornecimento de energia e proteção contra ataques cibernéticos. O projeto também contempla soluções de armazenamento elétrico para manter os serviços em funcionamento durante instabilidades no abastecimento. A plataforma deverá seguir padrões internacionais de segurança e as diretrizes da Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados (LGPD). Para o ministro das Comunicações, Frederico de Siqueira Filho, o investimento também representa um avanço na autonomia tecnológica brasileira e na redução da dependência de soluções estrangeiras. O desenvolvimento do Prisma terá duração de 36 meses, a partir da assinatura do convênio de pesquisa, desenvolvimento e inovação entre Finep e CPQD.
