artigo.texto: Previously viewed as a supplementary technical component, battery energy storage systems (BESS) are now being redefined as an energy service with its own pricing methodology and power purchase agreement framework under a new mechanism. The Ministry of Industry and Trade has issued Decision No. 2987/QD-BCT, approving the power generation price framework for standalone Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) for 2026. Accordingly, the maximum price (excluding Value Added Tax) is VND3,209.98 (around $0.12) per kWh, effective from November 11, 2026. The electricity price framework under Decision 2987 is specifically for independent energy storage systems not connected to any generation source. This maximum price provides a legal basis for developing large-scale electricity storage projects to serve the national power system. This marks the first time a specific electricity price framework has been established for BESS. Decision 2987 follows the Ministry's Decision 2946/QD-BCT, issued on November 5, 2026, which approved the solar power price framework for 2026, distinguishing prices for projects with and without storage systems. The issuance of these two decisions for different power sources within the same period indicates a national energy policy expanding in two parallel directions: encouraging BESS integration into solar power projects while creating a separate pricing basis for standalone storage systems. The VND3,209.98/kWh rate is the maximum price applicable to standalone BESS. For solar power combined with BESS, the maximum prices vary by region: VND1,813.48/kWh for the North, VND1,469.90/kWh for the Central region, and VND1,254.97/kWh for the South. For floating solar power combined with BESS, the corresponding rates are VND2,120.31/kWh, VND1,703.21/kWh, and VND1,461.39/kWh. These are ceiling prices, not fixed rates. The actual power generation service price for each project will be determined by the method specified in Circular 62/2025/TT-BCT, based on investment, operation, and maintenance costs over the project's entire lifecycle, with an internal rate of return (IRR) not exceeding 12%. Circular 62 also specifies the applicable entities: BESS connected to the national grid at 110 kV or higher voltage levels, with a capacity of 10 MW or more, serving national grid needs and aligning with the National Power Development Plan. Power Plan 8 (Decision 768/QD-TTg) sets a target of 10,000–16,300 MW of BESS by 2030. For solar power combined with BESS, Decision 2946 stipulates that the battery storage system used for price framework calculation must have a minimum capacity of 10% of the solar power plant's capacity, with a two-hour storage and discharge duration. Encouraging Industrial-Scale BESS Investment and Deployment According to experts, the newly issued power generation price framework for energy storage systems will impact the BESS investor, production, and consumption chain. The first and most directly affected group comprises independent BESS developers. Before Decision 2987, investors developing electricity storage projects had to link them to a generation source for pricing, a structure that increased capital scale and complicated legal procedures. The new framework allows for the separation of these two project types, providing a basis for investors to develop financial plans and negotiate power purchase agreements. This is a significant signal for infrastructure investment funds, energy companies, and international investors monitoring Vietnam's electricity storage market. However, the 3,209.98 VND/kWh rate is a ceiling, not a guaranteed revenue for all projects. Actual prices will depend on investment costs and specific contract conditions. The IRR constraint of 12% or less (stipulating that the internal rate of return of an investment project must not exceed a ceiling of 12% per annum), in the context of current capital costs, is a factor investors need to carefully consider before making decisions. The second group includes solar power developers currently or soon to implement projects. The 2026 price framework clearly distinguishes prices for projects with and without storage systems. This difference may incentivize investors to consider integrating BESS from the design phase, rather than solely focusing on expanding generation capacity. For operational solar power plants, the new mechanism also opens prospects for researching upgrade and BESS addition options. The third group consists of businesses in the energy equipment and service supply chain. Increased BESS investment demand creates more opportunities for battery manufacturers, power converter system (PCS) suppliers, battery management system (BMS) providers, energy management system (EMS) providers, EPC contractors, and operation and maintenance service units. As Vietnam promotes the development of supporting industries in the energy sector, this is an opportunity for domestic enterprises to participate more deeply in the electricity storage value chain. The fourth group, indirectly affected, includes industrial parks and manufacturing enterprises with high electricity consumption needs. Multinational corporations are increasingly focusing on the carbon footprint of their supply chains; access to clean, stable, and verifiable electricity sources is becoming a criterion in investment location decisions. For industrial park developers, combining rooftop solar power with storage systems can contribute to forming a green industrial infrastructure model, optimizing electricity costs, and enhancing competitiveness to attract tenants. At the individual enterprise level, BESS can be used for load management, peak power limitation, backup power support, and optimizing the use of self-generated solar power. However, it is important to distinguish that the pricing mechanism for large-scale standalone BESS under Decision 2987 differs from behind-the-meter storage models at factories or industrial parks. artigo.texto: Foto da manchete: ilustração-Divulgação Por Jurandir Antonio – Voz: Enéas Jacobina Texto do áudio O governador Otaviano Pivetta está participando da 31ª Conferência das Nações Unidas sobre Mudanças Climáticas, a COP 31, em Antália, na Turquia, com uma agenda voltada à abertura de oportunidades econômicas para Mato Grosso por meio da comercialização internacional de créditos de carbono e outros ativos ambientais. A missão acontece em um momento que o Governo do Estado busca estruturar instrumentos jurídicos e financeiros para transformar resultados de redução do desmatamento em receitas destinadas à conservação ambiental e à implementação de políticas de desenvolvimento sustentável. A COP 31 segue até 20 de novembro, reunindo representantes governamentais, instituições financeiras, empresas e organizações internacionais para discutir medidas relacionadas às mudanças climáticas, ao mercado de carbono e ao financiamento da preservação ambiental. Em Mato Grosso, uma das principais medidas relacionadas ao projeto é a proposta de criação da Companhia Mato-grossense de Ativos Ambientais S.A. O projeto de lei foi encaminhado pelo governador à Assembleia Legislativa e prevê a constituição de uma sociedade de economia mista destinada à estruturação, gestão e comercialização de créditos de carbono, créditos de biodiversidade e outros ativos ambientais gerados no território estadual. O Estado possui áreas dos biomas Amazônia, Cerrado e Pantanal, que apresentam características ambientais diferentes e exigem estratégias específicas de conservação. A programação da delegação também contempla discussões sobre riscos climáticos, prevenção e combate a incêndios florestais, economia florestal e estratégias para enfrentar crimes ambientais. Outro aspecto importante da conferência será a discussão sobre mecanismos capazes de ampliar o financiamento climático destinado a regiões que concentram grandes áreas de vegetação nativa. Pivetta permanecerá fora de Mato Grosso até 18 de novembro, de acordo com a programação divulgada pelo Governo do Estado. Sapicuá Rádio Agência, da redação em Cuiabá, Enéas Jacobina

artigo.texto: Coloque a eixos nas suas fontes preferidas do Google Veja nossas notícias com mais destaque nas suas buscas. Coloque a eixos nas suas fontes preferidas do Google Veja nossas notícias com mais destaque nas suas buscas. O desenvolvimento de novos projetos de data centers no Brasil mostra que a tendência é que os investidores busquem instalar seus empreendimentos em locais próximos às infraestruturas de energia, para garantir maior segurança no fornecimento de energia elétrica. Em entrevista ao estúdio eixos, durante a EVEx Lisboa 2026, a sócia do Neves, De Rosso e Fonseca Advogados (NDF), Rossana Fonseca, conta que, por mais resiliente que o Sistema Interligado Nacional (SIN) seja, ele está sujeito a interrupções no suprimento. Confira na íntegra. “Hoje a tendência é que os contratos firmados entre os data centers e as empresas de suprimento de energia elétrica estabeleçam multas, porque espera-se que o fornecimento dessa energia seja realizado de forma perene, sem interrupção”. Mas ao mesmo tempo, quando você observa o funcionamento do ONS [Operador Nacional do Sistema Elétrico], você percebe que é praticamente impossível que um fornecimento, por mais resiliente que ele seja, ocorra sem que haja um mínimo que seja de queda… Isso obviamente empurra os investidores a ter um cuidado maior na busca da localidade de instalação desses data centers”, comentou. A advogada destaca que o Redata traz estímulos ao desenvolvimento de data centers no Brasil, mas ainda há gargalos importantes no licenciamento estadual desses empreendimentos Ela cita que falta linearidade entre os estados no processo de licenciamento – alguns, segundo ela, exigem licença de empreendimentos pequenos que deveriam ser dispensados pelos princípios da Lei Geral do Licenciamento Ambiental. “A gente vê que não há uma linearidade entre os estados para concessão dessas licenças. Para você ter ideia, existem estados, por exemplo, que estão exigindo licenças de pequenos empreendimentos, de pequenos data centers, com consumo não muito grande e que, nesses casos, a ideia é que não fosse necessária licença para esses empreendimentos”, disse. Principais assuntos tratados: - Redata estimula data centers, mas ainda há gargalos no licenciamento estadual. - Falta linearidade entre os estados, e alguns exigem licença de empreendimentos pequenos que deveriam ser dispensados. - Tendência é que investidores busquem localizar data centers perto de subestações. - Litígios climáticos já surgem nos EUA, e o Redata tenta blindar projetos; - Insegurança jurídica vem do Judiciário, do legislador e do regulador, e o Redata busca previsibilidade mínima. - Na mobilidade elétrica, Portugal tem gestão unificada e serviço público, enquanto o Brasil adota lógica comercial com liberdade de preço. artigo.texto: Especialistas explicam quem fica com o valor do carbono A advogada Ana Carolina de Campos Honora e Larissa Albino, da Future Climate Group, analisam como a receita dos créditos chega a povos indígenas e comunidades tradicionais e o que a Lei no 15.042/2024 já assegura nesses territórios O avanço do mercado de carbono no Brasil tem alcançado territórios de povos indígenas, quilombolas e outras comunidades tradicionais, onde se localiza parte dos projetos de maior potencial, como os de redução de emissões por desmatamento e degradação florestal (REDD+). Nesse contexto, a advogada socioambiental Ana Carolina de Campos Honora, doutoranda em Mudança Social e Participação Política pela Universidade de São Paulo (USP), e a oceanógrafa (UFES) e mestre em Planejamento Energético (COPPE/UFRJ) Larissa Albino, gerente de Operações de Clima e Inteligência Artificial da Future Climate Group, examinam uma pergunta ainda sem resposta simples: quem fica com o valor do carbono. Para elas, o debate vai além do volume financeiro dos créditos. "A discussão não se limita à geração de valor: é preciso saber quanto efetivamente chega às comunidades, segundo quais regras e com que grau de influência sobre o desenho, a negociação e a governança dos projetos", afirmam. Uma cadeia extensa entre o crédito e o território Segundo as especialistas, não há um número único que indique a fatia destinada às comunidades, e essa ausência integra o problema. A receita se dilui entre desenvolvimento do projeto, estruturação jurídica, auditoria, certificação, intermediação e venda. A parcela da repartição de benefícios costuma ser pactuada caso a caso, em contratos privados entre a comunidade, ou suas entidades representativas, e o desenvolvedor. O retorno também varia de forma. Estudo apresentado em 2023 no encontro da Sociedade Brasileira de Economia Ecológica (EcoEco) apontou que, em projetos REDD+ da Amazônia, os mecanismos vão de pagamentos em dinheiro a regularização fundiária, infraestrutura, apoio produtivo e fortalecimento de organizações locais. Para Ana Carolina e Larissa, essa diversidade dificulta a comparação entre iniciativas e pode ocultar quanto de fato permanece no território. O que a legislação já prevê No campo legal, a Lei nº 15.042/2024 criou o Sistema Brasileiro de Comércio de Emissões de Gases de Efeito Estufa (SBCE) e trouxe a primeira garantia federal explícita no tema. O artigo 47 assegura a povos indígenas e comunidades tradicionais, via entidades representativas, o direito de vender créditos de carbono e Certificados de Redução ou Remoção Verificada de Emissões (CRVEs) gerados em suas terras, cumpridas as salvaguardas socioambientais. A comercialização depende de consentimento obtido em consulta livre, prévia e informada, nos termos da Convenção nº 169 da Organização Internacional do Trabalho (OIT), custeada pelo desenvolvedor. A lei exige repartição justa e equitativa, gestão participativa dos recursos em conta específica e garante às comunidades ao menos 50% dos créditos de projetos de remoção e 70% nos de REDD+ de abordagem de mercado. A operacionalização desses mecanismos ainda depende de regulamentação, iniciada parcialmente pela Resolução nº 19, de 1º de agosto de 2025, da Comissão Nacional para REDD+ (CONAREDD+). As duas lembram que a norma já foi questionada: em agosto de 2026, o Ministério Público Federal (MPF) recomendou a revisão do artigo 7º, por entender que planos de consulta feitos pelo Estado podem enfraquecer o veto de cada comunidade e ignorar protocolos autônomos. Certificação e integridade Outra camada de regras vem de padrões privados, como Verra, Gold Standard e Cercarbono, que exigem salvaguardas sociais e planos de repartição, mas priorizaram a comprovação de processos em vez de resultados distributivos uniformes. Em novembro de 2024, o Conselho de Integridade do Mercado Voluntário de Carbono (ICVCM) aprovou três metodologias de REDD+ e apontou que versões antigas da Verra, fora da avaliação, respondiam por cerca de um quarto dos créditos aposentados em 2023. Consulta não equivale a poder de decisão Para Ana Carolina e Larissa, a comunidade ser ouvida e poder recusar um projeto é fundamental, mas difere de ter assento real na negociação. "O direito de ser consultada e de recusar a implementação de um projeto não assegura às comunidades, por si só, condições equitativas de negociação sobre aspectos essenciais da relação contratual, como a definição de preços, a duração dos contratos, os critérios de reajuste, a governança dos fundos e a destinação das receitas", observam. Assimetrias de informação técnica, jurídica e comercial podem desequilibrar essa participação. artigo.texto: The 442 MWh Smareg 13 battery energy storage system (BESS) project in Vöhringen, Bavaria, Germany, is advancing through a partnership between ju:niz Energy and Envision Energy. Also known as Vöhringen II, the project will add large-scale electricity storage capacity to ju:niz Energy’s German portfolio and support grid flexibility as renewable energy generation expands. Announced on November 9, 2026, Smareg 13 will provide 442 MWh of energy storage capacity. The project will use Envision Energy’s Gen 8 battery storage platform. Additionally, it is designed for four-hour storage and will feature grid-forming capabilities to support grid stability. However, the announcement did not disclose its power output in MW, investment value or expected completion date. ju:niz Energy will oversee project development, financing and delivery. It will also manage the facility’s long-term operation. Meanwhile, Envision Energy will supply the battery storage technology and support project delivery. Smareg 13 is the third project under the companies’ partnership. Together, their portfolio will reach nearly 600 MWh. However, this figure represents the combined capacity of their projects, not Smareg 13 alone. Smareg 13 BESS: Project Scope and Technical Specifications The Smareg 13 BESS project will be built next to the existing Smareg 12 battery storage facility in Vöhringen. Additionally, this location will expand ju:niz Energy’s storage presence in the area. It will also strengthen the company’s collaboration with Envision Energy. However, Smareg 12 is already operational, while Smareg 13 remains a separate project under development. The installation will use Envision’s Gen 8 battery energy storage platform. It combines battery technology with grid-forming capabilities. Additionally, these controls can help stabilise grid voltage and frequency. However, their performance will depend on the system configuration and the requirements of the connected network. The four-hour storage design means the facility is intended to discharge energy over a longer period than a typical two-hour battery installation. However, the exact discharge rate, usable energy, efficiency and operating parameters for the project have not been disclosed yet. The Smareg 13 BESS project also features a low-noise design to address site acoustic requirements. Additionally, this is important for battery installations near existing developments and noise-sensitive areas. Cooling systems and other equipment can affect noise levels. However, specific noise limits and performance figures remain undisclosed. Development Status and Delivery Outlook Smareg 13 BESS project is currently at an advanced stage of development. Construction has also not started. The project’s commissioning date and cost have also not been disclosed yet. The project builds on a partnership involving two earlier battery storage developments. However, Envision stated that those projects had not yet completed delivery when Smareg 13 was announced. Consequently, the new development expands the companies’ project pipeline, while further delivery milestones remain to be confirmed. Contribution to Germany’s Energy Infrastructure Battery energy storage systems help balance electricity supply and demand. They charge when power is available and discharge when the grid needs additional electricity. Additionally, they support Germany’s growing use of wind and solar energy. These renewable sources vary with weather conditions and time of day. Smareg 13 aims to provide additional flexibility and grid-balancing capacity in Bavaria. However, its contribution will depend on construction completion, grid connection and operational performance. Furthermore, the project will support the wider expansion of grid-scale storage infrastructure. This is essential for managing changing electricity generation patterns and maintaining a reliable power supply. Other countries in Europe are also working to increase their battery storage portfolio. Some such as the UK are even repurposing former coal site for storage projects as it being done at the Fiddler’s Ferry BESS site in Warrington, England. For ju:niz Energy, the development adds to a business model covering project development, financing, construction and long-term operation. For Envision Energy, it extends the company’s battery technology deployment in Germany through a growing relationship with a local storage developer. However, the companies have not yet disclosed the full project schedule, financing structure or commercial operating arrangements. Envision Energy : Supplier of the Gen 8 battery storage platform and technology and project delivery partner. SMAREG 13 GmbH & Co. artigo.texto: Researchers at Dongguk University have developed an ultrathin anode-less thin-film battery architecture designed to enhance operational stability and volumetric energy density while maintaining an overall cell thickness of only 2.77 micrometers. The experimental study introduces an engineered tin and carbon bilayer on the current collector alongside an integrated prelithiation step, establishing a structural framework that guides uniform lithium deposition and mitigates degradation during continuous electrochemical cycling. All-solid-state batteries have emerged as prominent candidates for next-generation energy storage applications because replacing conventional liquid electrolytes with solid counterparts offers substantial theoretical improvements in device safety and energy density. Despite these intrinsic benefits, solid-state systems that utilize lithium metal anodes frequently suffer from severe operational instabilities arising from non-uniform lithium plating and stripping across the solid interface. In this operational format, the battery is assembled without an active anode layer; instead, lithium ions stored within the cathode migrate across the solid electrolyte during the initial charge cycle and plate directly onto the bare current collector to create the negative electrode in situ. This design substantially elevates volumetric energy density and simplifies device fabrication, presenting particular utility for micro-scale and thin-film form factors. Standard anode-less configurations remain highly susceptible to rapid capacity decay caused by cumulative lithium loss. Non-uniform nucleation frequently induces uneven lithium morphology, yielding electrically isolated fragments of inactive metal commonly described as dead lithium. Furthermore, the repeated stripping of metallic lithium during discharge can trigger mechanical delamination and loss of physical contact with the rigid solid electrolyte, severely compromising cycling reversibility and overall battery life. To overcome these interfacial failure modes, an engineering team led by Professor Hyun-Suk Kim from the Department of Energy and Materials Engineering at Dongguk University in South Korea investigated surface modification strategies for the metallic substrate. Their work, published in Advanced Energy Materials following initial online availability on May 7, 2026, focused on regulating early-stage nucleation dynamics through targeted material coatings applied directly to current collectors. The researchers conducted a systematic screening evaluation comparing carbon-only coatings, metal-only coatings, and combined metal-and-carbon hybrid bilayers applied to substrate surfaces. Through this experimental analysis, the team determined that introducing an active seed interlayer effectively promoted homogeneous lithium nucleation under rigorous anode-less conditions. Among all tested formulations, a tin and carbon bilayer applied to a bare copper current collector demonstrated the most favorable deposition behavior, nucleation kinetics, and interfacial stability. Detailed mechanistic investigations revealed complementary functional roles for the individual components of the tin and carbon bilayer. The underlying tin layer facilitates lithium nucleation by substantially lowering the energetic barrier and enhancing interfacial alloy formation. Concurrently, the carbon overlayer governs subsequent lithium crystal growth, mitigating irregular dendrite-like morphology and physically stabilizing the dynamic interfacial region formed between tin and metallic lithium. To further reinforce electrochemical stability, the team incorporated a precise prelithiation step immediately following the synthesis of the tin-and-carbon-coated copper current collector. During this stage, an ultrathin metallic lithium layer was deposited onto the modified collector surface to serve as an internal lithium reservoir. The complete thin-film solid-state cell was constructed by combining an amorphous lithium vanadium oxide cathode, an inorganic lithium phosphorus oxynitride solid electrolyte, and the modified copper current collector. When subjected to electrochemical testing at a cycling rate of 0.01 C, the resulting microbattery attained a volumetric energy density of 235.13 watt-hours per liter at its 100th cycle, demonstrating sustained energy delivery across extended charge and discharge operations. Structural analysis of the working electrodes revealed that during the initial plating process, a three-dimensionally textured tin-lithium alloy phase developed within the seed interlayer. This textured matrix possessed the mechanical resilience necessary to accommodate dynamic volume swings and morphological adjustments during subsequent stripping and plating cycles, preventing interfacial detachment from the solid electrolyte. The engineered current collector platform illustrates how combining interfacial surface chemistry with targeted lithium-inventory management can address fundamental degradation modes in anode-less solid-state systems. The peer-reviewed investigation, formally titled “Pushing Energy Density Limits: Anode-Less Solid-State Battery Integrated with Amorphous Lithium Vanadium Oxide Thin-Film Cathode,” was documented in Volume 16, Issue 31 of Advanced Energy Materials on August 19, 2026, following its initial online release on May 7, 2026. Registered under digital object identifier 10.1002/aenm.71042, the experimental study details an architectural breakthrough in energy storage that reconciles the severe mechanical and interfacial challenges inherent to solid-state systems. Corresponding author Dr. Hyun-Suk Kim, who currently serves as a Professor in the Department of Energy and Materials Engineering at Dongguk University in the Republic of Korea, earned his master’s degree in 2003 and his doctorate in 2006 from the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology. artigo.texto: Calibrant Energy has closed a $145 million debt financing facility led by Investec to support solar and battery storage projects across multiple U.S. electricity markets, including a 120 megawatt-hour (MWh) battery energy storage system serving a hyperscale data center customer in PJM. Announced November 10, 2026, the financing combines the recapitalization of operating assets with funding for new construction as the company expands its energy infrastructure portfolio. Citi, Liberty Bank and Siemens Financial Services also participated in the facility. Calibrant said construction mobilization has begun for the 120 MWh battery project, although it has not identified the data center customer, project location, battery supplier or expected completion date. The transaction comes as data center developers face increasing difficulty securing electricity and timely grid connections. Calibrant is positioning battery storage as a way for large electricity users to manage their demand more flexibly, potentially reducing the infrastructure requirements associated with connecting new facilities. $145M financing supports existing and new energy assets The Investec-led facility covers solar and battery storage projects across several U.S. power markets. Its structure serves two purposes: refinancing or recapitalizing operating assets and providing capital for new construction. This makes the transaction broader than a single-project construction loan. Calibrant is using the financing to support an established portfolio while advancing additional infrastructure for large commercial and industrial electricity users. The company has not disclosed how the $145 million is divided between operating assets and new developments. It has also not identified the individual projects included in the financing, provided the loan’s maturity or interest rate, or disclosed how much capital will support the 120 MWh data center installation. Calibrant develops, finances, owns and operates distributed energy infrastructure, including solar generation and battery storage. Its turnkey model allows customers to obtain energy infrastructure without funding the full upfront construction cost themselves. Backed by Macquarie Asset Management, Calibrant reported more than 2.2 gigawatts (GW) of power capacity and 5.9 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of battery storage across projects in operation, under construction or covered by exclusive development agreements. The company also disclosed that its portfolio includes additional battery storage sites associated with the same hyperscale data center customer involved in the 120 MWh project. However, it has not provided their locations, capacities or individual development schedules. 120 MWh battery project targets PJM data center power constraints The largest specifically identified battery installation within the financing portfolio is a 120 MWh system serving an undisclosed hyperscale data center customer in the PJM electricity market. Calibrant said site mobilization has begun, marking a move from project financing toward construction. The company has not released the system’s power rating in megawatts, so its discharge duration cannot yet be established. That distinction is important when evaluating the project’s ability to support a data center. A battery’s MW rating determines how much electricity it can deliver at a given moment, while its MWh capacity measures the amount of energy it can store and discharge. For example, a 120 MWh battery rated at 30 MW could theoretically deliver its full rated output for four hours. However, Calibrant has not confirmed that configuration, and the actual discharge duration will depend on the project’s undisclosed power rating and operating conditions. The company says its engineered storage systems allow energy-intensive customers to control when and how they draw electricity from the grid. By charging batteries during selected periods and discharging them when demand rises, data centers can potentially reduce peak grid demand and offer utilities a more flexible load. Calibrant argues that this approach can support faster interconnection timelines and reduce the need for costly grid infrastructure upgrades that might otherwise affect other electricity customers. However, the announcement does not identify which specific grid upgrades the 120 MWh project could avoid, the utility responsible for its interconnection or the operating restrictions attached to the customer’s electricity supply. The extent to which the battery can accelerate the data center’s connection will depend on those arrangements. Previous projects demonstrate Calibrant’s data center strategy The PJM installation builds on Calibrant’s earlier partnerships with data center operators seeking alternatives to lengthy utility infrastructure upgrades. In October 2025, Calibrant and Aligned Data Centers announced plans for a 31 MW/62 MWh battery system at Aligned’s Hillsboro campus in Oregon. The companies designed the installation to help the data center obtain grid power and scale its operations years earlier than conventional utility upgrades would otherwise allow. The project involves coordination with a regional utility to use battery storage as a flexibility resource. Rather than treating the data center as an inflexible electricity consumer, the arrangement allows its power demand to respond to grid requirements. Calibrant also partnered with Iron Mountain in February 2026 to deploy a 23 MWh battery system at an Iron Mountain data center in New Jersey. The installation is designed to integrate with an existing 7.2 MW rooftop solar facility. These projects demonstrate two applications of Calibrant’s model: using battery storage to facilitate data center grid access and combining storage with existing on-site renewable generation. artigo.texto: Industrial Manufacturing Data Center Ballot Measures Pass by Wide Margins in Dozens of Communities In last week's elections, voters in small and rural communities adopted dozens of local proposals to pause, limit or ban construction of data centers. Released Tuesday, November 10, 2026 Written by John Egan for IIR News Intelligence (Sugar Land, Texas) Summary In last week's elections, voters in small and rural communities adopted dozens of local proposals to pause, limit or ban construction of data centers. Voters Turn Against Data Centers in Local Elections On November 3, voters in 40 local jurisdictions across 10 states turned decisively against data centers, voting to either pause, impede or ban them by 3-to-1 or 4-to-1 margins, according to data tracked by the ballot-tracking website Ballotpedia. The local results are best read as strong, place-specific NIMBY ("Not in My Backyard") resistance in communities where the issue was salient enough to reach the ballot, typically in smaller and rural communities. In a comparatively small handful of local communities, voters backed data center bans, moratoria, size limits or extra review requirements. But there were no state-wide or national data center measures on the November 3 ballot. Ohio alone had 21 data center measures, all of which went against data centers. In addition, seven Illinois communities also voted against data center measures. Small or rural communities in California, Florida, Kansas, Maine, Nevada, New Jersey and Wisconsin also voted against data center-related measures on Election Day, Ballotpedia said. Earlier this year, the vote-tracking website said voters opposed data center measures in six small communities in New Hampshire, Wisconsin, Michigan and California. Later this year, voters will decide the fate of data center initiatives in three small communities in Arkansas and North Dakota, Ballotpedia said. Only one of those local measures passed: In Harwood, North Dakota, voters rejected a proposal that would require additional review before the city could approve of future industrial developments, including data centers. Although data center measures appeared on ballots for federal, state and local offices, the results do not appear to signal a generalized, national turn against the data centers many see as key to dominating 21st century economic and national security strength. In an NBC voter exit poll, voters said four issues--government corruption, cost of living, the war in Iran and immigration enforcement--were the most important issues for them. Approximately 56% said artificial intelligence (AI) and data centers were a crucial or major factor in their vote for Congress. By the Numbers - 41: Number of initiatives relating to data centers that went before the voters in small and rural communities in 10 states November 3. Voters in nearly all cases opposed data centers. - 6: Number of local initiatives in four states opposing or limiting data centers that were voted on before November 3. - 3: Number of voter initiatives relating to data centers in Arkansas and North Dakota that will be voted on in December. Data Centers Likely to Continue Moving Forward The scope and scale of U.S. data center construction plans is unprecedented. For more on that, see September 22, 2026, article - As Data Center Construction Plans Soar, U.S. Electric Utilities Race to Serve Once-in-a-Lifetime Load Growth. Despite votes against data centers in small and rural communities in a number of states, voters surveyed in a national exit poll from NBC, and a national pre-Election Day poll from Fox News, agreed that other issues, among them government corruption, high prices, the war in Iran and immigration enforcement, were far more important to voters across the country. That said, Big Tech companies and data center developers will have to work with a very different Congress and a number of new governors. On a national level, Democrats flipped at least seven seats in the U.S. Senate and at least 41 in the House of Representatives, with about two dozen races still undecided. But both houses will have Democratic majorities when the next congressional term begins in January. Although a few newly elected senators strongly oppose data centers, they will be the most junior members in that chamber when they take their oath of office in two months. Junior members of the U.S. Senate typically do not have the ability to push their measures through that body absent broad support from their party, or from the other party. Election Day also brought a new crop of Democratic governors to office, and some of them opposed data centers. Voters elected new governors in Texas, Georgia and Ohio, states where the previous executives had been enthusiastic supporters of data centers. Those three states accounted for about 173 gigawatts (GW) of data center capacity, roughly 39% of the data center pipeline, according to an analysis by Industrial Info Resources. That said, the outlook for data center construction is not black and white. For example, of the 173 GW of planned data center capacity in Texas, Georgia and Ohio, 14.2 GW already is under construction. And no state, aside from New York, has instituted a pause on data center construction. Will the newly elected governors of those three states follow through on their campaign promises to oppose data center construction? If so, executive orders won't be forthcoming until next January at the earliest. Legislation will take even longer. In either case, litigation may commence. In several states, voters cast their ballots for candidates vying to be members of the state public utility commission, which regulate utilities. Early indications are that several data center skeptics were elected. artigo.texto: BYD faz acordo com a TIM para conexão da frota e da fábrica no Brasil Com parceria, diferentes modelos da marca passarão a contar com chips virtuais (eSIM) da TIM, com conexão 4G em 100% das cidades brasileiras e 5G em 1,1 mil cidades A TIM fechou um contrato com a BYD para fornecer internet a toda a frota de veículos leves da montadora chinesa no Brasil, além do seu polo industrial. Com a parceria, os diferentes modelos da marca passarão a contar com chips virtuais (eSIM) da TIM, com conexão 4G em 100% das cidades brasileiras e 5G em 1,1 mil cidades onde a operadora oferece cobertura. A previsão é de que cerca de 200 mil veículos da montadora chinesa contem com essa conectividade embarcada nos próximos 24 meses. Assim, a BYD busca avançar no desenvolvimento de novas funcionalidades que envolvam serviços conectados. Com o crescimento de serviços como inteligência artificial e uso de funções como mapas e streaming a bordo, um carro já tem consumo de dados quase equiparável a de um plano básico pós-pago, tipo 'controle'. Do lado da TIM, o negócio representa uma expansão no setor automotivo, onde já oferece conexão para cerca de 630 mil veículos. A tele italiana possui uma parceria com a antiga FCA (Fiat Chrysler Automóveis) – hoje parte do grupo Stellantis – para fornecer conectividade 4G e eSIM em veículos das marcas Fiat, Jeep e Ram no Brasil. O contrato entre a TIM e a BYD envolve também a implantação de infraestrutura dedicada de redes 5G e 4G no complexo industrial da montadora em Camaçari, na Bahia. Essa é a maior fábrica de veículos eletrificados da América Latina, com 4,6 milhões de m². O projeto prevê a instalação de sete pontos de cobertura externa e 63 equipamentos distribuídos entre os galpões e as áreas operacionais, garantindo uma rede preparada para acompanhar o crescimento da produção e as demandas tecnológicas do complexo.

artigo.texto: LONDON: The European Union (EU) and the United Kingdom (UK) are in the final stages of a deal to link their emissions markets, a move that would boost liquidity and eventually save companies millions of euros in carbon border taxes. The agreement, to be announced at a key summit later this month, would enable carbon permits to be traded across the two emissions systems, almost six years after Britain started its own cap-and-trade program in the wake of Brexit. Negotiators have already ironed out details on emissions caps, supply controls and free permits, according to people with knowledge of the matter. The treatment of financial derivatives is the only outstanding issue. The EU’s carbon market is the region’s key way to meet its carbon reduction goals. Started in 2005, the market imposes gradually shrinking emissions limits on around 10,000 facilities in sectors from steel and cement to fertilisers, power production and aviation. Once linked, it will allow mutual recognition of permits from both markets for compliance, helpful for companies with operations in both regions. The linkage deal is set to be one of the main deliverables at the Nov 20 meeting of UK and EU leaders, alongside matching university tuition fees for students travelling between the two. Other areas of agreement include committing to minimising the effect of their trade measures on vulnerable sectors like steel and electric cars, and deepening cooperation on cyber threats, Bloomberg reported last month. The European Commission declined to comment on the agreement, in line with its long-standing policy of not commenting on draft documents. The agreement will not automatically exempt the parties from their respective Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanisms (CBAM), which put emissions costs on certain imported products to shield local producers against competitors from regions with laxer climate rules. Instead, it will pave the way for a waiver once the parties fulfill certain condition embedded in their domestic laws, the people said. The EU law sets two requirements for such a move: full linkage with its emissions trading system (ETS) and effective carbon pricing without preferential rebates. Once those are met, the EU will add the UK to a list of countries outside of the CBAM regulation scope via a delegated act. While the EU carbon border tax became operational this year, with the first compliance deadline set for September, the UK mechanism is to kick off at the start of 2027. UK carbon prices have already narrowed their discount to the EU ETS market since the two parties committed last year to establishing a link. The UK carbon contract for December closed at a £64.81 per tonne last Friday while benchmark EU allowances were at €86.55. The price gap could shrink further over the next two years, as UK allowances move closer to EU permits, Moutaz Altaghlibi, Senior Energy Economist at ABN Amro wrote in a note on Nov 5. That would mean UK firms having to pay more for permits. “Linking the systems should also improve liquidity, make carbon prices more consistent across Europe, and reduce CBAM-related costs and paperwork for trade between the UK and EU,” he said. Although the idea of re-linking carbon markets has been discussed for years, Britain’s current Prime Minister Andy Burnham is also working to bring the UK closer to Europe on a broader level. A key parameter in the agreement will be the cap on emissions in the UK ETS. The EU is set to recognise emissions caps in the British system in the 2028 to 2030 period, according to people with knowledge of the issue. From 2031, the annual UK issuance will be capped at 7.1% of permits to be issued in the EU ETS. The UK will also create its own Market Stability Reserve, a mechanism that the EU has had for more than a decade to automatically control the supply of carbon permits and alleviate a glut of allowances that emerged and weighed on prices. — Bloomberg

artigo.texto: Governo planeja investir R$ 46,3 milhões em plataforma de gerenciamento de dados em data centers O Ministério das Comunicações informou nesta segunda-feira (9) que o governo federal planeja investir R$ 46,3 milhões no desenvolvimento de uma plataforma de gerenciamento e distribuição de dados entre mini data centers no Brasil. Batizado de Prisma, o projeto utilizará inteligência artificial para identificar onde e como os dados devem ser processados, distribuindo automaticamente os recursos computacionais entre diferentes infraestruturas. Na prática, o Executivo espera que a tecnologia reduza gastos com energia e custos operacionais, acelere o acesso às informações e aumente a proteção de dados estratégicos. Os recursos serão administrados pela Financiadora de Estudos e Projetos (Finep), e o projeto será executado pelo Centro Brasileiro de Inovação em Tecnologias da Informação e da Comunicação (CPQD). O prazo de execução é de 36 meses, a partir da celebração do convênio de pesquisa, desenvolvimento e inovação entre a Finep e o CPQD. O ministro das Comunicações, Frederico Filho, afirmou que o projeto possibilitará maior autonomia e soberania no tratamento de dados no País. “Investir em tecnologia nacional é garantir que o Brasil tenha mais autonomia para proteger suas informações e desenvolver soluções para os desafios do futuro. Estamos fortalecendo a inovação brasileira e criando condições para uma infraestrutura digital mais moderna, segura e sustentável, reduzindo nossa dependência de tecnologias desenvolvidas no exterior”, afirmou em nota.

artigo.texto: Newswise — O3-type layered oxides are attractive SIB cathodes because they combine high theoretical capacity with high initial sodium content and flexible TM chemistry. At high voltages (≥4.0 V), deep sodium extraction weakens electrostatic screening between adjacent TM–O slabs, promoting slab gliding, O–P phase transitions, and redox-coupled distortion of TMO6 octahedra. These structural changes can accelerate lattice degradation and compromise electrochemical reversibility. Electrochemically inactive dopants can reinforce the framework, but they may also dilute the redox-active components and reduce reversible capacity. Moreover, their selection has remained largely empirical, often guided by average ionic radius, oxidation state, or elemental composition. Such averaged descriptors cannot fully account for the distribution of ionic field strengths among constituent TM cations, which is associated with local bonding heterogeneity, strain accumulation, and nonuniform phase evolution. A quantitative descriptor that connects dopant chemistry with ionic field strength heterogeneity is therefore essential for designing structurally reversible, high-voltage O3-type cathodes. The study, published (DOI: 10.1021/jacs.6c11691) online on October 20, 2026, in the Journal of the American Chemical Society, comes from Nankai University, Nanjing University of Science and Technology, the China Spallation Neutron Source Science Center, the Institute of High Energy Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences, and the Haihe Laboratory of Sustainable Chemical Transformations. The team combined synthesis, structural analysis, electrochemical testing, and computation to test the design rule for O3-type SIB cathodes. The work systematically investigates how ionic field strength disparity influences local TM–O coordination, phase evolution, lattice-strain accumulation, and electrochemical stability under high-voltage operation. The study compares a low-η cathode (η = 0.34) with a high-η analogue (η = 0.395). Both adopt the same O3-type framework, but the low-η material follows a more reversible O3–P3–O3 path structural evolution, and avoids the additional high-voltage phase transitions seen in the high-η sample. In situ X-ray diffraction reveals smaller changes in lattice parameters for the low-η cathode, indicating improved structural stability during deep desodiation. Differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (DEMS) shows no detectable O₂ evolution within the investigated voltage window and substantially suppressed CO₂ generation, suggesting mitigated oxygen-related degradation and interfacial side reactions. Furthermore, synchrotron X-ray absorption spectroscopy and atomic-resolution strain mapping reveal reduced local coordination disorder, improved structural reversibility, and suppressed heterogeneous strain accumulation. These improvements are consistent with an ionic field strength compensation mechanism, in which inactive cations with intermediate field strengths mitigate disparities among redox-active cations, promoting more homogeneous TM–O bonding and coordinated structural evolution during cycling. Notably, the low-η cathode exhibits a much smaller increase in η during desodiation (7.35%) than the high-η counterpart (17.72%), further supporting the importance of maintaining a stable ionic field strength distribution. The descriptor also enables composition-guided dopant screening, as demonstrated by two additional cathode chemistries with improved electrochemical performance. A control pair with comparable average ionic radii and TM valence states but different η values further confirms the significance of ionic field strength disparity beyond conventional averaged descriptors. The authors said η turns dopant selection from an empirical search into a quantitative design task. They said the descriptor captures local chemical-field disparities that average composition, radius, or valence cannot resolve, and that lowering it helps synchronize TM–O bond changes and phase evolution during deep desodiation. They added that low η does not require maximal compositional complexity and that simpler cation combinations may avoid capacity and processing penalties. They also said the framework should be extended cautiously to oxygen-redox cathodes, where TM migration and lattice-oxygen loss add separate failure modes. The approach could accelerate cathode development for stationary storage and high-voltage SIBs by narrowing dopant candidates before costly cell testing. Because η is calculated from formal valence, ionic radius, and cation fraction, it can be adapted to other multicomponent O3-type layered oxides. The results also suggest that low disparity, rather than high entropy alone, should guide composition design; excessive inactive ions can reduce reversible capacity and increase synthesis risk. Before commercial use, the rule needs validation across more compositions, including oxygen-redox-active cathodes, and under practical full-cell conditions. By connecting cation-level chemical descriptors with macroscopic electrochemical performance, this work provides a quantitative foundation for the design of more durable sodium-ion battery cathodes. ### References DOI Original Source URL https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.6c11691 Funding information The Acknowledgments list the Ministry of Science and Technology of China (2025YFE0100200); National Natural Science Foundation of China (22479080, 92372203, 92372001); Tianjin Natural Science Foundation Project (24JCJQJC00220, 24ZXZSSS00310); Haihe Laboratory of Sustainable Chemical Transformations (25HHWCSS00013); Fundamental Research Funds for the Central Universities of Nankai University (63253167, 63261001); and the “111 Center” (B25010). artigo.texto: Energy Investment LLC and CORNEX New Energy have entered into a strategic cooperation agreement to develop a 1 GWh battery energy storage system (BESS) project in Romania, supporting the country’s efforts to strengthen energy storage infrastructure and integrate renewable energy into its electricity network. The agreement follows an announcement made in June 2026 during The smarter E Europe exhibition, held in Munich from June 23 to 25. CORNEX highlighted the partnership in its official communication regarding its participation in the event, referring to a 1 GWh agreement with Energy Investment for a project in Romania. Under the arrangement, Energy Investment LLC will be responsible for the complete development and execution of the project, while CORNEX New Energy will supply the battery energy storage technology. The cooperation agreement represents a development partnership and does not indicate that the proposed storage capacity is already operational. According to information published by Energy Investment on LinkedIn on June 26, 2026, the company will oversee the project’s development and implementation. Romanian publication Profit.ro also reported on June 29 that CORNEX would provide the storage technology. Marius Ion, Founder and CEO of Energy Investment LLC, stated that energy storage would play an important role in Romania’s energy transition by enabling renewable electricity to be used when required by the power system. He highlighted that the partnership with CORNEX would provide access to the technology needed to advance the proposed 1 GWh project. The company indicated that the first projects could reach commissioning in 2027. However, the timeline remains dependent on several development stages, including permitting, grid connection, regulatory authorizations, financing and equipment procurement. The proposed project is expected to support Romania’s renewable energy integration by providing storage capabilities to improve electricity system flexibility. The partnership also reflects growing cooperation between international technology suppliers and project developers as European markets expand their battery storage infrastructure. artigo.texto: Seu navegador não suporta esse video. Oposição terá, no mínimo, 54 senadores, caminha para maioria robusta na Câmara e elege governadores em estados importantes e simbólicos. O mercado financeiro focado em tecnologia não tem vivido seus melhores dias recentemente e o índice Nasdaq chegou a registrar sua maior queda diária desde abril de 2025 na última quinta-feira (5). A queda foi de 5,5% e resultou na redução de US$ 2,5 trilhões (R$ 13,4 trilhões em conversão direta) do valor de mercado das principais empresas do setor, influenciadas pelas midterms dos Estados Unidos. O motivo para esse derretimento abrupto tem relação com as recentes eleições de meio de mandato, as midterms norte-americanas. Na última rodada, a expressiva vitória do Partido Democrata contra o Partido Republicano no pleito acendeu o temor de que a expansão da inteligência artificial sofra mais regulações nas mãos dos democratas. A Nvidia, empresa mais poderosa do planeta e absoluta na venda de chips para servidores, viu suas ações caírem 9%. Com a rival direta, a AMD, a queda foi ainda mais chamativa e bateu nos 17%. O índice de semicondutores da Filadélfia (SOX) também registrou uma queda notória de 12%, o nível mais baixo dos últimos seis meses. O clima pesado não está restrito somente aos Estados Unidos e chega a outros países em um efeito cascata. Bolsas asiáticas, como a japonesa Nikkei e a sul-coreana Kospi, operaram em forte queda. O índice VIX, chamado de “termômetro do medo” em Wall Street, registrou seu maior salto desde 2024 e aumentou a apreensão dos acionistas. - 🪧Índice VIX (Termômetro do medo): essa é uma métrica de Wall Street que mede a expectativa de volatilidade do mercado para os próximos 30 dias. Quando o índice dispara, significa que há insegurança por parte de investidores e possibilidade de quedas na bolsa. IA pode esbarrar em decisões políticas Analistas do mercado financeiro mostram que o receio de acionistas e investidores é que os democratas façam força contra a construção de novos data centers em solo americano. Um dos motivos é o fato desses centros de dados exigirem grandes volumes de água para resfriar os servidores, além dos gastos em energia e o barulho. Uma estimativa do UBS aponta que quase 30% da capacidade adicional de data centers esperada para 2028 nos Estados Unidos tem risco de sofrer paralisações. Como o mercado de IA se expandiu rapidamente nos últimos anos, isso se tornou um empecilho para investidores da categoria, que demandam novas instalações para o treinamento dos modelos de IA. Gigantes responsáveis por essas tecnologias, como a Amazon e Alphabet (dona do Google) viram quedas de 2,2%. No caso da Microsoft, o recuo foi de 3,6%. Aliás, a companhia de Redmond já teria começado a apertar a supervisão de projetos terceirizados de data centers. Por falar em IA e problemas financeiros, o caso de infidelidade do CEO da Nvidia pode trazer grandes consequências à empresa e ao mercado global. artigo.texto: Prefeitura abre licitação de R$ 7 milhões para manter data center da Capital Empresa vencedora ficará responsável pelo suporte por 2 anos A Prefeitura de Campo Grande lançou licitação para contratar uma empresa especializada em manter o funcionamento e a "alta disponibilidade" do data center da Capital. De acordo com o aviso de licitação publicado nesta segunda-feira (9), o Executivo pode investir até R$ 7 milhões. RESUMO Nossa ferramenta de IA resume a notícia para você! A Prefeitura de Campo Grande abriu licitação para contratar empresa que mantenha o funcionamento e a alta disponibilidade do data center da Capital, com investimento de até R$ 7 milhões. O contrato prevê estrutura em contêiner, operação ininterrupta, manutenção preventiva, preditiva e corretiva, peças, insumos e suporte técnico por dois anos. Segundo a Agetec, o data center, no Horto Florestal, já existe, e a lei impede aditivos. As propostas vão até 25 de novembro de 2026, às 7h44. O edital prevê que a estrutura que dará suporte ao data center será um contêiner. A empresa vencedora deverá entregar a estrutura, com operação ininterrupta, manutenção integral preventiva, preditiva e corretiva, fornecer peças, insumos e suporte técnico para garantir a estabilidade e a segurança por dois anos. Ao Campo Grande News, o diretor-presidente da Agetec (Agência Municipal de Tecnologia da Informação e Inovação de Campo Grande), Leandro Basmage, explicou que já há um data center, localizado na região do Horto Florestal, e que a licitação é referente ao serviço que garante o funcionamento. Segundo ele, a licitação foi lançada porque a legislação não permite aditivos e renovação. O certame será coordenado pela Secretaria Especial de Licitações e Contratos. As empresas interessadas têm até as 7h44 do dia 25 de novembro de 2026 para enviar suas propostas. A sessão de disputa de preços será aberta logo em seguida, às 7h45 do mesmo dia, pelo site compras.campogrande.ms.gov.br. Receba as principais notícias do Estado pelo Whats. artigo.texto: A 31ª Conferência das Nações Unidas sobre Mudança do Clima (COP31), iniciada na segunda-feira (9), em Antália, na Turquia, colocou a execução dos compromissos internacionais como fiel das negociações entre os países. Até o dia 20, governos, instituições financeiras, empresas e organizações internacionais discutem mecanismos para transformar as metas do Acordo de Paris em investimentos, políticas públicas e redução das emissões de gases de efeito estufa. Para o agronegócio, a agenda inclui financiamento de sistemas produtivos resilientes, recuperação de terras degradadas, redução das emissões de metano e instrumentos econômicos relacionados à conservação ambiental. “Além de enviar sinais, a COP31 precisa acelerar as soluções”, afirmou Simon Stiell, secretário-executivo da Convenção-Quadro das Nações Unidas sobre Mudança do Clima (UNFCCC), durante a abertura oficial. Em seu discurso, Stiell cobrou medidas para ampliar o financiamento da adaptação climática, facilitar o acesso dos países aos recursos já comprometidos e acelerar a redução das emissões. A conferência ocorre em um momento no qual os governos precisam detalhar como executar seus planos nacionais, incluindo políticas de energia, uso da terra, indústria e infraestrutura. Um dos pontos apresentados pela presidência turca é a segurança alimentar, incluída entre os dez temas prioritários da Agenda de Ação da COP31. O programa contempla a relação entre disponibilidade de água, produção agrícola e mudanças climáticas, além do financiamento para mulheres agricultoras, participação de jovens e desenvolvimento de sistemas produtivos capazes de enfrentar eventos extremos. A proposta é coordenar iniciativas governamentais e privadas, embora os compromissos anunciados nessa agenda não tenham automaticamente o mesmo caráter das decisões negociadas entre os países. A conferência é presidida por Murat Kurum, ministro do Meio Ambiente, Urbanização e Mudança Climática da Turquia, enquanto Chris Bowen, ministro australiano de Mudança Climática e Energia, conduz as negociações formais. O arranjo entre os dois países foi definido durante a COP30, realizada em Belém, no Pará, em 2025. Na abertura, Kurum apresentou uma iniciativa denominada Climate Implementation Bridge, concebida para conectar necessidades locais de financiamento e tecnologia à capacidade de instituições e governos de executar projetos. A estrutura e os resultados desse mecanismo ainda dependem dos desdobramentos da conferência. Para o Brasil, que passou a presidência da COP à Turquia, uma das frentes é ampliar o financiamento de atividades agropecuárias relacionadas à recuperação de áreas degradadas e à redução de emissões. No primeiro dia, a programação do Pavilhão Brasil incluiu um debate organizado com a participação do Ministério da Agricultura e Pecuária, do Imaflora e de organizações internacionais sobre recuperação de terras agrícolas, segurança alimentar e mitigação de metano. A atividade integra os trabalhos da iniciativa RAIZ, voltada ao investimento em agricultura resiliente e à meta de degradação líquida zero de terras. A discussão prossegue em 11 de novembro, quando representantes da Organização das Nações Unidas para a Alimentação e a Agricultura (FAO), do Ministério da Agricultura e da coalizão internacional Food and Land Use Coalition participam de um encontro sobre investimentos na restauração produtiva de terras e em sistemas agroalimentares resilientes. Dois dias depois, em 13 de novembro, o tema retorna à programação brasileira em um painel com participação do Conselho Empresarial Mundial para o Desenvolvimento Sustentável (WBCSD), do Ministério da Agricultura e da consultoria Boston Consulting Group (BCG), dedicado à mobilização de capital internacional para a recuperação produtiva de áreas degradadas. A presença dessas iniciativas na programação coloca em discussão um dos desafios da transição agrícola: a disponibilidade de financiamento para práticas que exigem investimento antes de gerar retorno econômico. Recuperação de pastagens, melhoria do manejo do solo e adoção de sistemas integrados dependem de recursos, assistência técnica e acompanhamento dos resultados. O financiamento também aparece entre as prioridades das negociações internacionais. Stiell defendeu a implementação do compromisso de triplicar os recursos destinados à adaptação climática, estabelecido na conferência anterior. A questão envolve a capacidade dos países em desenvolvimento de financiar obras de infraestrutura, sistemas de produção, gestão de recursos hídricos e medidas de proteção contra secas e inundações. O acesso aos recursos, as condições de financiamento e os mecanismos de acompanhamento permanecem entre os assuntos que dependem de decisões dos governos. Mercado de carbono entra nas discussões Outra frente da participação brasileira é a implantação do Sistema Brasileiro de Comércio de Emissões (SBCE), criado para estabelecer um mercado regulado de carbono no país. O Ministério da Fazenda informou que uma das ações na COP31 será debater os avanços da regulamentação e da cooperação internacional nessa área. A programação inclui a participação da secretária extraordinária do Mercado de Carbono, Cristina Reis, em debates sobre mensuração, relato e verificação de emissões, contabilidade de carbono e integração entre os sistemas nacionais. O Brasil preside a Coalizão Aberta para Mercados Regulados de Carbono, lançada durante a COP30, com China e União Europeia na copresidência. Em 13 de novembro, representantes de governos e de instituições internacionais participam de uma discussão sobre a iniciativa. Para o dia 16 de novembro está prevista uma mesa-redonda com autoridades dos países integrantes. O trabalho pretende aproximar regras e metodologias dos diferentes mercados, uma questão que também interessa às empresas brasileiras com operações internacionais e compromissos de redução de emissões. “Chegamos à COP31 com uma agenda integrada de desenvolvimento econômico, inclusão e enfrent

artigo.texto: RWE and KKR join forces to deliver 2.8 gigawatts of new offshore wind capacity in the UK – an investment of around £12 billion 11.11.2026 RWE has started construction of its first Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) in Italy. The 62,5-megawatts (MW) Ragusa battery will be located in Sicily. It will consist of 42 containers with lithium-ion batteries, being able to deliver its maximum output for 4 hours. This corresponds to a nominal storage capacity of 262,5 megawatt hours (MWh). Commissioning is scheduled for the end of 2027. Sopna Sury, CEO RWE Renewables Europe & Australia: “The start of construction of our Ragusa battery storage marks an important milestone. We have been operating in Italy for many years, using the energy from the wind and the sun. In a world of growing renewable energy, battery storage systems are crucial for stabilising the grid and ensuring that electricity is used when it is needed most. Ragusa battery will be capable of covering the evening peak demand of around 21.000 households for 4 hours. We look forward to establishing further battery storage capacity in Italy soon – in addition to wind and solar power – in order to support Italy in building a resilient energy system.” Ragusa battery will provide balancing energy to stabilise the electricity grid. It also features the technology necessary to provide new grid forming services such as instantaneous reserve (inertia). In addition to the batteries, RWE will build the associated grid infrastructure. This includes a high-voltage transformer to connect to the 150-kV grid. Battery storage at RWE As a driver of the energy transition, RWE develops, builds and operates battery storage systems in the US, Europe and Australia. Globally, RWE currently operates battery storage systems with a total capacity of around 1.7 gigawatts (GW) and 3 GW are under construction. As an integral part of its growth strategy, RWE plans to significantly expand its battery storage capacities worldwide. RWE Renewables Italia – strong presence in Italy’s renewables market RWE is a key player in the Italian renewables market. The company takes an integrated project approach that incorporates the development, construction and operation as well as the marketing of wind farms and solar plants. With 18 onshore wind farms, one photovoltaic plant and three agrivoltaic plants in operation, RWE currently manages a total installed capacity of approximately 670 MW in Italy, enough to supply green electricity to more than 550,000 Italian households. In addition, RWE currently has around 200 MW of further wind and solar capacity under construction in Italy. artigo.texto: Solidion Technology Reaffirms Commitment to Address Growing Energy Storage Needs of AI Data Centers Solidion’s patented anode technology and PEAK UPS design target the space, lifespan and cost demands of AI-scale infrastructure. DALLAS, Oct. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — Solidion Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ: STI) (“Solidion Technology” or “the Company”), an advanced battery technology solutions provider, today reaffirmed its commitment to address energy storage for artificial intelligence and data center infrastructure, centered on its PEAK Series uninterruptible power supply (UPS) system. As AI workloads increase the power density of data centers, operators face growing pressure on the systems that keep facilities running during grid disruptions. Uninterruptible power supply (UPS) batteries take up floor space that could otherwise hold AI servers and additional computing equipment, and they require periodic replacement. Solidion’s approach is built around its PEAK Series, a UPS battery system built for AI data centers using its proprietary 5500 silicon-carbon anode cell, designed for AI data center environments and well positioned to address these evolving requirements. The Company’s strategy focuses on three priorities: - Energy density and space efficiency: Based on Company testing, PEAK is designed to reduce UPS footprint by up to 30%, freeing floor space for servers. - Reliability and longevity: The 5500 cell is designed to last up to three times longer than conventional backup systems, reducing replacement cycles and maintenance. Solidion is focused on advancing technologies intended to support demanding data center operating environments. - Materials-level innovation: Solidion’s portfolio of +385 patents covering silicon anodes, graphene and next generation battery chemistries, together with its pilot production facility in Dayton, Ohio, gives the Company a U.S. based foundation for developing data center energy storage. Jaymes Winters, Chairman and CEO of Solidion, said, AI infrastructure represents a compelling market for advanced energy storage, “Our focus is on translating our technology into practical commercial solutions that address real customer demand. We are not betting on which chips win; we are focused on supplying something every data center needs.” Solidion intends to continue pursuing opportunities to apply its battery technologies directly to end users READ the latest Batteries News shaping the battery market Solidion Technology Reaffirms Commitment to Address Growing Energy Storage Needs of AI Data Centers, source

artigo.texto: ‘We are all in’: Honda solid-state battery plans are advanced and could blow past BYD, Chery and more Dom works as CarsGuide's News Editor after starting his career at the Sydney Morning Herald's Drive section before moving into News Corp's automotive coverage. Read full bio CarsGuide puts every effort into ensuring the accuracy of the information it publishes. Double-check the details that matter to you before buying. Learn more about how we fact check. Key takeaways: - Honda is well advanced in its plans to produce solid-state batteries at scale - Honda Australia boss said solid-state batteries have cost, weight, performance, charging times benefits - The CEO said it was just a matter of reducing the time needed to make the cells so it can be scaled for mass-production A new electric car arms race is coming to a head, with multiple car and battery makers claiming solid-state cells are just around the corner. Honda Australia boss Jay Joseph told CarsGuide the benefits of the new electric car power-plant are off the charts. “Solid-state absolutely is a game-changer,” said Joseph. “Cost, weight, performance, charging times. It is a hard reset in the capability of battery electric vehicles (BEVs), and we are all in on that. “Dr Chris Brooks, who’s the chief scientist over in the lab that’s doing [solid-state development] absolutely believes this is a game-changer. You can get twice the energy density in the same way, or you can get the same energy density in half the weight at a dramatically reduced cost,” he said. Solid-state battery production problems Many carmakers have been claiming solid-state batteries are imminent for years, but all have blown past their claimed deadline. Joseph said there are two elements to this: one is the battery chemistry and the other is scaling production. Honda appears to have the chemistry sorted, with the company well advanced in the manufacturing stage. Subscribe to our newsletter Stay up to date with the CarsGuide weekly newsletter By subscribing you agree to our Privacy Policy. “The way batteries are developed, you develop the chemistry, you figure out what works, you do all the testing on that, and then you start figuring out how to manufacture it,” he said. “We’re fairly advanced in that production proof of concept. “It’s just getting the time out of the process so that we can scale it out.” Joseph explained the structure of solid-state batteries is more brittle and the testing environment for automotive is the toughest outside of military-specification, which is part of the difficulty getting the cells to market. Honda won’t waste solid-state benefits Joseph cautioned against carmakers wasting the benefits of the futuristic cells by making bigger and heavier electric cars to house them. He said the batteries could be used to make EVs lighter and deliver the same driving range as current vehicles. Lighter electric cars would be more efficient, drive better, be safer and create less wear and tear on roads and consumable parts such as brakes. Honda currently has one electric vehicle on sale in Australia, the compact Super One. It has a small battery that delivers a claimed range of 202km, but if it has a solid-state battery in the future it could have a driving range of more than 400km with the same sized power-source. Honda is building a new factory in the US state of Ohio to build large hybrid SUVs before switching to EVs. Honda’s solid-state proof of concept solid-state production line is also in Ohio, which points to potential future US-built large electric SUVs. Chery hot on Honda’s heels Chery has confirmed its Exlantix sub-brand - called Exeed in China - is headed to Australia in 2027. Exeed is the "crown jewel" in Chery’s stable and will be the first to debut the company’s solid-state battery tech in 2027. The first Exeed vehicle in China to score the new battery is claimed to have an electric driving range of up to 1500km. Chery Australia Chief Operating Officer Lucas Harris said “we won’t be left wanting” for solid-state battery-powered cars Down Under. When and what form those vehicles will be is still a mystery. artigo.texto: MINNEAPOLIMEDIA NEWS | Minneapolis Advances Data Center Restrictions as Residents Challenge Energy Demand, Water Use and the Future of Downtown Development With a temporary moratorium approaching expiration, the City Council faces a November 12 vote on regulations that would limit where data centers can operate and how much space their computing equipment can occupy. MINNEAPOLIS, MN (November 10, 2026). Minneapolis is moving toward its first specific zoning regulations for data centers as city officials confront growing public opposition to facilities that consume substantial electricity and water while offering developers another potential use for vacant commercial buildings. A City Council committee advanced proposed regulations Monday, November 9, setting up a full council vote scheduled for Thursday, November 12. The proposal would permit data centers in existing buildings within two downtown zoning districts while limiting the space devoted to servers and related computing equipment to 150,000 square feet. The debate comes as Minneapolis approaches the November 21 expiration of a six-month moratorium on new data centers. If city officials fail to adopt new regulations or extend the moratorium, additional facilities could continue to qualify for permits under existing zoning rules. The decision has implications for neighborhoods, electricity customers, water resources, commercial property owners and the city's long-term development strategy. Eight Existing Facilities, Limited Specific Regulation Minneapolis already has eight data centers. Yet the city's zoning code does not explicitly establish a separate regulatory category for them. Under existing rules, data centers can generally be permitted in 10 of the city's 15 primary zoning districts without specific limits on their size. That arrangement has become increasingly controversial as demand for computing capacity grows alongside artificial intelligence and cloud-based services. Data centers house servers, networking equipment and supporting infrastructure. Their operations require continuous electricity and systems capable of controlling equipment temperatures. The scale of those requirements varies substantially by facility, making it important to distinguish a smaller urban installation from a massive industrial computing campus. Minneapolis officials are attempting to establish standards before additional development proposals advance. A Proposal Focused on Downtown Buildings The ordinance recommended Monday would restrict data centers to certain existing buildings in two downtown zoning districts. It would also impose a 150,000-square-foot limit on white space, the area occupied by computing equipment and servers. That distinction matters because a building's total square footage can include offices, corridors, mechanical equipment and other areas not used directly for computing. Limiting white space is one way to regulate the scale of an operation through land-use authority. The proposal would narrow the range of locations where data centers could be developed, rather than permitting them broadly across the city. Supporters of tighter restrictions argue that facilities should not be allowed to expand without meaningful examination of their effects on surrounding neighborhoods and public infrastructure. Others contend that data centers could help restore activity and property value to underused downtown commercial buildings. Public Opposition Has Grown The proposal follows months of public debate. Approximately 50 people testified during an October Planning Commission hearing, while more than 1,600 public comments have been submitted concerning data center regulations. Reporting indicates that the overwhelming majority of those comments opposed additional data centers. Some residents have called for a complete ban. A council committee previously deadlocked 6–6 on such a proposal, demonstrating that elected officials remain divided over how restrictive the city's approach should be. The debate has intensified following opposition to a proposed data center at the former Minnesota Star Tribune printing facility. For opponents, the central concern is whether the economic benefits of new development justify the demands placed on public resources. Water and Electricity Are Central Questions Data centers can require substantial electricity to power servers and supporting systems. Some also consume significant water for cooling, depending on the technology used. Minneapolis planning officials have argued that the city's existing water infrastructure can accommodate facilities of the scale contemplated under the proposed ordinance. The city has the capacity to draw approximately 100 million gallons of water per day from the Mississippi River and currently uses roughly 55 million gallons daily, according to figures cited during the debate. Those numbers describe system capacity, not the water consumption of any particular proposed facility. One existing data center associated with Sleep Number has reportedly averaged approximately 3 million gallons of water per month. That example illustrates why residents want project-specific information rather than general assurances about capacity. Questions also remain about electricity demand, infrastructure upgrades and whether increased consumption could affect costs borne by other customers. Those effects depend on utility regulation, project design and the financial arrangements governing new infrastructure. The Limits of City Authority Minnesota municipalities can regulate aspects of data center development through zoning, including location, physical size and certain noise impacts. However, state law limits municipal authority over matters such as electrical megawatt capacity, air emissions and heating and cooling systems. That division of responsibility complicates the debate.
